talk about the weather: When my grandfather meets his old friends in the park, they always talk about the weather for a long time.
我爺爺在公園遇到老朋友時，他們總是聊天氣聊很久。
a book about animals: For my birthday, my aunt gave me a book about animals, and I read it every night before I go to bed.
生日時阿姨送我一本關於動物的書，我每天睡前都會讀它。
How about a cup of tea?: You look very tired after washing all the dishes, so how about a cup of tea and some cookies?
洗完所有的碗盤你看起來很累，喝杯茶配點餅乾如何？
What about you?: I want to go swimming at the beach this Saturday because the weather will be hot, but what about you?
這週六天氣會很熱，我想去海邊游泳，那你呢？
worry about the test: Jenny did not sleep well last night because she kept worrying about the test in math class today.
珍妮昨晚睡不好，因為她一直擔心今天數學課的考試。
be excited about the trip: The students are so excited about the trip to Japan that they have already packed their bags a week early.
學生們對日本之旅感到非常興奮，提早一週就把行李打包好了。
be sorry about it: Tom broke his sister's favorite cup this morning, and he said he was really sorry about it.
湯姆今天早上打破了姊姊最喜歡的杯子，他說他為此感到非常抱歉。
What is it about?: My brother is watching a long movie in the living room, so I asked him what it is about.
我哥哥正在客廳看一部很長的電影，所以我問他這部電影是關於什麼的。
about ten o'clock: The train to Kaohsiung leaves at about ten o'clock, so we should get to the station a little earlier.
去高雄的火車大約十點出發，所以我們應該早一點到車站。
about 20 people: There were about 20 people waiting in line outside the new bakery before it opened this morning.
今天早上新的麵包店開門前，大約有二十人在外面排隊等待。
about to leave: We were about to leave for the movie theater when it suddenly started to rain very hard outside.
我們正要出發去電影院時，外面突然下起了大雨。
be about to cry: The little girl was about to cry because she could not find her mother in the crowded market.
小女孩快要哭了，因為她在擁擠的市場裡找不到媽媽。
walk about the park: On Sunday mornings my grandmother likes to walk about the park and say hello to her neighbors.
週日早上我奶奶喜歡在公園裡四處走走，跟鄰居打招呼。
Lisa is the best singer in our class, and there is no doubt about it because everyone loves her voice.
麗莎是我們班最棒的歌手，這點毫無疑問，因為大家都喜歡她的聲音。
be careful about money: My mother always tells me to be careful about money, so I write down everything I buy each week.
媽媽總是叫我小心用錢，所以我每週都會把買的東西記下來。
be crazy about baseball: My cousin is crazy about baseball, and he watches every game on TV even when it is very late at night.
我表哥對棒球很著迷，即使很晚他也會看電視上的每一場比賽。
about: The bus ride to the museum takes about an hour, or around an hour, so bring a book to read.
搭公車到博物館大約要一小時，也就是 around 一小時，所以帶本書去讀。
think about vs. think of: When I think about the test, I feel nervous, but when I think of my summer vacation, I feel happy.
當我思考考試的事，我會緊張，但當我想到暑假，我就會開心。
about three days (大約): It took my father about three days to fix the old bicycle, but now it runs better than before.
我爸爸花了大約三天修理那輛舊腳踏車，不過現在它比以前更好騎了。
on history (專門) vs. about history (一般): My teacher wrote a serious book on history, but my little brother only likes funny stories about history.
我老師寫了一本專門論述歷史的嚴肅著作，但我弟弟只喜歡一般談及歷史的有趣故事。
the sky above us: We lay on the grass after the picnic and looked at the sky above us, which was full of white clouds.
野餐後我們躺在草地上，看著我們頭頂的天空，上面滿是白雲。
above the clouds: When the plane flew above the clouds, the sun came out and everything outside the window turned bright.
飛機飛到雲層之上時，太陽出來了，窗外的一切都變得明亮。
the picture above the sofa: The picture above the sofa was painted by my grandmother when she was a young art student in Taipei.
沙發上方的那幅畫是我奶奶年輕時在台北當美術學生畫的。
fly above the sea: We watched many white birds fly above the sea while we were eating ice cream on the beach.
我們在海邊吃冰淇淋時，看著許多白色的鳥飛越海面上方。
a few lines above: If you do not understand this word, you can find its meaning a few lines above on the same page.
如果你不懂這個字，可以在同一頁上面幾行找到它的意思。
the floor above: The family on the floor above plays loud music every night, so my father went to talk to them.
樓上那一層的那家人每晚都放很大聲的音樂，所以我爸爸去跟他們談了。
above all: You should study hard and eat well, but above all, remember to get enough sleep before the big test.
你應該用功讀書、好好吃飯，但最重要的是，大考前要記得睡飽。
above zero: It was very cold this morning, but the weather report says it will stay just above zero this afternoon.
今天早上很冷，但氣象報告說今天下午氣溫會維持在零度以上一點。
children above ten: Children above ten have to buy a full ticket at this zoo, but younger kids can get in for free.
這間動物園十歲以上的孩子要買全票，但更小的小孩可以免費入場。
above the law: Nobody is above the law in our country, so even famous and rich people must follow the same rules.
在我們國家沒有人不受法律約束，所以即使有名又有錢的人也必須遵守相同的規定。
above and beyond: Our teacher stayed after school every day to help us, which went above and beyond what we expected.
我們老師每天放學後都留下來幫我們，這遠超出我們的預期。
the above rules: Everyone who joins the school sports club must read and follow the above rules at all times.
每個加入學校運動社團的人都必須隨時閱讀並遵守上述規定。
To learn how to make this paper bird, see the picture above and follow the six easy steps.
想學做這隻紙鳥，請見上圖並照著六個簡單的步驟做。
above (不接觸) vs. over (正上方／覆蓋): The lamp hangs high above the table without touching it, but the paper lies over the table and covers it.
燈高掛在桌子上方沒有碰到桌子，但紙覆蓋在桌子上面。
above vs. on top of: The clock is above the door, but the cat is sitting on top of the bookcase and looking down at us.
時鐘在門的上方，而貓坐在書櫃頂端上面低頭看著我們。
above sea level: Our hotel in the mountains was two thousand meters above sea level, so the nights were very cold.
我們在山上的旅館位於海平面以上兩千公尺，所以晚上非常冷。
over the river (橫越): We walked over the river on the old stone bridge while white birds flew high above the water.
我們走過古老的石橋跨過河，同時白色的鳥在水面上方高高飛翔。
walk across the street: Always look left and right before you walk across the street, even when the light is green.
過馬路前一定要先看左右，即使是綠燈也一樣。
swim across the river: My uncle can swim across the river in ten minutes, but I am still afraid of the deep water.
我叔叔十分鐘就能游過河，但我還是害怕深水。
across the road from school: There is a small bookstore across the road from school, and many students go there after class.
學校對面馬路邊有一間小書店，很多學生下課後會去那裡。
live across the street: Mrs. Lin lives across the street from us, and she often brings us fruit from her garden.
林太太住在我們對街，她常常帶自家花園的水果給我們。
a bridge across the river: A new bridge across the river opened last month, so now it takes only five minutes to get to town.
一座新的跨河大橋上個月通車了，所以現在到鎮上只要五分鐘。
run across the field: The dog saw a rabbit and started to run across the field as fast as it could.
那隻狗看到一隻兔子，就開始用最快的速度跑過田野。
across Taiwan: Heavy rain fell across Taiwan last weekend, and many baseball games had to be stopped.
上週末全台灣各地都下大雨，許多棒球比賽不得不中止。
all across the world: People all across the world watched the final game on TV and cheered for their favorite teams.
全世界各地的人都在電視上看了決賽，為他們最喜歡的球隊加油。
come across an old friend: I came across an old friend from my old school at the night market, and we talked for an hour.
我在夜市偶然遇到一位以前學校的老朋友，我們聊了一個小時。
come across a word: When you come across a word you do not know, write it down and look it up in the dictionary later.
當你碰到一個不認識的字時，先寫下來，稍後再查字典。
You will never guess who I ran across at the train station this morning before I went to work.
你絕對猜不到今天早上上班前我在火車站偶然碰到誰。
get across one's idea: It was hard for Amy to get across her idea in English, so she drew a picture to explain it.
艾美很難用英文讓人了解她的想法，所以她畫了一張圖來說明。
across from the bank: The post office is across from the bank, so you can send the letter after you get your money.
郵局在銀行對面，所以你領了錢之後可以順便寄信。
put a line across the page: The teacher asked us to put a line across the page and write the new words under it.
老師要我們在頁面上畫一條線，然後把新單字寫在線的下面。
sit across from me: At the family dinner, my little cousin sat across from me and kept making funny faces during the meal.
家庭聚餐時，我的小表弟坐在我對面，用餐時一直做鬼臉。
right across the hall: The music room is right across the hall from our class, so we can hear the piano every afternoon.
音樂教室就在走廊對面，正對著我們教室，所以我們每天下午都聽得到鋼琴聲。
across (表面橫越) vs. through (穿過內部): We walked across the big field in the sun and then went through the dark forest to reach the lake.
我們在陽光下橫越那片大田野，然後穿越陰暗的森林內部才到達湖邊。
walk across the park (穿越空地): It is faster to walk across the park than to go around it, so we take that way to school.
走過公園比繞公園走更快，所以我們上學走那條路。
walk through the forest (穿過林中): We did not walk across the open field; instead, we walked through the forest and listened to the birds.
我們沒有橫越空曠的田野，而是穿過森林裡面，聽鳥兒唱歌。
jump over the wall (跨越上方): The boy ran across the yard and tried to jump over the wall to get his ball, but he was too short.
男孩跑過院子，想跳過牆去拿他的球，但他太矮了。
across the bridge vs. over the bridge: Every morning my father drives across the bridge to work, and sometimes he says he drives over the bridge.
每天早上我爸爸開車過橋去上班，有時他說他 over 過橋，兩種說法都可以。
after school: After school, Peter and his friends usually play basketball in the park until it gets dark.
放學後，彼得和他的朋友通常在公園打籃球，直到天黑。
after dinner: My family likes to take a short walk around the block after dinner when the weather is nice.
天氣好的時候，我家人喜歡晚餐後在附近街區散步一下。
the day after tomorrow: We are going to visit my grandmother in Tainan the day after tomorrow, so I need to pack my bag.
我們後天要去台南探望外婆，所以我得打包行李。
after a while: The baby cried loudly at first, but after a while she fell asleep in her mother's arms.
寶寶一開始大聲哭，但過了一會兒她就在媽媽懷裡睡著了。
after all these years: After all these years, my mother still remembers the name of her first English teacher at school.
這麼多年之後，我媽媽還記得她在學校第一位英文老師的名字。
ten after six: The school bus comes at ten after six every morning, so I have to get up very early to catch it.
校車每天早上六點十分來，所以我必須很早起床才趕得上。
one after another: The students walked into the gym one after another and sat down quietly for the morning meeting.
學生們一個接一個走進體育館，安靜地坐下來參加早會。
day after day: Day after day, the old man sat by the window and waited for a letter from his son in America.
日復一日，老人坐在窗邊等待在美國的兒子寄來的信。
after all: I was angry that my brother ate my cake, but after all, he is only five years old.
我很氣弟弟吃了我的蛋糕，但畢竟他才五歲。
look after the baby: My mother asked me to look after the baby while she went to the supermarket to buy some milk.
媽媽去超市買牛奶時，請我照顧寶寶。
run after the bus: We had to run after the bus this morning because we spent too much time eating breakfast.
今天早上我們不得不追公車，因為我們花太多時間吃早餐了。
take after one's father: Everyone says that Jack takes after his father because they both have big eyes and love to tell jokes.
大家都說傑克長得像他爸爸，因為他們都有大眼睛，又愛講笑話。
be after money: I do not think he is a true friend, because he is only after money and never helps anyone for free.
我不認為他是真朋友，因為他只追求金錢，從不免費幫任何人。
name the baby after her grandmother: My parents decided to name the baby after her grandmother, so my little sister is also called Mei.
我爸媽決定以祖母的名字為寶寶命名，所以我妹妹也叫美。
When I met Mr. Wang at the market, he asked after my grandfather, who has been sick for a month.
我在市場遇到王先生時，他問候了我病了一個月的爺爺。
after you: When we got to the door at the same time, the tall man smiled at me and said, After you.
我們同時走到門口時，那位高大的男人對我微笑說：您先請。
after (之後) vs. behind (後面): We eat dinner after six o'clock, and the dog always sits behind my chair and waits for food.
我們六點之後吃晚餐，而狗總是坐在我的椅子後面等食物。
after vs. in (未來時間): I will see the doctor in two days, and after that visit I will know whether I can play again.
我兩天後要去看醫生，在那次看診之後我就會知道能不能再上場了。
in two days (從現在起): The new shopping mall near our school will open in two days, and we plan to go there right after school.
我們學校附近的新購物中心從現在起兩天後要開幕，我們打算放學後馬上去。
after two days (從某時起): After two days of heavy rain, the sun finally came out and the children ran outside to play.
連下兩天大雨之後，太陽終於出來了，孩子們跑到外面去玩。
against the law: Riding a motorcycle without a safety hat is against the law in Taiwan, and you may have to pay money.
在台灣騎機車不戴安全帽是違法的，你可能要罰錢。
against the rules: Using your phone during the test is against the rules, so please put it in your bag now.
考試中使用手機是違規的，所以請現在把它放進包包裡。
be against the plan: Most of the students are against the plan to have classes on Saturday because they want to rest.
大多數學生反對週六上課的計畫，因為他們想休息。
play against another team: Our school team will play against another team from Taichung in the final game next Sunday afternoon.
我們校隊下週日下午將在決賽中對抗來自台中的另一隊。
stand against the door: The tired boy had to stand against the door on the crowded train because there were no empty seats.
擁擠的火車上沒有空位，疲累的男孩只好靠門站著。
fight against the enemy: In the story, the brave young soldier had to fight against the enemy alone to save his village.
故事中，勇敢的年輕士兵必須獨自對抗敵人來拯救他的村子。
vote against it: When the class leader asked about having a party, many students voted for it but a few voted against it.
班長問要不要辦派對時，許多學生投贊成票，但有幾個人投票反對。
against the wind: It was hard to ride my bicycle against the wind this morning, so I was late for school.
今天早上逆風騎腳踏車很辛苦，所以我上學遲到了。
swim against the water: The little fish had to swim against the water for hours to get back to the place where it was born.
小魚必須逆流而上游好幾個小時，才能回到它出生的地方。
protect against the cold: Grandma made me a thick sweater to protect against the cold because winter in the mountains is hard.
奶奶幫我織了一件厚毛衣來防寒，因為山上的冬天很難熬。
against one's will: Nobody should make a child join a club against his will, because he will not enjoy it at all.
沒有人應該違背孩子的意願強迫他參加社團，因為他完全不會樂在其中。
against the clock: The doctors worked against the clock all night to save the man who was hurt in the car accident.
醫生整夜搶時間，搶救那位在車禍中受傷的男人。
a race against time: Finishing the school report before midnight became a race against time because I started too late.
在午夜前完成學校報告變成一場與時間賽跑，因為我開始得太晚了。
the dark hills against the sky: From the beach we could see the dark hills against the sky as the sun went down behind them.
從海灘上，我們看見太陽落到天空映襯下的黑色山丘後方。
have nothing against him: I have nothing against him, but I do not want to sit next to him because he talks too much in class.
我對他沒有意見，但我不想坐在他旁邊，因為他上課太愛講話。
against (反對) vs. for (支持): My mother is for the idea of getting a dog, but my father is against it because our apartment is small.
媽媽支持養狗的想法，但爸爸反對，因為我們的公寓太小。
Are you for or against it?: The teacher wants to change the time of the class trip, so are you for or against it?
老師想改變班遊的時間，你贊成還是反對？
against (靠著) vs. on (在上面): The boy put his bike against the wall and then put his heavy school bag on the ground.
男孩把腳踏車靠在牆上，然後把沉重的書包放在地上。
walk along the river: On warm evenings, my parents and I walk along the river and watch the lights of the city.
溫暖的夜晚，我和爸媽沿著河走，看城市的燈光。
along the road: There were many beautiful flowers along the road, so we stopped the car to take some pictures.
沿路有許多美麗的花，所以我們停車拍了幾張照片。
trees along the street: The tall trees along the street keep us cool when we walk home on hot summer afternoons.
街道兩旁的高大樹木在炎熱的夏日午後我們走路回家時讓我們保持涼爽。
drive along the coast: Last summer we drove along the coast for three hours and ate fresh fish at a small town.
去年夏天我們沿著海岸開了三小時的車，在一個小鎮吃新鮮的魚。
shops along the way: We stopped at several small shops along the way to buy drinks and snacks before we reached the beach.
到海邊之前，我們在沿路的幾家小商店停下來買飲料和零食。
Although my sister and I are very different, we get along with each other well and seldom fight.
雖然我和姊姊非常不同，我們相處得很融洽，很少吵架。
come along with us: We are going to the night market tonight, so why don't you come along with us and try some food?
我們今晚要去夜市，你何不跟我們一起來吃點東西？
bring your friend along: The party on Friday will be a lot of fun, so you can bring your friend along if you want.
週五的派對會很好玩，所以如果你想的話可以帶你朋友一起來。
go along with the plan: At first Tom did not like the idea, but in the end he decided to go along with the plan.
一開始湯姆不喜歡這個想法，但最後他決定贊同這個計畫。
move along, please: The police officer told the people on the street to move along, please, because the big show was coming.
警察告訴街上的人請往前走，因為大型表演隊伍要來了。
sing along with the music: When our favorite song came on the radio, everyone in the car started to sing along with the music.
當我們最愛的歌在收音機播出時，車上的每個人都開始跟著音樂唱。
all along: My mother knew all along that I broke the window, but she waited for me to tell her the truth.
媽媽一直以來都知道窗戶是我打破的，但她等著我自己說實話。
along with his family: Mr. Chen moved to Kaohsiung along with his family last year because he found a better job there.
陳先生去年和他的家人一起搬到高雄，因為他在那裡找到了更好的工作。
How are you getting along?: I have not seen you since you started your new school, so how are you getting along these days?
自從你開始上新學校後我就沒見過你了，你最近過得如何？
Come along!: Come along! The movie starts in ten minutes, and we still have to buy the tickets and some popcorn.
快點來！電影十分鐘後就開始了，我們還得買票和爆米花。
take an umbrella along: The sky looks gray this morning, so you should take an umbrella along when you go to school.
今天早上天空看起來灰灰的，所以你上學時應該隨身帶把傘。
along the way: On our trip to the mountains we met many kind people along the way who gave us food and water.
在我們去山上的旅途中，一路上遇到許多好心人給我們食物和水。
run along now: Grandpa gave us each a cookie and said, Run along now, because he wanted to take a short sleep.
爺爺給我們每人一塊餅乾，然後說：現在快走吧，因為他想小睡一下。
read along with me: The English teacher played the story and asked the whole class to read along with her slowly.
英文老師播放故事，請全班跟著她一起慢慢讀。
among friends: I feel most comfortable when I am among friends, because I can say anything without being afraid.
在朋友之間我感到最自在，因為我可以毫不害怕地暢所欲言。
popular among students: Bubble tea is very popular among students in Taiwan, and many of them buy a cup after school.
珍珠奶茶在台灣學生之間很受歡迎，許多人放學後會買一杯。
one among many: Our school is just one among many schools in the city, but we are the only one with a swimming pool.
我們學校只是城裡眾多學校之一，但我們是唯一有游泳池的學校。
share the cake among the children: Grandma cut the big cake into eight pieces and shared it among the children at the birthday party.
奶奶在生日派對上把大蛋糕切成八塊，分給孩子們。
among other things: At the meeting we talked about the school trip, the new uniforms, and the sports day, among other things.
會議上我們談到了校外教學、新制服和運動會，以及其他事情。
a house among the trees: My grandfather lives in a small house among the trees, and you can hear birds singing all day long.
我爺爺住在樹林中的一棟小房子裡，整天都聽得到鳥叫。
talk among themselves: The students talked among themselves for a few minutes before the teacher asked for their answer.
老師要他們回答前，學生們彼此交談了幾分鐘。
among the best: Our basketball team is among the best in the country, and we won the first prize again this year.
我們的籃球隊名列全國最佳之一，今年又拿下了第一名。
between (兩者) vs. among (三者以上): Mary stood between her two best friends for the photo, and then she sat among all her friends from class.
瑪麗站在她兩個最好的朋友之間拍照，然後坐進全班朋友之中。
between you and me: Between you and me, our new teacher is the kindest among all the teachers at school, but don't tell anyone.
你我之間說說就好，新老師是學校所有老師之中最親切的，但別告訴別人。
among the three of us: Among the three of us, Lisa is the tallest, so she always gets the things on the top shelf.
我們三人之間，麗莎最高，所以總是由她拿架子最上層的東西。
between the two trees: My father hung a rope between the two trees, and the birds sang among the leaves above his head.
爸爸在兩棵樹之間掛了一條繩子，鳥兒在他頭上的樹葉之中歌唱。
among the crowd: I lost my little brother among the crowd at the night market, but we found him near the ice cream shop.
我在夜市的人群之中和弟弟走散了，但我們在冰淇淋店附近找到了他。
choose between A and B: We had to choose between the zoo and the museum, but among the three of us, only I wanted the museum.
我們必須在動物園和博物館之間選擇，但我們三人之中只有我想去博物館。
choose among many: There were so many colors of shoes in the store that it took me an hour to choose among many.
店裡的鞋子顏色太多了，我花了一小時才在多者中選出一雙。
around the corner: The new bakery is just around the corner from our school, and the bread smells wonderful every morning.
新的麵包店就在我們學校轉角處，每天早上麵包都香氣四溢。
sit around the table: On New Year's Eve the whole family sits around the table and eats a big dinner together.
除夕夜全家人圍著桌子坐，一起吃一頓豐盛的晚餐。
walk around the lake: My grandmother and her friends walk around the lake every morning before they have breakfast together.
我奶奶和她的朋友每天早上一起吃早餐前都會繞著湖走。
look around the room: When I woke up in the hotel, I looked around the room and could not remember where I was.
我在旅館醒來時環顧房間，想不起來自己在哪裡。
all around the world: Children all around the world love to play games, even if the games are different in each country.
全世界的孩子都愛玩遊戲，即使每個國家的遊戲都不一樣。
travel around Taiwan: My uncle wants to travel around Taiwan by bicycle this summer, and he plans to finish in nine days.
我叔叔今年夏天想騎腳踏車環島旅行，他計畫九天內完成。
turn around: When someone called my name on the street, I turned around but saw no one that I knew.
有人在街上叫我的名字時，我轉身卻沒看到任何認識的人。
the other way around: People think my sister is older than me, but actually it is the other way around; I am older.
大家以為我姊姊比我大，但其實反過來，我才是比較大的。
around nine o'clock: The movie ends around nine o'clock, so I will call you when I get home a little later.
電影大約九點結束，所以我晚一點回到家時再打給你。
around 50 dollars: A ticket to the water park costs around 50 dollars for students, so bring your student card.
水上樂園的門票學生票大約五十元，所以要帶學生證。
around ten years old: When I was around ten years old, my family moved from a small town to a big city.
我大約十歲時，我們家從小鎮搬到大城市。
be around: Please be around at three o'clock this afternoon, because the man is coming to fix the computer.
今天下午三點請留在附近，因為修電腦的人要來。
show sb. around: When my cousin came to visit from Japan, I showed her around the school and my favorite night market.
我表妹從日本來拜訪時，我帶她參觀學校和我最愛的夜市。
stick around: The game will start again in ten minutes after the rain stops, so please stick around if you can.
雨停後十分鐘比賽會重新開始，如果可以的話請留在這裡別走。
fool around: If you fool around in class instead of listening, you will not pass the English test next week.
如果你在課堂上混時間而不聽課，下週的英文考試就不會及格。
hang around: Some students like to hang around at the park after school instead of going straight home.
有些學生放學後喜歡在公園閒晃，而不直接回家。
just around the corner: Summer vacation is just around the corner, so the students are already planning trips to the beach.
暑假即將到來，學生們已經開始計畫海邊之旅了。
look around for a job: After he finished school, my brother looked around for a job for two months before a bank hired him.
我哥哥畢業後到處找工作找了兩個月，才被一家銀行錄用。
get around: My grandfather hurt his leg last month, so now he needs a stick to get around the house.
我爺爺上個月腿受傷了，所以現在他需要拐杖才能在家裡四處走動。
around the clock: The hospital near our house is open around the clock, so you can go there even at three in the morning.
我們家附近的醫院日夜不停開放，所以即使凌晨三點你也可以去。
have been around: You can ask my grandmother any question about cooking, because she has been around for a long time.
你可以問我奶奶任何關於烹飪的問題，因為她見多識廣。
run around: The little children ran around in the yard for an hour and then fell asleep right after lunch.
小孩子在院子裡跑來跑去跑了一小時，然後午餐後馬上就睡著了。
ask around: I lost my cat yesterday, so I will ask around the neighbors to see if anyone has seen a white cat.
我昨天把貓弄丟了，所以我會到處問問鄰居有沒有人看到一隻白貓。
all year around: Because the weather in the south of Taiwan is warm all year around, farmers there can grow fruit in winter.
因為南台灣一年到頭天氣都溫暖，那裡的農夫冬天也能種水果。
work as a teacher: My aunt has worked as a teacher at a small school in the mountains for more than twenty years.
我阿姨在山上一所小學校當老師已經超過二十年了。
use the box as a chair: We did not have enough seats for the party, so my brother used a big box as a chair.
派對的座位不夠，所以我哥哥把一個大箱子當椅子用。
as a child: As a child, my father often went fishing with his grandfather at the river near their village.
我爸爸小時候常和他的爺爺到村子附近的河邊釣魚。
as a result: Tom stayed up late playing computer games last night, and as a result, he fell asleep in math class.
湯姆昨晚熬夜玩電腦遊戲，結果他在數學課上睡著了。
as a matter of fact: Many people think Jenny is shy, but as a matter of fact, she loves to sing in front of a big crowd.
很多人以為珍妮害羞，但事實上，她喜歡在一大群人面前唱歌。
as far as I know: As far as I know, the library closes at nine on weekdays, but you should check the time on the Internet.
就我所知，圖書館平日九點關門，但你應該上網確認一下時間。
as long as: You can borrow my bicycle this weekend as long as you bring it back before Monday morning.
只要你在週一早上前還我，這週末你可以借我的腳踏車。
as soon as possible: The teacher asked us to hand in our homework as soon as possible because he must give the grades on Friday.
老師要我們盡快交作業，因為他週五必須給出成績。
as well: We had noodles and dumplings for lunch, and my little brother wanted a bowl of hot soup as well.
我們午餐吃了麵和水餃，我弟弟也想要一碗熱湯。
as well as: My mother speaks English as well as Japanese, so she often helps the visitors who come to our shop.
我媽媽會說英文以及日文，所以她常幫助來我們店裡的客人。
as usual: As usual, my grandfather got up at five o'clock, drank a cup of tea, and read the newspaper.
像往常一樣，爺爺五點起床，喝了杯茶，然後看報紙。
as follows: The rules for the school library are as follows: no food, no loud talking, and return books on time.
學校圖書館的規定如下：不能帶食物、不能大聲說話、要準時還書。
as for me: My friends want to go to the mountains this weekend, but as for me, I would rather stay home and rest.
我朋友這週末想去山上，至於我，我寧願待在家休息。
such as: My little sister loves sweet food, such as chocolate cake, ice cream, and cookies with milk.
我妹妹喜歡甜食，例如巧克力蛋糕、冰淇淋，以及配牛奶的餅乾。
the same as: My new phone is the same as my brother's, so sometimes we pick up the wrong one by mistake.
我的新手機和我哥哥的一樣，所以有時候我們會拿錯。
as if: The sky turned very dark in the afternoon, as if a big storm was going to hit the city soon.
下午天空變得很暗，好像一場大風暴很快就要襲擊這座城市。
as (職業身分) vs. like (像): My aunt works as a doctor at a hospital, and she works like a machine because she never gets tired.
我阿姨的身分是醫院的醫生，而她工作起來像機器一樣，因為她從不疲倦。
work as a nurse (真的是): My mother works as a nurse at the hospital near our house, so she often comes home very late.
我媽媽在我們家附近的醫院當護士，所以她常常很晚回家。
work like a dog (像): My father works as a driver and works like a dog six days a week, so on Sunday he sleeps all day.
我爸爸的工作是司機，一週六天像狗一樣辛苦工作，所以週日他睡整天。
as a friend (身分): I am telling you this as a friend, not as your teacher: you should spend less time on your phone.
我是以朋友的身分告訴你這件事，不是以老師的身分：你應該少花點時間在手機上。
like a friend (比喻): Our new teacher talks to us like a friend, so everyone in the class feels comfortable in her lessons.
我們的新老師跟我們說話像朋友一樣，所以班上每個人上她的課都很自在。
think of A as B: I have known Kevin since we were five, and I think of him as my brother, not just a friend.
我從五歲就認識凱文，我把他當成我的兄弟，而不只是朋友。
at seven o'clock: My alarm clock rings at seven o'clock every morning, but I usually stay in bed for ten more minutes.
我的鬧鐘每天早上七點響，但我通常會再賴床十分鐘。
at noon: The sun is very strong at noon in summer, so remember to wear a hat when you go outside.
夏天中午的太陽很強，所以出門時記得戴帽子。
at night: My cat sleeps all day, but at night it runs around the house and wakes everyone up.
我的貓整天都在睡覺，但在夜晚它會在屋裡跑來跑去，把大家吵醒。
at midnight: On New Year's Eve we stayed up until midnight, and at midnight we watched the beautiful lights in the sky together.
除夕夜我們熬夜到半夜，在半夜我們一起看天空中美麗的燈光。
at the weekend: At the weekend my family likes to drive to the mountains and have a picnic by the river.
週末我家人喜歡開車到山上，在河邊野餐。
at Christmas: At Christmas, my aunt in America always sends us a big box of gifts and chocolate cookies.
聖誕節時，我在美國的阿姨總會寄給我們一大箱禮物和巧克力餅乾。
at the moment: My father is busy cooking dinner at the moment, so he will call you back in about half an hour.
我爸爸此刻正忙著做晚餐，所以他大約半小時後會回電給你。
at that time: My parents met at a bookstore twenty years ago, and at that time my mother was still a student.
我爸媽二十年前在一家書店相遇，那時我媽媽還是學生。
at first: At first I did not like living in the city, but now I enjoy the busy streets and night markets.
起初我不喜歡住在城市，但現在我喜歡熱鬧的街道和夜市。
at last: After waiting for the bus for forty minutes in the rain, we got home at last and had hot soup.
在雨中等公車等了四十分鐘後，我們終於到家喝了熱湯。
at the same time: It is hard to do your homework and watch TV at the same time, so turn off the TV first.
一邊做作業一邊看電視很難同時進行，所以先把電視關掉。
at the age of ten: At the age of ten, my sister already knew how to cook simple dishes like fried rice and egg soup.
我姊姊十歲時就已經會煮炒飯和蛋花湯這類簡單的菜了。
at the end of the month: My father gets paid at the end of the month, so that is when we usually go shopping for new clothes.
我爸爸在月底領薪水，所以我們通常那時候去買新衣服。
at present: My grandmother is living with us at present because she needs help after she hurt her back.
我奶奶目前和我們住在一起，因為她背部受傷後需要人幫忙。
at once: When the fire alarm rang, the teacher told everyone to leave the building at once and not take anything.
火警鈴響時，老師叫大家立刻離開大樓，不要拿任何東西。
at times: My grandfather usually eats healthy food, but at times he enjoys a big bowl of beef noodles with friends.
我爺爺通常吃健康的食物，但有時他會和朋友享用一大碗牛肉麵。
at home: My mother stayed at home with my sick brother, so she could not come to my basketball game today.
我媽媽留在家裡陪生病的弟弟，所以今天不能來看我的籃球比賽。
at school: The students have to be at school by seven thirty, and the first class begins at eight o'clock.
學生必須在七點半前到學校，第一節課八點開始。
at work: My father is at work until six, so please do not call him unless it is something very important.
我爸爸工作到六點，所以除非是很重要的事，請不要打給他。
at the bus stop: I waited at the bus stop for half an hour this morning, but the bus never came because of the rain.
今天早上我在公車站等了半小時，但因為下雨公車一直沒來。
at the door: Someone is knocking at the door, so could you open it and see who is there while I finish cooking?
有人在門口敲門，我煮完菜之前你能去開門看看是誰嗎？
at the top of the hill: When we reached the top of the hill, we sat at the top and enjoyed the view of the whole city.
我們到達山頂時，就坐在山頂上欣賞整座城市的風景。
at the bottom of the page: Write your name and class at the bottom of the page before you hand in your test paper to the teacher.
把考卷交給老師之前，請先在頁面底部寫上你的姓名和班級。
at the corner: My cat likes to sleep at the corner of the living room, where the afternoon sun shines through the window.
我的貓喜歡睡在客廳的角落，那裡下午的陽光會從窗戶照進來。
at the party: Everyone had a great time at the party last night because the music was loud and the food was delicious.
昨晚大家在派對上都玩得很開心，因為音樂很大聲，食物也很好吃。
at the table: My family sits at the table together every evening, and we talk about our day while we eat dinner.
我們家每天傍晚都一起坐在餐桌旁，邊吃晚餐邊聊一天發生的事。
at the back of the room: Tom could not see the board well because he was sitting at the back of the room.
湯姆看不清楚黑板，因為他坐在房間後面。
at the front of the class: The teacher asked Mary to stand at the front of the class and read her story to everyone.
老師請瑪麗站在班上前面，把她的故事讀給大家聽。
at the station: We waited at the station for twenty minutes, but the train was late because of the heavy rain.
我們在車站等了二十分鐘，但火車因為大雨而晚到了。
at sea: My uncle is a sailor, so he spends many months at sea and only comes home twice a year.
我叔叔是水手，所以他好幾個月都在海上，一年只回家兩次。
at a hotel: When we travel to Japan next summer, we will stay at a hotel near the beach for five days.
明年夏天我們去日本旅行時，會在海邊附近的一家旅館住五天。
be good at math: My sister is good at math, so she always helps me with my homework when I have problems.
我姊姊擅長數學，所以我作業有問題時她總是幫我。
be bad at singing: I am bad at singing, but I still enjoy singing songs with my friends at the KTV on weekends.
我不擅長唱歌，但週末我還是喜歡和朋友在 KTV 唱歌。
look at the picture: Please look at the picture on page ten and tell me what the children are doing in the park.
請看第十頁的圖，然後告訴我孩子們在公園裡做什麼。
laugh at him: It is not nice to laugh at him just because he gave the wrong answer in class today.
只因為他今天在課堂上答錯，就笑他是不好的。
Mom was angry at Tom because he came home very late and did not call her first.
媽媽生湯姆的氣，因為他很晚才回家，而且沒有先打電話給她。
be surprised at the news: We were all surprised at the news that our English teacher is going to move to Japan next month.
聽到英文老師下個月要搬去日本的消息，我們都感到很驚訝。
smile at me: The little girl smiled at me when I gave her my seat on the crowded bus this morning.
今天早上在擠滿人的公車上，我把座位讓給那個小女孩時，她對我微笑。
shout at the kids: The coach did not shout at the kids after they lost the game; instead, he told them to try again.
孩子們輸了比賽後，教練沒有對他們大吼，反而告訴他們再試一次。
point at the map: The tour guide pointed at the map and showed us the fastest way to get to the night market.
導遊指著地圖，告訴我們到夜市最快的路。
at least: You should drink at least eight glasses of water every day, especially when the weather is hot.
你每天至少應該喝八杯水，尤其是天氣很熱的時候。
at most: The small boat can carry at most six people, so some of us have to wait for the next one.
這艘小船最多只能載六個人，所以我們有些人得等下一班。
at all: I did not understand the movie at all because everyone in it spoke French very quickly.
我完全看不懂那部電影，因為裡面每個人都講很快的法文。
not at all: When I thanked my neighbor for carrying my heavy bags, she smiled and said, Not at all.
當我感謝鄰居幫我提重袋子時，她笑著說：一點也不麻煩。
at first sight: At first sight, the old house looked dark and strange, but inside it was warm, clean, and full of books.
一見之下，那間老房子看起來又暗又奇怪，但裡面卻溫暖、乾淨，而且滿是書。
at the age of: My grandfather started working on a farm at the age of twelve because his family was very poor.
我爺爺在十二歲時就開始在農場工作，因為他家很窮。
at a low price: We bought these fresh vegetables at a low price because the market was about to close for the day.
我們以低價買到這些新鮮蔬菜，因為市場當天快要收攤了。
at full speed: The driver went at full speed down the hill, and everyone on the bus held their seats and closed their eyes.
司機全速衝下山坡，公車上每個人都抓住座位並閉上眼睛。
at hand: Always keep a pen and some paper at hand so that you can write down important things quickly.
隨時把筆和紙放在手邊，這樣你才能快速寫下重要的事。
at a time: Please come into the office one at a time because the doctor can only see one student now.
請一次進來辦公室一個人，因為醫生現在一次只能看一位學生。
two at a time: The boys ran up the stairs two at a time because they did not want to miss the start of the game.
男孩們一次跨兩個臺階跑上樓，因為他們不想錯過比賽的開始。
be at a loss: When the teacher asked me a hard question in front of everyone, I was at a loss for words.
當老師在大家面前問我一個難題時，我不知所措，說不出話來。
at ease: After the big test was over, all the students felt at ease and went out to play basketball.
大考結束後，所有學生都放鬆下來，跑出去打籃球了。
at the thought of: Little Amy feels sick at the thought of eating fish, so her mother cooks chicken for her instead.
小艾咪一想到吃魚就覺得不舒服，所以媽媽改煮雞肉給她。
at the sight of: The children shouted with joy at the sight of the big birthday cake on the kitchen table.
孩子們一看到廚房桌上的大生日蛋糕就開心地大叫。
at the sound of: At the sound of the school bell, everyone ran out of the room and hurried to the playground to play.
一聽到學校鐘聲，大家就跑出教室，趕往操場去玩。
at (時刻) / on (日子) / in (月年): My piano class starts at seven on Friday, and in July my teacher will give a big show for us.
我的鋼琴課星期五七點開始，而七月老師會為我們辦一場大型表演。
at 3:00 / on Monday / in May: Let us meet at 3:00 on Monday because in May the library is very crowded in the afternoon.
我們星期一三點見吧，因為五月圖書館下午很擠。
at night vs. in the morning: My father reads the newspaper in the morning, but he likes to watch old movies at night.
我爸爸早上看報紙，但晚上喜歡看老電影。
at noon vs. in the afternoon: We usually eat lunch at noon, and then the whole family takes a short rest in the afternoon.
我們通常中午吃午餐，然後全家人下午會小睡一會兒。
at the weekend vs. on the weekend: My British friend says at the weekend, but my American cousin always says on the weekend instead.
我的英國朋友說 at the weekend，但我的美國表哥總是說 on the weekend。
at (地點一點) / in (範圍內) / on (表面): Tom waited at the bus stop, his sister stayed in the car, and their dog slept on the roof.
湯姆在公車站等候，他妹妹留在車裡，而他們的狗睡在車頂上。
at the corner (街角) vs. in the corner (房間: The bakery is at the corner of the street, and inside, a little cat sleeps in the corner of the shop.
麵包店在街角，而店內一隻小貓睡在店裡的角落。
at home vs. in the house: Dad is at home today, but he is not in the house because he is washing the car in the yard.
爸爸今天在家，但他不在屋子裡，因為他正在院子裡洗車。
at school (上學) vs. in the school (建築內): My brother is at school now, and later his class will meet the new teacher in the school hall.
我弟弟現在在上學，稍後他們班會在校舍的大廳見新老師。
arrive at the station vs. arrive in Taip: We will arrive at the station at nine, and my aunt will arrive in Taipei one hour later by bus.
我們九點會到車站，而我阿姨會在一小時後搭公車到台北。
at the table (用餐) vs. on the table (桌上): The whole family was sitting at the table for dinner, and a big bowl of soup was on the table.
全家人坐在餐桌旁吃晚餐，一大碗湯放在桌面上。
Mary was angry at the broken window, but she was not angry with her little brother who broke it.
瑪麗對打破的窗戶很生氣，但她沒有生打破窗戶的小弟弟的氣。
shout at (生氣地) vs. shout to (叫喚): Do not shout at your sister when you are angry; just shout to her from the garden if you need help.
生氣時不要對妹妹吼；如果你需要幫忙，從花園向她喊一聲就好。
throw at (攻擊) vs. throw to (傳給): The angry boy threw a stone at the dog, but his kind friend threw the ball to it to play.
那個生氣的男孩把石頭丟向狗，但他善良的朋友把球丟給狗一起玩。
laugh at (嘲笑) vs. laugh with (一起笑): Good friends never laugh at you when you fall; they laugh with you and help you stand up again.
好朋友在你跌倒時從不嘲笑你；他們會和你一起笑，並幫你再站起來。
before dinner: Wash your hands before dinner, and remember to help your grandmother set the plates on the table.
晚餐前先洗手，並記得幫奶奶把盤子放到桌上。
the day before yesterday: The day before yesterday, we visited the zoo and saw a baby elephant playing with its mother.
前天我們去了動物園，看到一隻小象在和它的媽媽玩。
before long: Keep practicing the piano every day, and before long you will be able to play your favorite songs.
每天持續練鋼琴，不久之後你就能彈你最喜歡的歌了。
long before: My grandmother says that long before I was born, this busy street was just a quiet field with cows.
我奶奶說，很久以前，在我出生之前，這條熱鬧的街只是一片有牛的安靜田野。
before dark: We should get back to the camp before dark because it is easy to get lost in the mountains at night.
我們應該在天黑前回到營地，因為晚上在山裡很容易迷路。
the night before: The night before the big test, Lisa went to bed early instead of watching TV with her brother.
大考的前一晚，麗莎沒有和弟弟看電視，而是早早上床睡覺。
ten minutes before the show: Please be in your seats ten minutes before the show, because the doors will close when it starts.
請在表演前十分鐘坐到位子上，因為表演開始後門會關上。
before it is too late: You should see a doctor about your cough before it is too late and you get really sick.
趁還來得及，你應該去看醫生處理咳嗽，不然會病得很重。
stand before the class: Jack was nervous when he had to stand before the class and talk about his trip to Japan.
傑克必須站在全班面前談他的日本之旅時，感到很緊張。
before the judge: The man stood quietly before the judge and said he was sorry for taking the money from the store.
那名男子安靜地站在法官面前，說他很抱歉從商店拿了錢。
put the family before work: My father always puts the family before work, so he never misses our birthday dinners or school shows.
我爸爸總是把家庭放在工作之前，所以他從不錯過我們的生日晚餐或學校表演。
right before your eyes: The magician made the coin disappear right before your eyes, and nobody in the room knew how he did it.
魔術師就在你眼前讓硬幣消失，房間裡沒有人知道他是怎麼做到的。
B comes before C: In the alphabet, B comes before C, so you will find the word bread before the word cake in a dictionary.
在字母表中，B 在 C 之前，所以在字典裡你會先找到 bread 再找到 cake。
ladies before gentlemen: My grandfather always opens the door for my grandmother because he believes in ladies before gentlemen.
我爺爺總是替奶奶開門，因為他相信女士優先。
before (之前) vs. in front of (正前方): Finish your homework before dinner, and then wait for me in front of the school gate tomorrow morning.
晚餐前把作業做完，然後明天早上在校門正前方等我。
before vs. ago: I visited Japan before my trip to Korea, and I came back home just two weeks ago.
我在去韓國之前先去了日本，而我兩個星期前才回到家。
two days ago (距今): Two days ago, my cousin gave me a new bike, and the day before that, he fixed my old one for free.
兩天前我表哥送我一輛新腳踏車，而在那之前一天，他免費修好了我的舊車。
two days before (距某時): Lisa moved to Taipei last May, and two days before the move she said goodbye to all her old friends.
麗莎去年五月搬到台北，在搬家之前兩天，她向所有老朋友道別了。
before long (不久) vs. long before (很久以前): Long before cars were common, people rode horses, but before long we may all be riding in flying cars.
很久以前汽車還不普遍時，人們騎馬，但不久之後我們或許都會坐飛天車了。
behind the door: Your umbrella is behind the door, so please take it with you because it will rain this afternoon.
你的雨傘在門後，請帶著它，因為今天下午會下雨。
hide behind the tree: During the game of hide and seek, my little brother always tries to hide behind the tree in the yard.
玩捉迷藏時，我弟弟總是想躲在院子裡的樹後。
sit behind me: In the movie theater, a very tall man came to sit behind me, so he could still see the screen well.
在電影院裡，一個很高的男人來坐在我後面，所以他還是能把銀幕看得很清楚。
the garden behind the house: Every spring, my grandmother grows tomatoes and pretty flowers in the small garden behind the house.
每年春天，我奶奶都會在屋後的小花園種番茄和漂亮的花。
look behind you: Look behind you before you step back, or you might knock over the glass of juice on the small table.
往後退之前先看你後面，否則你可能會打翻小桌上的那杯果汁。
the car behind us: The car behind us kept making loud noises, but Dad stayed calm and drove slowly in the heavy rain.
我們後面的車不停地發出很大的聲音，但爸爸保持冷靜，在大雨中慢慢開。
fall behind: If you miss too many classes when you are sick, you will fall behind and need extra help with math.
如果你生病時缺太多課，你會落後，數學就需要額外的幫助。
be behind in one's work: Peter is behind in his work because he spent the whole weekend playing computer games with his friends.
彼得的工作進度落後，因為他整個週末都在和朋友玩電腦遊戲。
leave sb. behind: When we go hiking, we never leave Tom behind, even though he walks much slower than the rest of us.
我們去健行時從不把湯姆丟下，即使他走得比我們其他人慢很多。
stay behind after class: The teacher asked me to stay behind after class because she wanted to talk about my science project.
老師要我課後留下來，因為她想談談我的科學專題。
behind the times: My grandfather still sends letters by mail, and my sister says he is behind the times because everyone uses email now.
我爺爺還是用郵寄寫信，我姊姊說他落伍了，因為現在大家都用電子郵件。
behind one's back: It is wrong to talk about your friends behind their backs; if you have a problem, tell them directly.
背著朋友說他們的閒話是不對的；如果你有問題，就直接告訴他們。
the reason behind it: Nobody understood the reason behind his sudden decision to leave the soccer team in the middle of the season.
沒有人明白他在球季中突然決定離開足球隊背後的原因。
be behind the plan: Everyone loved the school festival, and we learned later that our music teacher was behind the whole plan.
大家都喜歡校慶，我們後來得知音樂老師是整個計畫的推手。
ten minutes behind: The train was ten minutes behind this morning, so I had to run to school in order not to be late.
今天早上火車晚了十分鐘，所以我得跑著去學校才不會遲到。
behind closed doors: The two teachers talked about the new rules behind closed doors, so the students did not know anything about them.
兩位老師關起門來祕密討論新規定，所以學生們完全不知道內容。
behind (後面) vs. after (之後／追): The library is behind the gym, and after lunch we will go there to borrow some books for the report.
圖書館在體育館後面，午餐之後我們會去那裡借報告要用的書。
run after (追) vs. run behind: The dog ran after the cat across the street, and a little boy ran behind them laughing loudly.
狗追著貓穿過街道，一個小男孩在他們後面跑，大聲笑著。
at the back of: The small shop is behind the post office, which means it is at the back of the big building.
那間小店在郵局後面，也就是說它位在那棟大樓的後方。
below the window: There is a long wood bench below the window, and my cat loves to sleep there in the warm afternoon sun.
窗戶下方有一張長木椅，我的貓喜歡在溫暖的午後陽光下睡在那裡。
below the surface: The lake looked quiet, but below the surface of the water, hundreds of small fish were swimming around the rocks.
湖面看起來很平靜，但水的表面之下有數百條小魚在岩石間游來游去。
the valley below: From the top of the mountain, we could see the green valley below and a small river running through it.
從山頂我們可以看到下方的綠色山谷，還有一條小河流過。
below sea level: Parts of that country are below sea level, so the people there build strong walls to keep the water out.
那個國家有些地方在海平面以下，所以那裡的人築起堅固的牆來擋水。
look below: When you stand on the tall bridge and look below, you can see boats moving slowly on the river.
當你站在高高的橋上看下方，可以看到船在河上慢慢移動。
see the notes below: If you do not understand the new words in the story, please see the notes below for their meanings.
如果你不懂故事裡的新單字，請見下方註解了解它們的意思。
below zero: It was five degrees below zero last night, so the water in the garden turned into ice.
昨晚氣溫是零度以下五度，所以花園裡的水都結成冰了。
children below 12: Children below 12 can enter the museum for free, but they must come with a parent or a teacher.
十二歲以下的孩子可以免費進博物館，但必須有家長或老師陪同。
below the line: Please write your name below the line at the bottom of the page and hand the paper to the teacher.
請把名字寫在頁面底部的線以下，然後把紙交給老師。
far below: His test score was far below the class, so his parents asked an older student to help him after school.
他的考試分數遠低於全班，所以他父母請一位學長放學後幫他。
the floor below: The noise from the floor below woke me up at midnight, so I could not sleep well before the test.
樓下那一層傳來的噪音半夜把我吵醒，所以考試前我沒睡好。
below (下方不接觸) vs. under (正下方／覆蓋): The clock hangs below the window, and my little dog likes to sleep under the chair right under it.
時鐘掛在窗戶下方，而我的小狗喜歡睡在正下方那張椅子底下。
under the table (正下方): The bird flew below the clouds, and when the loud thunder came, the scared cat hid under the table.
鳥在雲的下方飛，雷聲大作時，受驚的貓躲到桌子下。
below the picture (較低處): The teacher wrote the date below the picture on the board so that everyone could copy it into their notebooks.
老師在黑板上的圖下方寫了日期，讓大家可以抄到筆記本上。
under 18 vs. below 18: People under 18 cannot buy this game, and children below 18 also need a parent to go to the bank with them.
未滿十八歲的人不能買這個遊戲，十八歲以下的孩子去銀行也需要家長陪同。
sit beside me: Come and sit beside me on the bus so that we can share my snacks and talk about the game.
來坐在我旁邊的公車座位上，這樣我們就可以分享我的零食並聊比賽。
the house beside the river: My grandmother lives in the white house beside the river, and we often go fishing there in summer.
我奶奶住在河邊的白色房子裡，夏天我們常去那裡釣魚。
stand beside the door: A tall man was standing beside the door, and he smiled and held it open for the old lady.
一個高高的男人站在門旁，他微笑著替老太太把門打開。
a lamp beside the bed: There is a small lamp beside the bed, so I can read a book for a while before I go to sleep.
床邊有一盞小燈，所以我睡前可以看一會兒書。
walk beside her: I like to walk beside her on the way home because she always tells me funny stories about her cat.
我喜歡回家路上走在她身旁，因為她總是跟我講她的貓的有趣故事。
beside the point: The teacher said my answer was beside the point because the question was about history, not science.
老師說我的回答離題了，因為題目是關於歷史，不是科學。
beside (旁邊) vs. besides (除了…還有): Tom sat beside his mother at dinner, and besides rice and fish, she also cooked his favorite soup.
湯姆晚餐時坐在媽媽旁邊，而除了飯和魚，她還煮了他最喜歡的湯。
sit beside him (旁邊): At the movie theater, I sat beside him, and we shared a big box of popcorn during the whole film.
在電影院裡我坐在他旁邊，整部電影我們一起吃一大盒爆米花。
Besides English, he speaks French and a little Japanese, so he can talk to many visitors at the hotel.
除了英文，他還會法文和一點日文，所以他能和旅館裡的許多客人交談。
beside oneself with joy: When Amy heard that she won first prize in the drawing game, she was beside herself with joy.
當艾咪聽到自己在繪畫比賽中得了第一名，她高興得忘了自己。
be beside the point: What you had for breakfast is beside the point; we are talking about why you were late for school.
你早餐吃了什麼與主題無關；我們在談的是你為什麼上學遲到。
next to: The post office is beside the bank, so it is right next to the place where Mom gets money every month.
郵局在銀行旁邊，所以它就在媽媽每個月領錢的地方隔壁。
We should go home now because it is cold outside. Besides, it is late and Mom is waiting for us.
我們現在該回家了，因為外面很冷。此外，很晚了，媽媽在等我們。
besides me: Besides me, three other students in our class also joined the school swimming team this year.
除了我之外，我們班還有另外三個學生今年也加入了學校游泳隊。
What do you do besides study?: What do you do besides study on weekends, and do you ever go to the park with your friends?
你週末除了讀書還做什麼？你會和朋友去公園嗎？
besides that: The bus is slow and crowded, and besides that, the ticket costs more than the train now.
公車又慢又擠，除此之外，現在車票也比火車貴。
Besides reading, she likes music, so she plays the piano for an hour every day after dinner.
除了閱讀，她也喜歡音樂，所以她每天晚餐後都彈一小時鋼琴。
Who else came besides Tom?: Who else came to the party besides Tom, and did anyone bring a cake or some drinks?
除了湯姆還有誰來派對？有人帶蛋糕或飲料嗎？
besides (包含) vs. except (不含): Besides Tom, Mary and Jack also passed the test, but everyone except Peter was happy with the result.
除了湯姆，瑪麗和傑克也通過了考試，但除了彼得以外，大家都對結果滿意。
Besides John, Mary came too, so we had enough people to play a game of basketball in the park.
除了約翰，瑪麗也來了，所以我們人數夠在公園打一場籃球。
Besides Mary, everyone came except John, because he had a bad cold and his mother told him to stay in bed.
除了瑪麗，大家都來了，只有約翰沒來，因為他重感冒，媽媽要他躺在床上休息。
besides: The food at that restaurant is cheap and delicious, and besides, the waiters are always very friendly to kids.
那家餐廳的食物便宜又好吃，此外，服務生對小孩總是很友善。
sit between Tom and me: On the school bus, Jenny always likes to sit between Tom and me because we tell the funniest jokes.
在校車上，珍妮總是喜歡坐在湯姆和我之間，因為我們講的笑話最好笑。
the river between the two towns: The river between the two towns is very wide, so people have to take a boat to cross it.
兩鎮之間的河很寬，所以人們必須搭船過河。
a wall between the rooms: There is only a thin wall between the rooms, so I can hear my brother playing the guitar at night.
房間之間只有一道薄牆，所以我晚上聽得到弟弟彈吉他。
between the lines: The teacher wrote some notes between the lines of my story to show me how to make it better.
老師在我故事的字裡行間寫了一些筆記，告訴我怎樣寫得更好。
between the sofa and the wall: My cat likes to hide between the sofa and the wall when strangers come to visit our house.
當陌生人來我們家拜訪時，我的貓喜歡躲在沙發與牆之間。
between eight and nine: The doctor sees patients between eight and nine in the morning, so please arrive early to get a number.
醫生早上八點到九點之間看診，所以請早點到以拿到號碼牌。
between meals: My mother says I should not eat too many cookies between meals because they are bad for my teeth.
媽媽說我不應該在兩餐之間吃太多餅乾，因為對牙齒不好。
between classes: Between classes, the students usually run to the playground to play basketball for ten minutes.
下課時間，學生們通常會跑到操場打十分鐘的籃球。
between now and Friday: You have to finish the science report between now and Friday, or the teacher will not accept it.
你必須在從現在到週五之間完成科學報告，否則老師不會接受。
between 2010 and 2020: Between 2010 and 2020, our small town grew quickly, and many new shops and schools were built.
2010 到 2020 年間，我們的小鎮快速成長，蓋了許多新商店和學校。
the difference between A and B: Can you tell me the difference between a frog and a fish, because both of them can live in the water?
你能告訴我青蛙與魚的差別嗎？因為它們都能生活在水裡。
choose between the two: Mom said I could only have one pet, so I had to choose between the puppy and the rabbit.
媽媽說我只能養一隻寵物，所以我必須在小狗和兔子之間二選一。
share the money between us: We found a hundred dollars on the street and gave it to the police instead of sharing the money between us.
我們在街上撿到一百元，把它交給警察，而不是我們兩人分這筆錢。
a friendship between them: A strong friendship between them began when they sat together in the first grade of the same school.
他們之間深厚的友情，從在同一所學校一年級坐在一起時就開始了。
between jobs: My uncle is between jobs right now, so he has more time to take us to the beach this summer.
我叔叔現在正待業中，所以今年夏天他有更多時間帶我們去海邊。
few and far between: Sunny days are few and far between in winter here, so we go out to play whenever the sun comes out.
這裡冬天的晴天少之又少，所以太陽一出來我們就出去玩。
in between: The movie theater is at the end of the street, and a bookstore and a bakery are in between.
電影院在街的盡頭，而一家書店和一家麵包店在中間。
read between the lines: When my sister said she was fine, I could read between the lines and knew she was still sad.
當我姊姊說她沒事時，我能領會言外之意，知道她還是很難過。
between (兩者) vs. among (多者): The teacher divided the cake between the two girls and shared the cookies among all the other students.
老師把蛋糕分給那兩個女孩，並把餅乾分給其他所有的學生。
between A and B (不用 to): The library is open between nine and five on weekdays, but it closes at noon on Saturdays and Sundays.
圖書館平日九點到五點之間開放，但星期六和星期日中午關門。
from A to B: The bus goes from Taipei to Tainan in four hours, and it stops at two small towns between the two cities.
這班公車從台北到台南要四小時，中途會在兩座城市之間的兩個小鎮停靠。
between Monday and Friday: My father works between Monday and Friday, but on the weekend he takes us to the mountains or the beach.
我爸爸週一到週五之間上班，但週末他會帶我們去山上或海邊。
among the students: Lisa sat between Tom and me, but among the students in our class, she is the only one who speaks French.
麗莎坐在湯姆和我之間，但在我們班的學生之中，她是唯一會說法文的人。
beyond the river: My grandmother lives in a small village beyond the river, so we take a boat to visit her every holiday.
我奶奶住在河的另一邊的小村子，所以每個假日我們都搭船去探望她。
beyond the mountains: Beyond the mountains, there is a beautiful lake where many families go camping in the summer.
山的那一邊有一座美麗的湖，許多家庭夏天會去那裡露營。
the town beyond the hill: The town beyond the hill has a famous night market, and my cousin takes me there every Saturday.
山丘外的小鎮有個著名的夜市，我表哥每個星期六都帶我去。
look beyond the sea: We stood on the beach and looked beyond the sea, hoping to see the ship bringing Dad home.
我們站在沙灘上望向海的遠方，希望看到載爸爸回家的船。
beyond the city: My aunt lives beyond the city, where the air is fresh and you can see stars at night.
我阿姨住在城外，那裡空氣清新，晚上還看得到星星。
beyond words: The evening sky over the sea was beautiful beyond words, so we just stood there quietly and watched it.
海上的傍晚天空美得無法用言語形容，所以我們只是靜靜地站在那裡看著。
beyond control: The fire spread so fast that it was soon beyond control, and everyone had to leave the building quickly.
火勢蔓延得太快，很快就無法控制，大家都得趕快離開大樓。
beyond repair: My old bike is beyond repair after the accident, so Dad says he will buy me a new one next month.
車禍後我的舊腳踏車已經無法修理了，所以爸爸說下個月會買一輛新的給我。
beyond one's reach: Mom keeps the cookies on the top shelf, beyond my little brother's reach, so he cannot eat them all.
媽媽把餅乾放在最上層的架子上，我弟弟拿不到，這樣他就不會全部吃掉。
beyond my power: Fixing the computer is beyond my power, so we should ask my uncle, who knows a lot about machines.
修電腦超出我的能力，所以我們應該問我叔叔，他很懂機器。
beyond doubt: It is beyond doubt that Jenny is the best swimmer in our school, because she wins every race.
毫無疑問珍妮是我們學校最棒的游泳選手，因為她每場比賽都贏。
beyond ten o'clock: The store does not stay open beyond ten o'clock, so we need to buy the milk before it closes.
這家店十點以後就不營業了，所以我們得在關門前買牛奶。
and beyond: Our teacher hopes we will keep learning English in high school, in college, and beyond.
我們的老師希望我們在高中、大學以及更遠的未來都繼續學英文。
go beyond the limit: If you go beyond the limit of two hours of screen time, your eyes will feel tired and dry.
如果你超過兩小時螢幕時間的限度，眼睛會覺得又累又乾。
by ten o'clock: Please finish your homework by ten o'clock tonight, or you will be too tired to get up for school tomorrow.
請在今晚十點前完成作業，否則明天你會累到起不來上學。
by tomorrow: The teacher told us to hand in our book reports by tomorrow, so I have to finish reading tonight.
老師要我們在明天以前交讀書報告，所以我今晚必須把書讀完。
by the end of the week: By the end of the week, we must choose a topic for our science project and tell the teacher.
我們必須在週末前選好科學專題的題目，並告訴老師。
by then: The train leaves at six, and by then we will have packed our bags and said goodbye to Grandma.
火車六點出發，到那時候我們應該已經收好行李，並和奶奶道別了。
by now: The bus left an hour ago, so my brother should be at the airport by now and waiting for his flight.
公車一小時前就出發了，所以我弟弟到現在應該已經在機場等他的班機了。
by the time I got home: By the time I got home, my family had already finished dinner, so I ate the noodles alone in the kitchen.
我到家時，家人已經吃完晚餐了，所以我獨自在廚房吃麵。
by day: Owls sleep by day and hunt for food at night, which is why we rarely see them in the park.
貓頭鷹白天睡覺，晚上出來覓食，這就是為什麼我們很少在公園看到它們。
by night: The city looks completely different by night, with bright lights shining from every tall building and shop.
這座城市夜間看起來完全不同，每棟高樓和商店都閃著明亮的燈光。
day by day: Day by day, the little plant on my desk grew taller, and finally a small yellow flower appeared.
我桌上的小植物一天天地長高，最後開出了一朵小黃花。
little by little: Little by little, my grandfather learned to use his new phone, and now he sends us pictures every day.
我爺爺一點一點地學會用新手機，現在每天都傳照片給我們。
one by one: The students walked up to the stage one by one to receive their prizes from the school principal.
學生們一個一個地走上舞台，從校長手中領取獎品。
by the hour: My cousin works at the coffee shop and gets paid by the hour, so she tries to work longer on weekends.
我表姊在咖啡店工作，按小時領薪水，所以她週末盡量多排班。
step by step: The teacher showed us step by step how to make a paper boat, and soon everyone had a boat of their own.
老師一步一步地教我們怎麼摺紙船，很快每個人都有了自己的船。
sit by the window: I always like to sit by the window on the train so that I can watch the mountains and rice fields.
搭火車時我總喜歡坐在窗邊，這樣就能看山和稻田。
a house by the sea: My dream is to live in a small house by the sea, where I can hear the waves every morning.
我的夢想是住在海邊的一間小房子，每天早上都能聽到海浪聲。
stand by the door: A guard stands by the door of the bank all day to keep the customers and the money safe.
一位警衛整天站在銀行門邊，保護顧客和錢的安全。
by the river: Every Sunday afternoon, my family has a picnic by the river and feeds bread to the ducks.
每個星期日下午，我們家都在河邊野餐，並拿麵包餵鴨子。
pass by the shop: When I pass by the shop on my way home, I always stop to look at the toys in the window.
我回家路上經過商店時，總會停下來看櫥窗裡的玩具。
walk by: An old man walked by slowly with his dog, and he smiled at us when we said good morning.
一位老先生帶著狗慢慢走過，我們說早安時他對我們微笑。
close by: My best friend lives close by, so we ride our bikes to school together every morning.
我最好的朋友住在附近，所以我們每天早上一起騎腳踏車上學。
by my side: When I was sick in the hospital, my mother stayed by my side all night and held my hand.
我生病住院時，媽媽整晚待在我身邊，握著我的手。
by bus: It takes about thirty minutes to get to the museum by bus, but it is much faster if you take the MRT.
搭公車到博物館大約要三十分鐘，但搭捷運快很多。
by train: We are going to Tainan by train this weekend because the trip is cheaper and we can enjoy the view.
這個週末我們要搭火車去台南，因為比較便宜，而且可以欣賞風景。
by car: My father usually goes to work by car, but today he took the bus because the car needed repairs.
我爸爸通常開車上班，但今天車子要修理，所以他搭公車。
by bike: Many students in our school come to class by bike because it is good exercise and saves money.
我們學校很多學生騎腳踏車上學，因為這是很好的運動，也能省錢。
by plane: Traveling to Japan by plane takes only three hours, so we can arrive before lunch and start our trip.
搭飛機去日本只要三小時，所以我們可以在午餐前抵達並開始旅程。
by boat: To visit the small island, you must go by boat because there is no bridge or airport there.
要去那座小島必須搭船，因為那裡沒有橋也沒有機場。
by hand: My grandmother makes all her sweaters by hand, and each one takes her about two weeks to finish.
我奶奶所有的毛衣都是用手工做的，每一件大約要花她兩個星期完成。
by mail: I sent the birthday card to my aunt by mail, and she said it arrived just in time for her party.
我把生日卡片郵寄給阿姨，她說剛好在派對前收到了。
by phone: Mom ordered a pizza by phone, and a young man brought it to our door in just twenty minutes.
媽媽用電話訂了披薩，一位年輕人只花二十分鐘就送到我們家門口。
by email: Our teacher sends us the homework by email every Friday, so we can check it even when we are at home.
我們老師每個星期五用電子郵件把作業寄給我們，所以我們在家也能查看。
by check: My father paid for the new refrigerator by check because he did not want to carry so much cash.
我爸爸用支票付新冰箱的錢，因為他不想帶那麼多現金。
by credit card: Many people pay by credit card at the supermarket now, but my grandmother still likes to use cash.
現在很多人在超市用信用卡付款，但我奶奶還是喜歡用現金。
pay by cash (常誤) → pay in cash: Some students say pay by cash by mistake, but the correct way is to say that we pay in cash.
有些學生會誤說 pay by cash，但正確的說法是我們 pay in cash（用現金付款）。
by heart: I learned the whole poem by heart last night, so I can say it in front of the class without looking.
我昨晚把整首詩記住了，所以可以不看稿在全班面前背出來。
by mistake: I took my sister's umbrella by mistake this morning because it looks almost the same as mine.
今天早上我不小心拿了姊姊的雨傘，因為它和我的看起來幾乎一樣。
by accident: The famous cookie was invented by accident when a baker put the wrong kind of chocolate in the cake mix.
這種著名的餅乾是意外地發明出來的，因為一位麵包師傅把錯的巧克力放進蛋糕糊裡。
by chance: I met my old teacher by chance at the night market, and we talked about my first year at school.
我在夜市碰巧遇到以前的老師，我們聊起了我在學校第一年的日子。
by the way: By the way, did you remember to bring the tickets for the movie, or are they still at home?
順便一提，你記得帶電影票了嗎？還是它們還在家裡？
by oneself: Since my parents both work late, I often have to cook dinner and eat by myself on weekdays.
因為我爸媽都工作到很晚，平日我常常得自己煮晚餐並獨自吃飯。
by weight: At the fruit stand, apples and oranges are sold by weight, so bigger fruit usually costs more money.
在水果攤，蘋果和橘子是按重量賣的，所以越大的水果通常越貴。
by name: Our new teacher is very kind, and she already knows every student in the class by name after only two days.
我們的新老師很親切，她才來兩天就已經能按名字認出班上每一位學生了。
a book by Mark Twain: My brother is reading a book by Mark Twain for his English class, and he says the story is really funny.
我哥哥正在為英文課讀一本馬克吐溫寫的書，他說那個故事真的很好笑。
a song by the band: We listened to a song by the band on the radio this morning, and now I cannot stop singing it.
今天早上我們在收音機上聽了這個樂團的一首歌，現在我忍不住一直唱。
be hit by a car: Please look both ways before you cross the road, because a boy was hit by a car near our school last week.
過馬路前請左右看一下，因為上週有個男孩在我們學校附近被車撞了。
be made by hand: These little cookies are made by hand in my grandmother's kitchen, so each one looks a little different.
這些小餅乾是在我奶奶的廚房裡手工製作的，所以每一片看起來都有點不一樣。
be surprised by the news: Everyone in the office was surprised by the news that our quiet manager was going to get married next month.
辦公室裡每個人都對我們安靜的經理下個月要結婚的消息感到驚訝。
by far: Of all the restaurants in this town, the small noodle shop near the station is by far the most popular.
在這個鎮上所有的餐廳中，車站附近的小麵店遠遠是最受歡迎的。
by all means: If you want to borrow my bike this weekend, by all means take it, because I will be busy at home anyway.
如果你這個週末想借我的腳踏車，務必拿去用，因為我反正會在家忙。
by no means: The math test was by no means easy, so most of the students in my class needed the whole hour to finish it.
這次數學考試絕不簡單，所以我班上大部分的學生都需要整整一小時才能寫完。
by the sea: My aunt lives in a small white house by the sea, and we can hear the waves from her bedroom window at night.
我阿姨住在海邊一棟白色的小房子裡，晚上我們從她臥室的窗戶就能聽到海浪聲。
by nature: My little sister is shy by nature, so she often hides behind my mother when she meets new people.
我的小妹天生害羞，所以她遇到新朋友時常常躲在我媽媽身後。
by birth: Although Mr. Lin is Japanese by birth, he has lived in Taiwan for twenty years and speaks Chinese very well.
雖然林先生出生起就是日本人，但他已經在台灣住了二十年，中文說得很好。
by law: By law, everyone who rides a motorcycle in Taiwan must wear a hat for safety, or they will have to pay money.
依法，在台灣騎機車的每個人都必須戴安全帽，否則就得罰錢。
by the rules: Our coach always tells us to play by the rules, because winning a game is not important if we cheat.
我們的教練總是告訴我們要按規定比賽，因為如果作弊，贏得比賽也不重要。
by myself: I finished the whole science project by myself last night, so I feel very proud of my work today.
我昨晚靠我自己完成了整個自然科學作業，所以今天我對我的作品感到很驕傲。
three by three: The teacher drew a big square on the board and divided it into three by three smaller boxes for our game.
老師在黑板上畫了一個大正方形，然後把它分成三乘三的小格子來玩我們的遊戲。
by (在…之前) vs. until (直到): You must hand in the report by Monday, but you can keep the library book until the end of the month.
你必須在週一之前交報告，但那本圖書館的書你可以一直借到月底。
Our teacher asked us to finish the English report by Friday, so my group will meet after school every day.
我們老師要我們在週五前完成英文報告，所以我這組每天放學後都會聚在一起。
I must go back to Taipei by Thursday, but Grandma will wait here until Friday, because my uncle will pick her up then.
我週四前必須回台北，但奶奶會在這等到週五，因為我叔叔那時候會來接她。
by bus (交通方式) vs. on the bus (在車上): I usually go to school by bus, and this morning I met my best friend on the bus, so we talked the whole way.
我通常搭公車上學，今天早上我在公車上遇到我最好的朋友，所以我們一路聊天。
by car vs. in the car: We went to the beach by car, and my little brother slept in the car for the whole trip because it was so early.
我們開車去海邊，我的小弟弟因為太早起，整段路程都在車裡睡覺。
on foot (不用 by): My father goes to work by bus, but because the bookstore is only five minutes away, I always go there on foot.
我爸爸搭公車上班，但因為書店只有五分鐘的路程，我總是走路去那裡。
by hand vs. with my hands: My grandmother still makes dumplings by hand, and she taught me to shape each one carefully with my hands.
我奶奶還是手工做水餃，而且她教我用我的手小心地把每一顆捏成形。
by (工具／方法) vs. with (手持工具): You can pay for the tickets by credit card at the window, or you can buy them with coins from the machine.
你可以在窗口用信用卡付票錢，或是用硬幣在機器買票。
cut it with a knife: Mom paid for the birthday cake by credit card, and then she told me to cut it with a knife into eight pieces.
媽媽用信用卡付了生日蛋糕的錢，然後她叫我用刀把它切成八塊。
send it by mail: Instead of sending the photos by email, my grandfather likes to send them by mail in a big brown envelope.
我爺爺不喜歡用電子郵件寄照片，他喜歡用一個棕色大信封郵寄。
by (被動作者) vs. with (材料): The letter was written by my cousin, and she filled the whole page with little hearts drawn with a red pen.
這封信是由我表姊寫的，她用一支紅筆畫的小愛心填滿了整頁。
be written by him: This poem was written by him when he was only twelve, and now every student in our school reads it.
這首詩是他十二歲時由他所寫的，現在我們學校每個學生都在讀它。
be covered with snow: The mountain road was covered with snow, so the path was closed by the police and nobody could drive up.
山路被雪覆蓋了，所以那條路被警察封閉，沒有人可以開車上山。
be made of wood: The old table was made by my grandfather, and because it is made of wood, we clean it with a dry towel every week.
這張舊桌子是我爺爺做的，而且因為它是木製的，我們每週都用一條乾毛巾擦它。
be made from grapes: The sweet purple juice is made from grapes, and the grapes are grown by a farmer who lives near my uncle.
這種甜甜的紫色果汁是由葡萄製成的，而那些葡萄是由住在我舅舅家附近的一位農夫種的。
by far the best: Of all the movies we watched this summer, the one about the lost dog was by far the best, and we all cried.
在我們今年夏天看過的所有電影中，那部關於走失小狗的電影是到目前為止最好的，我們全都哭了。
go down the stairs: Be careful when you go down the stairs at night, because the light at the bottom has not worked for a week.
晚上走下樓梯時要小心，因為樓梯底下的燈已經壞了一個星期。
walk down the street: Every Sunday morning, my grandfather and I walk down the street to buy fresh bread and hot milk tea.
每個星期天早上，我和爺爺都會沿街走去買新鮮的麵包和熱奶茶。
fall down the hill: The little boy lost his ball and almost fell down the hill while he was running after it in the park.
小男孩的球丟了，他在公園裡追球時差點滾下山坡。
down the road: There is a small night market just down the road from our school, and the fried chicken there is delicious.
從我們學校沿路過去有一個小夜市，那裡的炸雞很好吃。
roll down the hill: We watched the big orange ball roll down the hill, and the dog chased it all the way to the river.
我們看著那顆橘色大球滾下山坡，而那隻狗一路追著它到河邊。
down the river: The boat moved slowly down the river, and we saw many white birds standing in the water along the way.
小船順流而下慢慢地前進，沿途我們看到許多白色的鳥站在水中。
down the hall: The nurse told us to walk down the hall and turn left, because the doctor's room is at the very end.
護士告訴我們沿走廊走然後左轉，因為醫生的診間就在最尾端。
look down the well: The children stood at the edge to look down the well, but it was so deep and dark that they could not see the water.
孩子們站在井邊往井下看，但井又深又黑，他們看不到水。
sit down: When the teacher walked into the room, she asked everyone to sit down quickly and take out their English books.
老師走進教室時，要大家快點坐下並拿出英文課本。
lie down: After playing basketball for two hours in the hot sun, Jack went home and lay down on the sofa for a rest.
在大太陽下打了兩小時的籃球後，傑克回到家躺下在沙發上休息。
turn down the TV: Could you please turn down the TV a little, because the baby is sleeping in the next room and might wake up?
可以請你把電視關小聲一點嗎？因為寶寶在隔壁房間睡覺，可能會被吵醒。
turn down the offer: My father decided to turn down the offer of a new job in Japan because he did not want to leave our family.
我爸爸決定拒絕去日本工作的新提議，因為他不想離開我們的家人。
write down the number: Please write down the number of the shop on this piece of paper, so we can call them if the cake is late.
請把店家的號碼寫下在這張紙上，這樣如果蛋糕送晚了我們就可以打電話給他們。
put down the pen: When the bell rang, the teacher told us to put down the pen at once and pass our test papers to the front.
鈴聲響起時，老師叫我們馬上放下筆，把考卷傳到前面。
calm down: My sister was so angry about the broken phone that it took her an hour to calm down and talk to us again.
我姐姐對手機壞掉這件事非常生氣，她花了一小時才冷靜下來再跟我們說話。
slow down: The road was wet after the heavy rain, so Dad told the taxi driver to slow down near the school.
大雨過後路面很濕，所以爸爸請計程車司機在學校附近慢下來。
break down: Our old washing machine finally broke down last night, so we had to wash all the clothes by hand this morning.
我們的舊洗衣機昨晚終於故障了，所以今天早上我們只好用手洗所有的衣服。
cut down on sugar: The doctor told my uncle to cut down on sugar and sweet drinks, because he has gained too much weight this year.
醫生要我叔叔減少吃糖和含糖飲料，因為他今年體重增加太多了。
let sb. down: I promised to help Tom with his science project, so I cannot let him down just because I want to watch TV tonight.
我答應要幫湯姆做自然作業，所以我不能只因為今晚想看電視就讓他失望。
You should never look down on people who have less money than you, because everyone has something to teach us.
你永遠不應該看不起比你沒錢的人，因為每個人都有值得我們學習的地方。
come down with a cold: Mary came down with a cold after she played in the rain, so she stayed home from school for two days.
瑪麗在雨中玩耍之後感冒了，所以她在家休息兩天沒去上學。
settle down: After moving to five different cities, my uncle finally decided to settle down in a quiet town near the mountains.
搬了五個不同的城市之後，我叔叔終於決定在山邊一個安靜的小鎮安頓下來。
fall down: The floor in the kitchen was wet, and my little brother fell down and started to cry very loudly.
廚房的地板是濕的，我的小弟弟跌倒了，然後開始大聲地哭。
get down to work: Stop playing games on your phone and get down to work, because the big test is only three days away.
別再用手機玩遊戲了，開始認真工作，因為大考只剩三天了。
burn down: The old house at the end of our street burned down last night, but luckily nobody was hurt in the fire.
我們這條街盡頭的那間老房子昨晚燒毀了，但幸好沒有人在火災中受傷。
pull down the old house: The city plans to pull down the old house next to the park and build a new library for the children there.
市政府計畫拆掉公園旁邊的舊房子，在那裡為孩子們蓋一座新圖書館。
take down the notes: During the class, I always take down the notes carefully, so I can study them again before the test.
上課時我總是仔細地記下筆記，這樣考試前我才能再複習。
back down: The two boys argued about the game for an hour, but neither of them would back down and say sorry first.
兩個男孩為了那場比賽吵了一小時，但他們都不肯退讓先道歉。
close down: The little toy shop near my school had to close down last month because fewer and fewer people shopped there.
我學校附近的那間小玩具店上個月不得不關閉，因為去那裡買東西的人越來越少。
cool down: Let the soup cool down for a few minutes before you drink it, or you will burn your tongue again like yesterday.
喝湯前先讓它冷卻幾分鐘，否則你會像昨天一樣又燙到舌頭。
go down (price): The price of vegetables will go down after the typhoon season ends, so Mom is waiting to buy more then.
颱風季結束後蔬菜的價格就會下跌，所以媽媽等著那時候再多買一些。
knock down: A fast motorcycle almost knocked down an old woman on the street this morning, but luckily she jumped back in time.
今天早上一輛快速的機車差點在街上撞倒一位老太太，幸好她及時往後跳開。
bring down the price: The shop owner agreed to bring down the price of the bike by two hundred dollars because it had a small mark on it.
店老闆同意把那輛腳踏車降價兩百元，因為車上有一個小痕跡。
hold down a job: My cousin found it hard to hold down a job because he was always late for work and argued with his boss.
我表哥覺得很難保住工作，因為他上班老是遲到，還跟老闆吵架。
shut down: The factory near the river had to shut down for a month because it was making the water dirty and smell bad.
河邊的那間工廠因為把河水弄得又髒又臭，必須關閉一個月。
stand down: After the two teams finished the game, the coach told the players to stand down and let the next group practice.
兩隊比完賽後，教練要球員退下，讓下一組練習。
keep the noise down: Mom asked us to keep the noise down while Grandpa was sleeping in the next room after lunch.
媽媽要我們在爺爺午餐後在隔壁房間睡覺時保持安靜。
upside down: My little sister held the picture book upside down and laughed because all the animals looked like they were falling.
我小妹把圖畫書拿得上下顛倒，然後笑了出來，因為所有的動物看起來都像在往下掉。
be down: Jenny has been down all week because her best friend moved to another city, so let's invite her to the movies.
珍妮這整個星期心情都很低落，因為她最好的朋友搬到別的城市去了，我們邀她去看電影吧。
feel down: Whenever I feel down after a bad test, my mother makes my favorite noodles and tells me funny stories.
每次考試考差讓我覺得沮喪時，我媽媽就會煮我最愛的麵，講好笑的故事給我聽。
down with the flu: Half of the players on our basketball team are down with the flu, so the game on Saturday has been cancelled.
我們籃球隊有一半的球員因流感而病倒，所以星期六的比賽取消了。
down to earth: Although Mr. Wang is a famous singer, he is very down to earth and still eats at the same little night market.
雖然王先生是有名的歌手，他卻非常腳踏實地，仍然在同一個小夜市吃東西。
from top to bottom: Before Grandma arrived, we washed the house from top to bottom and even got down to clean the dirty space under the beds.
在奶奶到達之前，我們把房子從頭到尾打掃乾淨，甚至蹲下來清床底下髒髒的地方。
ups and downs: Every friendship has its ups and downs, but good friends always find a way to talk and forgive each other.
每段友誼都有起起落落，但好朋友總會找到方法溝通並原諒彼此。
down to the last one: The cookies were so delicious that my brother and I ate them down to the last one before Dad came home.
餅乾太好吃了，我和弟弟在爸爸回家前就把它們吃到最後一個都不剩。
be down to two choices: After talking for an hour, we are down to two choices for our class trip, the zoo or the beach.
討論了一小時後，我們班級旅行只剩兩個選擇，動物園或海邊。
Down with the king!: In the story, the angry people marched to the castle and shouted Down with the king because he took all their food.
在故事裡，憤怒的人民遊行到城堡前大喊打倒國王，因為他拿走了他們所有的食物。
count down: On New Year's Eve, the whole family stood in front of the TV and began to count down from ten together.
除夕夜，全家人站在電視前，一起從十開始倒數。
during the summer: During the summer, my family usually goes to the beach in the south, and we swim in the sea every morning.
在夏天期間，我家通常會去南部的海邊，我們每天早上都在海裡游泳。
during the class: Please do not talk to your friends during the class, because the other students cannot hear what the teacher says.
上課時請不要和朋友聊天，因為其他同學會聽不到老師在說什麼。
during the night: It rained heavily during the night, so the playground was full of water when we got to school this morning.
夜裡下了大雨，所以今天早上我們到學校時操場滿是水。
during the meeting: My father turned off his phone during the meeting, so he did not see my message about the school play until later.
我爸爸在會議期間把手機關了，所以他後來才看到我關於學校話劇的訊息。
during lunch: Our teacher let us watch a short English movie during lunch today, and everyone ate quietly for once.
今天午餐時我們老師讓我們看一部英文短片，大家難得安靜地吃飯。
during the trip: We took hundreds of pictures during the trip to Japan, and my favorite one shows my sister eating a big ice cream.
旅途中我們在日本拍了幾百張照片，我最喜歡的那張是我姐姐在吃一支大冰淇淋。
during the day: My grandmother sleeps very little during the day because she likes to work in her garden and talk with her neighbors.
我奶奶白天很少睡覺，因為她喜歡在花園裡忙，還有跟鄰居聊天。
during the war: During the war, my great-grandfather had very little food, so he never wastes even one bowl of rice today.
戰時我的曾祖父食物非常少，所以他現在連一碗飯都不會浪費。
during the show: Please turn off your phones during the show, because the bright light will bother the people sitting behind you.
表演期間請關掉手機，因為亮光會干擾坐在你後面的人。
during the week: I have to get up at six during the week, but on Saturday and Sunday I can sleep until ten.
平日我必須六點起床，但星期六和星期日我可以睡到十點。
during (期間, 名詞) vs. while (當…時, 子句): My little brother fell asleep during the long movie, while my parents were still laughing at the funny parts.
我的小弟弟在長長的電影期間睡著了，當時我父母還在為好笑的部分大笑。
during the meal: Nobody in my family is allowed to use a phone during the meal, so we talk about our day at school instead.
我家用餐時不准任何人用手機，所以我們改聊在學校的一天。
while we were eating: While we were eating dinner, the lights went out, and during the dark minutes my little sister held my hand hard.
我們在吃飯時燈熄了，在黑暗的那幾分鐘裡，我的小妹妹緊緊握著我的手。
during (何時) vs. for (多久): It snowed during the winter holiday, and my cousins played outside in the snow for three hours every day.
寒假期間下雪了，我的表兄弟姐妹每天在外面的雪地裡玩三個小時。
during the night (時段): The baby woke up three times during the night, so my aunt looked very tired at breakfast this morning.
寶寶夜間醒來了三次，所以今天早上吃早餐時我阿姨看起來很累。
for three hours (長度): We waited in line for three hours during the holiday to buy tickets for the famous new movie about dragons.
假期期間我們排了三小時的隊，去買那部有名的新龍電影的票。
in the night: The dogs next door barked during the night and woke me up, so I was sleepy in class the next morning.
隔壁的狗夜間叫個不停，把我吵醒了，所以隔天早上我在課堂上很困。
during vs. in (強調全程): It rained during the whole trip, so we spent most of our time in the hotel playing cards and watching TV.
整趟旅途全程都在下雨，所以我們大部分的時間都在飯店打牌和看電視。
everyone except me: Everyone except me went to the night market after the game, because I had to go home and finish my homework.
比賽後除了我每個人都去了夜市，因為我得回家寫完功課。
every day except Sunday: The small bakery near our house opens early every day except Sunday, when the owner goes to church with his family.
我們家附近的小麵包店除了週日每天都早早開門，週日老闆會和家人去教堂。
except for the rain: Except for the rain on the last day, our trip to the mountains was perfect, and we all want to go again next year.
除了最後一天下雨以外，我們的山區之旅很完美，我們都想明年再去。
nothing except water: The doctor told my father to drink nothing except water for one day before he goes to the hospital for the test.
醫生告訴我爸爸在去醫院檢查前一天，除了水什麼都不能喝。
do anything except study: On weekends my lazy brother will do anything except study, so he cleans his room and even washes the dog.
週末我那懶惰的哥哥什麼都做就是不讀書，所以他打掃房間，甚至幫狗洗澡。
all except one: All except one of the students passed the English test, and the teacher promised to help that student after class.
除了一個以外全部學生都通過了英文考試，老師答應下課後幫助那位學生。
except that it was cold: The picnic by the lake was really fun, except that it was cold, so we drank hot tea to keep warm.
湖邊的野餐真的很好玩，只不過天氣冷，所以我們喝熱茶保暖。
except when it rains: My grandfather walks in the park every morning except when it rains, and then he does exercises at home instead.
我爺爺每天早上都去公園散步，除了下雨的時候，那時他就改在家裡做運動。
except (不含) vs. besides (包含): Everyone except Amy likes math, but besides math, Amy also enjoys science, so she is still a very good student.
除了艾美每個人都喜歡數學，但除了數學之外，艾美也喜歡自然科學，所以她還是個很好的學生。
except vs. except for: All the students except Jack brought lunch, and except for the heavy rain, it would have been a great picnic day.
除了傑克之外所有學生都帶了午餐，若不是那場大雨，那本來會是很棒的野餐日。
Except for Tom, everyone came to the party on time, because he missed the bus and had to walk all the way.
除了湯姆，大家都準時來到派對，因為他錯過了公車，只好一路走過來。
except vs. expect (期待): I expect my friends to come to my birthday party on Sunday, and everyone except Lisa has already said yes.
我期待朋友們星期日來我的生日派對，而除了麗莎以外每個人都已經答應了。
but: Nobody in the class except Peter knew the answer, but he said nothing because he is too shy to speak up.
班上除了彼得沒有人知道答案，但他什麼都沒說，因為他太害羞不敢開口。
accept (接受) vs. except (除了): Mary would accept any job except one that makes her work on weekends, because she wants time with her family.
瑪麗願意接受任何工作，除了要週末上班的工作，因為她想要和家人共度時光。
for three hours: We waited for three hours at the airport because the plane was late, and my little brother slept the whole time.
因為飛機誤點，我們在機場等了三小時，我的小弟弟整段時間都在睡覺。
for a long time: My grandfather and grandmother have lived in the same old house by the river for a long time, and they never want to move.
我的爺爺和奶奶在河邊同一棟老房子住了很長一段時間，他們從來不想搬家。
for a while: After the long walk up the mountain, we sat down on a big rock for a while and enjoyed the cool wind.
爬了很久的山之後，我們在一塊大石頭上坐了一會兒，享受涼風。
for ages: I have not seen my cousin for ages, so I was really excited when she called to say she was visiting this weekend.
我很久沒見到我表姊了，所以當她打電話說這週末要來看我時，我真的很興奮。
for the first time: Yesterday my little sister rode a bike without help for the first time, and she laughed all the way down the street.
昨天我小妹第一次沒人幫忙就騎腳踏車，她一路沿街笑著騎過去。
for the moment: For the moment, we are staying at my aunt's house, but we will move into our new apartment at the end of May.
目前我們住在我阿姨家，但五月底我們就會搬進新的公寓。
for now: For now, please put your bags under your desks, and I will tell you where to leave them after the meeting.
暫時請把你們的袋子放在桌子底下，會議結束後我再告訴你們要放哪裡。
for ever: When I was a child, I thought my grandfather would live for ever, so I was very sad when he got sick.
小時候我以為爺爺會永遠活著，所以當他生病時我非常難過。
for good: After the terrible typhoon, my uncle decided to leave the small island for good and move to Kaohsiung with his family.
那場可怕的颱風之後，我叔叔決定永遠離開那座小島，和家人搬到高雄。
for life: My grandmother says that a good book can be a friend for life, so she still keeps her favorite one from school.
我奶奶說一本好書可以是終生的朋友，所以她還留著她學生時代最愛的那本書。
for the time being: The computer room is closed for the time being, so students must use the library computers to finish their reports.
電腦教室目前暫時關閉，所以學生們必須用圖書館的電腦來完成報告。
a gift for you: I made a gift for you with my own hands, and I hope you will like the little blue bird on the card.
我親手做了一份給你的禮物，希望你會喜歡卡片上那隻藍色的小鳥。
a letter for me: There was a letter for me on the kitchen table this morning, and it came all the way from my friend in Japan.
今天早上廚房桌上有一封給我的信，是我在日本的朋友千里迢迢寄來的。
leave for Taipei: We have to leave for Taipei at six tomorrow morning, so please pack your bags and go to bed early tonight.
我們明天早上六點就得出發去台北，所以今晚請把行李收好早點睡。
the train for Tainan: The train for Tainan leaves from platform two in ten minutes, so we should hurry and buy our tickets now.
開往台南的火車十分鐘後從第二月台出發，所以我們應該快點現在就買票。
wait for the bus: Every morning I wait for the bus with my neighbor Lily, and we talk about our favorite TV shows until it comes.
每天早上我都和鄰居莉莉一起等公車，我們聊最愛的電視節目直到公車來。
look for the keys: Dad spent twenty minutes looking for the keys this morning, and in the end he found them in his coat pocket.
今天早上爸爸花了二十分鐘找鑰匙，最後他在外套口袋裡找到了。
ask for help: If you do not understand the homework, you should ask for help from the teacher instead of copying from a friend.
如果你不懂作業，你應該向老師請求幫助，而不是抄朋友的。
pay for the meal: My uncle always wants to pay for the meal when we eat out, but this time my father got to the counter first.
我們外食時我叔叔總是想付餐費，但這次我爸爸先到了櫃台。
thank you for coming: Thank you for coming to my birthday party tonight, and I hope you enjoyed the chocolate cake my mother made.
謝謝你今晚來我的生日派對，希望你喜歡我媽媽做的巧克力蛋糕。
for sale: The red house across the street has been for sale for six months, but nobody wants to buy it because it is so old.
對街那棟紅房子已經出售六個月了，但因為太舊沒有人想買。
for rent: My aunt has a small apartment for rent near the university, so many college students come to look at it every week.
我阿姨在大學附近有一間小公寓要出租，所以每週都有很多大學生來看房。
for free: The museum is open for free on the first Sunday of every month, so my class is planning to visit it together.
博物館每個月的第一個星期日免費開放，所以我們班計畫一起去參觀。
for fun: On Saturday afternoons, my friends and I play basketball just for fun, and nobody cares who wins or loses.
星期六下午我和朋友打籃球只是為了好玩，沒有人在乎誰輸誰贏。
for example: Many foods are good for your eyes, for example carrots, eggs and fish, so you should eat them more often.
許多食物對眼睛有益，例如紅蘿蔔、雞蛋和魚，所以你應該多吃一些。
for instance: My brother is interested in many sports, for instance swimming, baseball and tennis, so he is never bored on weekends.
我哥哥對許多運動都有興趣，例如游泳、棒球和網球，所以他週末從不無聊。
for sure: I do not know if it will rain tomorrow, but for sure it will be very hot, so bring a hat and some water.
我不知道明天會不會下雨，但肯定會非常熱，所以要帶帽子和水。
for a change: We always eat rice for dinner, so tonight Mom is going to cook noodles with tomato and beef for a change.
我們晚餐總是吃飯，所以今晚媽媽要換換口味煮番茄牛肉麵。
for the weekend: What are your plans for the weekend, because my family is going to the beach and you are welcome to join us?
你週末有什麼計畫？因為我家要去海邊，歡迎你加入我們。
for breakfast: My father usually has an egg and a cup of coffee for breakfast, but on Sundays he makes sandwiches for everyone.
我爸爸早餐通常吃一顆蛋配一杯咖啡，但星期天他會做三明治給大家吃。
