What is this for?: When my grandmother saw the strange little machine in the kitchen, she asked my brother, What is this for?
我奶奶看到廚房裡那台奇怪的小機器時，問我哥哥：這是做什麼用的？
good for your health: Doctors say that walking for thirty minutes every day is good for your health, so my parents walk after dinner.
醫生說每天走路三十分鐘對健康有益，所以我父母晚餐後都會去散步。
bad for your eyes: Reading in the dark is bad for your eyes, so please turn on the lamp before you open your comic book.
在黑暗中閱讀對眼睛不好，所以請在打開漫畫書前把檯燈開著。
be famous for: The small town where my grandfather lives is famous for its sweet pineapple cakes, and visitors buy them every day.
我爺爺住的那個小鎮以香甜的鳳梨酥聞名，遊客每天都來買。
be known for: Our English teacher is known for her funny jokes, so nobody ever falls asleep in her class, even after lunch.
我們的英文老師以她好笑的笑話著稱，所以就算是午餐後也沒有人在她的課上睡著。
be late for school: I was late for school again this morning because I forgot to set my alarm clock before I went to bed.
今天早上我上學又遲到了，因為我睡前忘了設鬧鐘。
be ready for the test: I studied for three hours last night, so I feel ready for the test and I am not nervous at all today.
我昨晚讀了三小時的書，所以我覺得已經準備好考試，今天一點也不緊張。
be sorry for: Tom felt sorry for breaking his sister's favorite cup, so he bought her a new one with his pocket money.
湯姆為打破姐姐最愛的杯子感到抱歉，所以他用零用錢買了一個新的給她。
a table for two: When we walked into the restaurant, my father asked the waiter for a table for two by the window with a view.
我們走進餐廳時，爸爸向服務生要了一張靠窗有風景的兩人桌。
for one thing: I do not want to join the baseball team, because for one thing, practice is every day, and I need time to study.
我不想加入棒球隊，因為一方面練習是每天都有，而我需要時間讀書。
for another: For one thing, the new phone is too expensive, and for another, my old one still works fine, so I will wait.
一方面新手機太貴，另一方面我的舊手機還能用，所以我會再等等。
for short: My brother's full name is Alexander, but everyone at school calls him Alex for short because it is easier to say.
我哥哥的全名是亞歷山大，但學校裡每個人都簡稱他艾力克斯，因為比較好叫。
for a living: My uncle sells fruit at the market for a living, and he gets up at four every morning to pick the best apples.
我叔叔在市場賣水果謀生，他每天早上四點起床挑最好的蘋果。
for the sake of: My mother stopped eating sweets for the sake of her health, and now she feels much better and has more energy.
我媽媽為了健康不再吃甜食，現在她覺得好多了，也更有活力。
for the most part: For the most part, the students in my class are friendly, so new students usually feel at home after a few days.
我班上的學生大部分都很友善，所以新同學通常幾天後就會覺得很自在。
for a reason: My mother always says things happen for a reason, so when I missed the bus, I just read a book and waited calmly.
我媽媽總是說事情發生都是有原因的，所以當我錯過公車時，我就只是看書，平靜地等待。
for nothing: We waited in the rain for an hour for nothing, because the store had already sold out of the game we wanted.
我們在雨中白白等了一小時，因為那間店已經把我們想要的遊戲賣完了。
for all I know: For all I know, the new student might be from Japan, because I heard him talking to his mother on the phone yesterday.
據我所知，那位新同學可能來自日本，因為我昨天聽到他在電話上和媽媽說話。
for once: My brother is always late for dinner, but for once he came home early tonight and even helped Mom set the table.
我哥哥吃晚餐總是遲到，但今晚他就這一次早早回家，甚至還幫媽媽擺餐具。
for real: At first I thought Peter was joking, but he is leaving for America for real next month, and his family has already packed.
一開始我以為彼得在開玩笑，但他下個月真的要去美國了，他的家人已經打包好了。
for the best: Moving to a new school was hard, but my parents told me it was for the best, and now I have many good friends.
轉到新學校很難受，但我父母告訴我那是為了最好的結果，現在我有很多好朋友。
for your information: For your information, the library will close early this Friday, so you should return your books before three o'clock.
供你參考，圖書館這個星期五會提早關門，所以你應該在三點前把書還回去。
be in for: If you forget to study for the big test again, you are in for a hard time when your parents see your grades.
如果你又忘了為大考準備，等你父母看到成績時你即將遭遇一段難受的日子。
run for president: In social studies class we learned that anyone over forty can run for president in our country, and we found that exciting.
社會課上我們學到在我們國家任何四十歲以上的人都可以競選總統，我們覺得這很令人興奮。
too big for me: This jacket is too big for me, so could you please bring me a smaller size in the same blue color?
這件夾克對我來說太大了，可以請你拿一件同樣藍色但小一號的給我嗎？
for 100 dollars: My sister bought a used bike for 100 dollars at the weekend market, and it still rides as well as a new one.
我姐姐在週末市集以一百元買了一輛二手腳踏車，它騎起來還像新的一樣好。
word for word: Our teacher told us not to copy the story word for word, but to write the ideas in our own simple English.
我們老師告訴我們不要逐字地抄那篇故事，而是用自己簡單的英文寫出想法。
once and for all: Let's clean up the dirty room once and for all today, so we do not have to argue about it every single weekend.
我們今天就把這間髒亂的房間一次解決打掃乾淨，這樣就不用每個週末為此吵架。
a feel for music: My little cousin has a real feel for music, because she can play any song on the piano after hearing it only once.
我的小表妹對音樂真的很有感覺，因為她只聽一遍就能在鋼琴上彈出任何歌。
have an eye for: My mother has an eye for pretty clothes, so my friends always ask her for advice before they go shopping.
我媽媽對漂亮衣服有鑑賞眼光，所以我的朋友去買衣服前總會向她請教。
take sb. for a fool: Do not take me for a fool, because I know you ate the last cookie even though you said the dog did it.
別把我當傻瓜，因為我知道最後一片餅乾是你吃的，雖然你說是狗吃的。
for the life of me: For the life of me, I cannot remember where I put my new glasses, and I have looked in every room of the house.
我怎麼也想不起來我把新眼鏡放哪了，我已經找遍家裡每個房間。
for all: For all his money and big house, my rich uncle often says that he is less happy than my parents in their small apartment.
儘管我有錢的叔叔有錢又有大房子，他常說他比住在小公寓裡的我父母還不快樂。
for (支持) vs. against (反對): Most students in my class voted for a longer lunch break, but three students were against the idea because school would end later.
我班上大部分的學生投票支持延長午休，但有三個學生反對這個想法，因為放學會變晚。
for (多久) vs. since (從何時起): My family has lived in Taichung for ten years, since 2016, and we still love the night markets here.
我家在台中住了十年，從二零一六年起，我們仍然很愛這裡的夜市。
for two years: Mr. Chen has taught English at our school for two years, and all his students say his classes are never boring.
陳老師在我們學校教英文已經兩年了，他所有的學生都說他的課從不無聊。
since 2020: My family has had the same little brown dog since 2020, and he still runs to the door for us every afternoon.
我家從二零二零年起就養著同一隻棕色小狗，他每天下午還是會跑到門口迎接我們。
for (多久) vs. during (哪段期間): It rained for two hours during the baseball game yesterday, so the players had to wait inside until it stopped.
昨天棒球比賽期間下了兩小時的雨，所以球員們得在室內等到雨停。
leave for (前往) vs. leave (離開): Dad will leave for Tainan at seven tomorrow, and after he leaves the house, I will have to feed the dog myself.
爸爸明天七點會出發前往台南，他離開家後，我就得自己餵狗。
leave Taipei for Tokyo: My aunt will leave Taipei for Tokyo next Monday because she found a new job at a hotel there.
我阿姨下週一會離開台北前往東京，因為她在那裡的一間飯店找到新工作。
wait for (等) vs. expect: I will wait for you at the station after school, and I expect you to be on time this time, Jack.
放學後我會在車站等你，傑克，我預期你這次會準時。
for (目的／對象) vs. to (方向): I baked these cookies for my grandmother, and tomorrow I will take the train to her house and give them to her.
我烤了這些餅乾給我奶奶，明天我會搭火車到她家把餅乾給她。
a gift for you vs. give it to you: This scarf is a gift for you, so please do not give it to your sister even if she says she loves it.
這條圍巾是給你的禮物，所以就算你姐姐說她很喜歡，也請不要把它給她。
It is kind of you (不用 for): It is very kind of you to carry my heavy bags for me, because my arm still hurts from the fall last week.
你真好心幫我提這些重袋子，因為我上週跌倒的手臂還在痛。
It is easy for me: It is easy for me to wake up early, but for my brother it is almost impossible without three alarm clocks.
對我來說早起很容易，但對我哥哥來說，沒有三個鬧鐘幾乎不可能。
famous for (特色) vs. famous as (身分): Our town is famous for its hot springs, and my grandfather is famous as the man who opened the first bath house there.
我們鎮上以溫泉聞名，而我爺爺則是以當地第一間澡堂的創辦人身分出名。
be good for (有益) vs. be good at (擅長): Swimming is good for your heart, and my cousin is also very good at it, so she goes to the pool every morning.
游泳對心臟有益，而我表姊也很擅長游泳，所以她每天早上都去泳池。
be sorry for (同情／抱歉) vs. sorry about: I feel sorry for Lisa because she lost her cat, and I am also sorry about missing her birthday party last night.
我為麗莎感到難過，因為她的貓不見了，我也對昨晚沒去她的生日派對感到抱歉。
come from Taiwan: The new girl in our class comes from Taiwan, but she has lived in America for five years, so her English is very good.
我們班的新女生來自台灣，但她在美國住了五年，所以英文非常好。
far from here: The new shopping center is not far from here, so we can walk there in ten minutes after we finish lunch.
新的購物中心離這裡不遠，所以我們吃完午餐後走十分鐘就能到。
from here to there: The teacher asked us to measure the distance from here to there, and we found it was about twenty meters.
老師要我們測量從這裡到那裡的距離，我們發現大約是二十公尺。
a letter from Mom: When I opened my lunch box at school, I found a short letter from Mom that said she was proud of me.
當我在學校打開便當盒時，發現一張媽媽寄來的短信，上面寫著她以我為榮。
the view from the top: After climbing for three hours, we finally enjoyed the view from the top, and the whole city looked like a toy.
爬了三小時後，我們終於欣賞到從山頂看的景色，整座城市看起來像玩具一樣。
fall from the tree: The little bird tried to fly but fell from the tree, so my brother carefully picked it up and put it back.
小鳥想要飛卻從樹上掉下來，所以我哥哥小心地把它撿起來放回去。
across from the park: The new ice cream shop is right across from the park, so we can buy some ice cream and eat it on the grass.
新的冰淇淋店就在公園對面，所以我們可以買冰淇淋坐在草地上吃。
from Monday to Friday: My mother works at the bank from Monday to Friday, so she only has time to go shopping with us on weekends.
我媽媽從週一到週五在銀行工作，所以她只有週末才有時間和我們去逛街。
from nine to five: My father works from nine to five at a small company, and he always comes home in time for dinner with us.
我爸爸在一家小公司從九點到五點上班，他總是準時回家和我們一起吃晚餐。
from now on: From now on, I will finish my homework before I play computer games, because my grades have dropped this semester.
從現在起，我會先寫完功課再玩電腦遊戲，因為我這學期的成績退步了。
from then on: Jenny failed her first English test last year, and from then on she studied hard every night after dinner.
珍妮去年第一次英文考試不及格，從那時起她每天晚餐後都用功讀書。
from time to time: My grandfather lives in Tainan, but he comes to Taipei from time to time to visit us on weekends.
我爺爺住在台南，但他偶爾會在週末來台北看我們。
from day to day: The weather here changes from day to day, so I always check it before I leave home in the morning.
這裡的天氣日復一日地變化，所以我早上出門前總是會先查看天氣。
from the start: From the start of the game, our team played very well, and we finally won by ten points.
從一開始比賽，我們的隊伍就表現得很好，最後我們以十分之差獲勝。
from morning till night: My mother works in the restaurant from morning till night, so she is always very tired on weekends.
我媽媽在餐廳從早到晚工作，所以她週末總是很累。
from the beginning: I missed the first part of the movie, so could you tell me the story from the beginning?
我錯過了電影的第一部分，所以你可以從頭開始把故事告訴我嗎？
from that day on: Peter got a puppy on his birthday, and from that day on he walked it every afternoon after school.
彼得生日那天得到一隻小狗，從那天起他每天放學後都帶它去散步。
be different from: Life in the country is very different from life in the city because it is quiet and slow.
鄉下的生活與城市的生活非常不同，因為鄉下既安靜又慢。
be far from perfect: My English is far from perfect, but I am not afraid to talk to foreign visitors at the night market.
我的英文離完美很遠，但我不怕在夜市和外國遊客聊天。
keep away from: The doctor told my father to keep away from sweet food because he has some health problems now.
醫生告訴我爸爸要遠離甜食，因為他現在有一些健康問題。
stay away from the dog: Stay away from the dog in the yard, because it does not like strangers and may bite you.
離院子裡那隻狗遠一點，因為它不喜歡陌生人，可能會咬你。
tell A from B: The two sisters look so much alike that even their teacher cannot tell Amy from Annie in class.
這兩姊妹長得太像了，連老師在課堂上都無法分辨艾咪與安妮。
know right from wrong: Children should learn to know right from wrong when they are young, so parents must teach them well.
孩子小時候就應該學會分辨對錯，所以父母必須好好教導他們。
die from hunger: In some poor countries, many children still die from hunger because they do not have enough food to eat.
在一些貧窮的國家，許多孩童仍然死於飢餓，因為他們沒有足夠的食物可吃。
be free from pain: After taking the medicine for three days, my grandmother is finally free from pain and can walk again.
吃了三天的藥之後，我奶奶終於沒有痛苦，可以再走路了。
be absent from school: Kevin was absent from school for a week because he had a bad cold and a high fever.
凱文缺課一個星期，因為他得了重感冒還發高燒。
borrow money from him: I left my wallet at home this morning, so I had to borrow money from him to buy lunch.
我今天早上把皮夾忘在家裡，所以我只好向他借錢買午餐。
learn from mistakes: We all make mistakes, but a smart student learns from mistakes and does not make them a second time.
我們都會犯錯，但聰明的學生會從錯誤中學習，不會再犯第二次。
stop sb. from doing: The heavy rain stopped us from playing basketball, so we stayed in the room and played cards together.
大雨阻止我們打籃球，所以我們待在房間裡一起玩牌。
keep sb. from doing: The loud music next door kept me from sleeping, so I felt very tired at school this morning.
隔壁大聲的音樂使我無法入睡，所以我今天早上在學校覺得很累。
protect from the sun: Please wear a hat and put on some cream to protect your skin from the sun at the beach.
請戴帽子並塗一些乳霜，在海邊保護你的皮膚防曬。
hide from the rain: It suddenly started to rain very hard, so we ran into a small store to hide from the rain.
突然下起大雨，所以我們跑進一家小店躲雨。
I have not heard from my cousin since she moved to Japan, so I will write to her tonight.
自從我表姊搬到日本後我就沒收到她的消息，所以今晚我要寫信給她。
from my point of view: From my point of view, students should not use their phones in class because they cannot pay attention.
以我的觀點，學生不應該在課堂上用手機，因為這樣他們無法專心。
from the look of it: From the look of it, the cake in the window is very sweet, but we should ask the price first.
從外表看來，櫥窗裡的蛋糕很甜，但我們應該先問價錢。
from head to toe: After the game in the rain, the boys were dirty and wet from head to toe, so Mom was not happy.
在雨中比賽之後，男孩們從頭到腳又髒又濕，所以媽媽不太高興。
from house to house: On Halloween night, the children went from house to house and asked for candy in their funny clothes.
萬聖節晚上，孩子們穿著滑稽的服裝一家一家地要糖果。
from side to side: The little boat moved from side to side on the big waves, and some people on it got sick.
小船在大浪上左右搖晃，船上有些人暈船了。
from A to Z: My grandmother knows everything about cooking from A to Z, so I always ask her for help in the kitchen.
我奶奶對烹飪從頭到尾什麼都知道，所以我在廚房裡總是向她求助。
a week from today: The big test is a week from today, so we should start to study for it right now.
大考在一週後的今天，所以我們現在就應該開始準備了。
from scratch: My aunt baked the birthday cake from scratch instead of buying one, and it tasted really great.
我阿姨從零開始親手烤生日蛋糕，而不是買現成的，而且吃起來真的很棒。
from the heart: Her thank-you letter was written from the heart, and the teacher almost cried when she read it.
她的感謝信是發自內心寫的，老師讀的時候幾乎哭了出來。
from what I hear: From what I hear, the new restaurant near our school is cheap, and the noodles there are very good.
就我聽到的，我們學校附近的新餐廳很便宜，而且那裡的麵很好吃。
make a living from: Mr. Lin makes a living from selling fruit at the night market, and he works six days a week.
林先生靠在夜市賣水果謀生，他一週工作六天。
be away from home: When I was away from home at summer camp, I missed my mother's cooking very much every day.
我在夏令營離家在外時，每天都非常想念媽媽做的菜。
be tired from running: The students were tired from running around the track, so they sat down under a tree to rest.
學生們因在跑道上跑步而疲累，所以他們坐在樹下休息。
recover from a cold: It took my little brother a whole week to recover from a cold, so he missed many classes.
我弟弟花了整整一週才感冒痊癒，所以他缺了很多課。
order a book from the store: I ordered a book from the store last Monday, but it still has not arrived at my house.
我上週一向書店訂了一本書，但它還沒送到我家。
choose from the list: You can choose any two dishes from the list on the menu, and the soup is free today.
你可以從菜單的清單中選任兩道菜，而且今天湯是免費的。
from memory: Jason can say the names of all fifty states of America from memory, which surprises everyone in his class.
傑森能憑記憶說出美國五十個州的名字，這讓他班上的每個人都很驚訝。
be made from (看不出原料) vs. be made of (看得出: Cheese is made from milk, but this table is made of wood, so you can still see the wood.
起司由牛奶製成（看不出原料），但這張桌子是木製的（看得出原料），所以你還看得到木頭。
wine is made from grapes: Wine is made from grapes, and my uncle grows many grapes on his farm in the mountains every year.
酒由葡萄製成，而我叔叔每年在山上的農場種很多葡萄。
the desk is made of wood: The desk in my room is made of wood from an old tree, so it is heavy and hard to move.
我房間裡的桌子是用一棵老樹的木頭製成的，所以它很重，很難搬動。
from (起點) vs. since (持續至今): Our school library is open from eight to five every day, and it has been open since 1990.
我們學校的圖書館每天從八點開到五點，而且它從一九九〇年起（持續到現在）就開放了。
from 9 to 5: My father works in an office from 9 to 5, and he usually gets home at about six thirty.
我爸爸在辦公室從九點工作到五點，他通常大約六點半到家。
since 9 o'clock: Since 9 o'clock this morning, we have waited for the bus from Taipei, but it still has not come.
從今天早上九點起（至今），我們一直在等從台北來的公車，但它還沒來。
be tired from (因…而累) vs. be tired of (厭倦: I am tired from walking all day, but I am never tired of taking pictures of beautiful places.
我因走了一整天而疲累，但我從不厭倦拍美麗景點的照片。
die from (外因) vs. die of (疾病): The old man died of a heart problem last year, but his neighbor died from a car accident this spring.
這位老先生去年死於心臟疾病，但他的鄰居今年春天死於車禍這個外因。
be different from (非 than): Your answer is different from mine, so let us check the book to find out who is right.
你的答案與我的不同，所以我們來查書看看誰是對的。
hear from (收到來信) vs. hear of (聽說): I have heard of that famous singer, but I have never heard from him after I wrote the letter.
我聽說過那位有名的歌手，但我寫信之後從未收到他的消息。
borrow from vs. lend to: I borrowed a pen from Mary this morning, and she also lent two hundred dollars to my brother.
我今天早上向瑪麗借了一枝筆，她也借給我哥哥兩百元。
be far from (離…遠) vs. far away: Our school is far from the train station, so the students who live far away take the bus.
我們學校離火車站很遠，所以住在遙遠地方的學生搭公車上學。
in the morning: My father goes jogging in the park in the morning before he drives to his office in the city.
我爸爸在早上去公園慢跑，然後才開車去市區的辦公室。
in the afternoon: We usually play basketball in the afternoon after school, and then we buy cold drinks at the store nearby.
我們通常在下午放學後打籃球，然後到附近的商店買冷飲。
in the evening: My family likes to take a walk by the river in the evening because the air is cool and fresh.
我家人喜歡在傍晚到河邊散步，因為空氣涼爽又新鮮。
in May: Mother's Day is in May, so my sister and I are planning a special dinner for Mom this year.
母親節在五月，所以我和姊姊今年正在計畫為媽媽準備一頓特別的晚餐。
in 2026: My cousin is going to finish college in 2026, and then she wants to find a job in Japan.
我表姊將在 2026 年大學畢業，然後她想在日本找工作。
in spring: Many people visit the mountains in spring because the flowers are beautiful and the weather is warm.
很多人在春天去山上，因為花很美而且天氣溫暖。
in the 1990s: My parents met each other in the 1990s when they were both students at the same college in Taichung.
我父母在一九九〇年代相遇，當時他們都是台中同一所大學的學生。
in the past: In the past, people wrote letters to their friends, but now most of us just send messages on our phones.
在過去，人們寫信給朋友，但現在我們大多數人只用手機傳訊息。
in the future: Amy hopes to be a doctor in the future, so she studies science very hard every day after school.
艾咪希望在未來成為醫生，所以她每天放學後都很用功讀自然科學。
in a minute: Please wait for me at the door, and I will be ready in a minute after I find my keys.
請在門口等我，我找到鑰匙後一分鐘內就會準備好。
in two days: The box from Japan will arrive in two days, so my brother checks the mail every afternoon.
從日本寄來的箱子兩天後會到，所以我哥哥每天下午都去查看郵件。
in an hour: The movie starts in an hour, so we have enough time to eat some noodles first.
電影一小時後開始，所以我們有足夠的時間先吃點麵。
in time: Thanks to the kind taxi driver, we got to the airport in time and did not miss our plane.
多虧了那位好心的計程車司機，我們及時趕到機場，沒有錯過飛機。
in the end: The two friends argued for a long time, but in the end they said sorry to each other.
這兩個朋友爭吵了很久，但最後他們互相道歉了。
in the beginning: In the beginning, I did not like my new school, but now I have many good friends here.
起初我不喜歡我的新學校，但現在我在這裡有很多好朋友。
in no time: The pizza was so delicious that the hungry boys finished the whole thing in no time.
披薩太好吃了，飢餓的男孩們立刻就把整個吃完了。
in a week: The summer vacation will begin in a week, and we are going to the beach in Kenting with my cousins.
暑假一週後開始，我們要和表兄弟姊妹一起去墾丁的海邊。
in the middle of the night: The baby cried in the middle of the night, so my parents did not get much sleep at all.
寶寶在半夜哭了，所以我爸媽幾乎沒睡多少。
in the daytime: My uncle works at night and sleeps in the daytime, so we must be quiet at home when he rests.
我叔叔晚上工作、白天睡覺，所以他休息時我們在家必須保持安靜。
in those days: In those days, my grandmother did not have a phone, so she wrote letters to her friends who lived far away.
在那些日子裡，我奶奶沒有電話，所以她寫信給住在遠方的朋友。
in the room: There are twenty desks in the room, and a big map of Taiwan hangs on the wall near the door.
房間裡有二十張桌子，門邊的牆上掛著一張很大的台灣地圖。
in the box: The little girl found two old photos in the box and gave them to her mother for her birthday.
小女孩在盒子裡找到兩張舊照片，並把它們送給媽媽當生日禮物。
in Taipei: My aunt lives in Taipei, so we often take the train to visit her during the summer holidays.
我阿姨住在台北，所以我們常在暑假搭火車去看她。
in the sky: After the rain stopped, we saw a beautiful rainbow in the sky above the tall buildings downtown.
雨停之後，我們看見市中心高樓上方的天空中有一道美麗的彩虹。
in the picture: The boy in the picture is my father when he was ten years old and lived in Tainan.
圖片中的男孩是我爸爸十歲住在台南時的樣子。
in the newspaper: My grandfather read in the newspaper that a new park will open near our house next month.
我爺爺在報紙上讀到，下個月我們家附近會有一座新公園開放。
in the street: Children should not play ball in the street because many cars and scooters drive by very fast.
小孩不應該在街上玩球，因為很多汽車和機車開得很快經過。
in the corner: My cat likes to sleep in the corner of the living room where the warm sun shines in.
我的貓喜歡睡在客廳有溫暖陽光照進來的角落。
in bed: Mike stayed in bed all day on Sunday because he had a fever and a bad headache.
麥克星期天整天都躺在床上，因為他發燒而且頭很痛。
in line: We stood in line for thirty minutes to buy the famous milk tea near the night market.
我們排隊三十分鐘，為了買夜市附近有名的奶茶。
in the middle of the road: A big dog was lying in the middle of the road, so the bus driver had to stop quickly.
一隻大狗躺在路中間，所以公車司機必須快速停車。
in the front row: I always sit in the front row in math class because I cannot see the board clearly from the back.
我數學課總是坐在前排，因為我從後面看不清楚黑板。
in the back of the car: My little sister fell asleep in the back of the car on our long trip to Kaohsiung last weekend.
上週末我們長途開車去高雄時，我妹妹在車後座睡著了。
in the tree: Look at the two birds in the tree, because they are building a small home for their babies.
看看樹上的那兩隻鳥，它們正在為寶寶築一個小家。
in the rain: The boys kept playing soccer in the rain, so their clothes were wet and dirty when they got home.
男孩們在雨中繼續踢足球，所以他們回家時衣服又濕又髒。
in the sun: Do not leave the chocolate in the sun, or it will become like water and make your bag dirty.
不要把巧克力放在陽光下，否則它會融得像水一樣，把你的包包弄髒。
in the dark: I could not find my phone, so I walked around in the dark and hit my foot on the chair.
我找不到手機，所以我在黑暗中走來走去，腳撞到了椅子。
in the water: The children played happily in the water at the beach while their parents sat under a big umbrella.
孩子們在海邊的水裡開心地玩，他們的父母則坐在大傘下。
in the kitchen: Mom is cooking dinner in the kitchen, and the smell of the chicken soup makes me very hungry.
媽媽正在廚房煮晚餐，雞湯的香味讓我好餓。
in hospital: My grandfather has been in hospital for two weeks, so we visit him every day after school.
我爺爺已經住院兩個星期了，所以我們每天放學後都去看他。
in English: Our teacher asks us to speak only in English during class, so we can practice it more.
我們老師要求我們上課時只用英文說話，這樣我們才能多練習。
in a loud voice: The coach spoke in a loud voice so that every player on the field could hear him clearly.
教練大聲地說話，好讓場上的每位球員都能清楚聽見他。
in pencil: Please write your answers in pencil, so you can easily change them if you make a mistake.
請用鉛筆寫答案，這樣如果寫錯了，你可以輕鬆地修改。
in ink: The teacher told us to write the test in ink, because answers in pencil are hard to read.
老師告訴我們考試要用墨水筆寫，因為用鉛筆寫的答案很難看清楚。
in cash: The small shop does not take credit cards, so you have to pay for the food in cash.
這家小店不收信用卡，所以你必須用現金付餐費。
in red: The girl in red is my best friend Lily, and she dances better than anyone else in our class.
穿紅色的那個女孩是我最好的朋友莉莉，她跳舞比我們班上任何人都好。
in a hurry: Sam was in a hurry this morning, so he left his lunch box on the kitchen table at home.
山姆今天早上匆忙地出門，所以他把便當盒留在家裡的廚房桌上。
in trouble: Jack is in trouble again because he forgot to do his homework for the third time this week.
傑克又有麻煩了，因為他這週第三次忘了做作業。
in danger: The police ran into the burning building to save the people who were in danger from the fire.
警察衝進著火的大樓，去救那些處於火災危險中的人。
in love with: My older sister is in love with a boy from her class, and she talks about him all day long.
我姊姊愛上了她班上的一個男孩，她整天都在談他。
in fact: Many people think my brother is shy, but in fact he loves to sing in front of a big crowd.
很多人以為我哥哥很害羞，但事實上他很愛在一大群人面前唱歌。
in person: I have talked to my friend in Japan on the Internet for two years, but I have never met him in person.
我和在日本的朋友在網路上聊了兩年，但我從未親自見過他。
in public: It is not polite to talk loudly on the phone in public, especially on the bus or the MRT.
在公開場合大聲講電話很不禮貌，尤其是在公車或捷運上。
in private: The teacher asked to talk with Lisa in private after class because she wanted to help her with a problem.
老師下課後要求私下和麗莎談談，因為她想幫她解決一個問題。
in secret: My brother and I planned a party for Mom in secret, and she was really surprised on Sunday night.
我和哥哥祕密地為媽媽計畫了一場派對，星期天晚上她真的非常驚喜。
in other words: Tom said he was busy this weekend, or in other words, he did not want to go shopping with us.
湯姆說他這週末很忙，換句話說，他不想和我們一起去逛街。
in short: The food was cold, the waiter was rude, and the music was too loud, so in short, the restaurant was terrible.
食物是冷的、服務生很粗魯、音樂又太大聲，簡言之，這家餐廳糟透了。
in general: In general, students in Taiwan study very hard, but they also need some time to play and rest.
一般而言，台灣的學生很用功，但他們也需要一些時間玩樂和休息。
in total: We bought three hamburgers and two drinks at the shop, and they cost two hundred dollars in total.
我們在店裡買了三個漢堡和兩杯飲料，總計花了兩百元。
in half: Mom cut the big apple in half and gave one piece to me and the other to my sister.
媽媽把大蘋果切成兩半，一半給我，另一半給我妹妹。
in pieces: The glass fell off the table and broke in pieces, so please be careful where you walk.
玻璃杯從桌上掉下來摔成碎片，所以請小心走路的地方。
in a row: Our basketball team has won five games in a row, so everyone at school is excited about the final game.
我們的籃球隊已經連續贏了五場比賽，所以學校裡每個人都對決賽感到興奮。
in order: Please put these books in order on the shelf, from the biggest one down to the smallest one.
請把這些書井然有序地放到書架上，從最大的排到最小的。
in a way: In a way, failing the test was good for me because I started to study much harder after that.
在某方面，考試不及格對我是好事，因為從那之後我開始更努力讀書。
in this way: You can write new words on cards and read them every day, and in this way you will remember them.
你可以把新單字寫在卡片上每天讀，用這種方法你就會記住它們。
in the same way: My sister and I were taught in the same way, but we have very different ideas about life now.
我和姊姊是以同樣的方式被教導長大，但我們現在對人生的想法非常不同。
in return: Mrs. Wang often helps us with our homework, and in return we help her carry heavy bags from the market.
王太太常幫我們做功課，作為回報，我們幫她從市場提重袋子回來。
in case: Take an umbrella with you in case it rains this afternoon, because the sky looks very gray now.
帶把雨傘以防萬一下午下雨，因為現在天空看起來很灰暗。
in case of fire: In case of fire, do not run or push, and leave the building by the stairs as quickly as you can.
如果發生火災，不要奔跑或推擠，要盡快走樓梯離開大樓。
in charge of: Linda is in charge of the class library, so you should ask her if you want to borrow a book.
琳達負責班級圖書館，所以如果你想借書，應該去問她。
in common: Although Jim and I come from different countries, we have a lot in common, like our love for soccer.
雖然吉姆和我來自不同的國家，我們有很多共同點，例如我們都愛足球。
in need: Every winter, our class collects warm clothes and gives them to families in need in our small town.
每年冬天，我們班會收集保暖的衣服，送給我們小鎮上有需要的家庭。
in peace: After a long and busy week, Dad just wants to read his newspaper in peace on Sunday morning.
經過漫長又忙碌的一週，爸爸只想在星期天早上平靜地看報紙。
in surprise: When Mary opened the door and saw all her friends, she shouted in surprise and began to laugh.
當瑪麗打開門看到所有朋友時，她驚訝地大叫，然後開始笑了起來。
in silence: The students sat in silence and listened carefully while the teacher read the sad story to them.
學生們沉默地坐著仔細聽，老師則把那個悲傷的故事讀給他們聽。
in tears: The little boy was in tears because he lost his favorite toy on the way to school this morning.
小男孩流著淚，因為他今天早上在上學的路上弄丟了最喜歡的玩具。
in shape: My uncle runs five kilometers every morning to stay in shape, and he looks much younger than his age.
我叔叔每天早上跑五公里來保持身體狀況好，他看起來比實際年齡年輕很多。
in good health: My grandmother is ninety years old, but she is still in good health and cooks for the whole family.
我奶奶九十歲了，但她仍然很健康，而且為全家人煮飯。
in the name of: Our teacher gave a gift to the hospital in the name of the whole class, and the nurses thanked us.
我們老師以全班之名送了一份禮物給醫院，護士們向我們道謝。
in search of: The hungry cat walked around the night market in search of food and finally found some fish.
那隻飢餓的貓在夜市裡走來走去尋找食物，最後找到了一些魚。
in place of: Ms. Chen will teach our English class today in place of Mr. Lee, who is sick at home.
陳老師今天會代替在家生病的李老師來教我們的英文課。
in spite of: In spite of the heavy rain, hundreds of people came to the park to watch the big night show.
儘管下著大雨，還是有數百人來公園看這場盛大的夜間表演。
in front of: There is a tall tree in front of my house, and the birds sing in it every morning.
我家前面有一棵高高的樹，鳥兒每天早上都在樹上唱歌。
in the way: Please move your bike because it is in the way, and the old man cannot get through the door.
請把你的腳踏車移開，因為它擋路了，老先生沒辦法通過這扇門。
in style: My aunt always dresses in style, and people often ask her where she buys her beautiful clothes.
我阿姨總是穿得很時髦，人們常問她在哪裡買這些漂亮的衣服。
in fashion: Short hair is in fashion this year, so many girls in my class got a new haircut last week.
短髮今年很流行，所以我們班上很多女生上週都剪了新髮型。
in the air: After the ball game, the excited fans threw their hats in the air and shouted for joy.
球賽結束後，興奮的球迷把帽子丟到空中，開心地大喊。
in all: There were twelve students in all at the party, and each of them brought some food to share.
派對上總共有十二個學生，每個人都帶了一些食物來分享。
in part: The team lost the game in part because their best player hurt his leg in the first ten minutes.
這支隊伍輸了比賽，部分原因是他們最好的球員在前十分鐘就傷了腿。
in doubt: If you are in doubt about the answer, raise your hand and ask the teacher for help right away.
如果你對答案有疑問，就舉手馬上請老師幫忙。
in question: The student in question was not at school on the day the money was lost, so he is not the one.
討論中的那位學生在錢弄丟的那天不在學校，所以他不是那個人。
in turn: The teacher asked each student in turn to read one sentence aloud from the story in the book.
老師要求每位學生依次大聲朗讀書中故事的一個句子。
in use: The computer room is in use right now, so we have to wait until the next class ends.
電腦教室現在正在使用中，所以我們必須等到下一節課結束。
in size: These two shirts are the same in size, but the blue one is much cheaper than the red one.
這兩件襯衫在尺寸上一樣，但藍色那件比紅色那件便宜很多。
in color: The sky changed in color from blue to orange as the sun went down behind the mountains.
太陽在山後落下時，天空的顏色從藍色變成橘色。
in number: The birds in our park are growing in number because many people feed them every day.
我們公園裡的鳥在數量上越來越多，因為很多人每天餵它們。
in price: Fruit and vegetables have gone up in price this month, so my mother buys less at the market.
這個月水果和蔬菜的價格上漲了，所以我媽媽在市場買得比較少。
in one's twenties: My English teacher is in her twenties, and she likes to play basketball with us after school.
我的英文老師二十多歲，她喜歡放學後和我們一起打籃球。
in the middle of doing: I was in the middle of doing my homework when my friend called and asked me to play a game.
我正在做作業時，朋友打電話來叫我去玩遊戲。
in a word: The trip to Japan was fun, the food was great, and the people were kind, so in a word, it was wonderful.
日本之旅很好玩、食物很棒、人們很親切，總而言之，這趟旅行太美好了。
in the long run: Eating vegetables every day may seem boring, but it is good for your health in the long run.
每天吃蔬菜也許看起來很無趣，但長遠來看對你的健康有好處。
in the wrong: Jack was in the wrong when he hit his little brother, so he had to say sorry to him.
傑克打他弟弟是有錯的，所以他必須向弟弟道歉。
in the right: Even though everyone laughed at her idea, Lucy knew she was in the right and did not give up.
即使大家都笑她的想法，露西知道自己有理，所以沒有放棄。
in one's shoes: If I were in your shoes, I would tell the teacher the truth about the broken window right now.
如果我處於你的立場，我會馬上告訴老師打破窗戶的實情。
in a sense: In a sense, my dog is my best friend because he is always happy to see me after school.
在某種意義上，我的狗是我最好的朋友，因為他放學後總是很開心見到我。
in time for dinner: Dad promised to finish his work early and get home in time for dinner on my birthday this year.
爸爸答應今年我生日那天要早點完成工作，及時趕回家吃晚餐。
in bad weather: Planes cannot take off in bad weather, so many people had to wait at the airport for hours.
壞天氣時飛機無法起飛，所以很多人必須在機場等好幾個小時。
in the open: The farmers sell their fresh vegetables in the open near the train station every Saturday morning.
農夫們每週六早上在火車站附近的戶外賣新鮮蔬菜。
be in: Mom is not in at the moment, so please call again after six o'clock this evening, Mr. Brown.
布朗先生，媽媽現在不在家，所以請今天傍晚六點以後再打來。
in and out: The nurse was in and out of the room all night to check on the sick old man.
護士整晚在房間進進出出，查看那位生病的老先生。
in the first place: You should not have taken your brother's bike without asking in the first place, so do not be angry now.
你一開始就不應該沒問就拿走哥哥的腳踏車，所以現在不要生氣。
in no way: The broken cup was in no way your fault, so please do not cry about it anymore, Lily.
莉莉，打破杯子絕不是你的錯，所以請不要再為這件事哭了。
in the hope of: Jenny studies English two hours every night in the hope of getting a good grade on the big test.
珍妮每晚讀兩小時英文，希望在大考中拿到好成績。
in the eyes of: In the eyes of my little brother, our father is the strongest and smartest man in the whole world.
在我弟弟眼中，我們的爸爸是全世界最強壯、最聰明的人。
in the face of: The young doctor stayed calm in the face of danger and helped everyone get out of the burning house.
年輕的醫生面對危險時保持冷靜，幫助每個人逃出著火的房子。
in answer to: In answer to your question, the library closes at nine on weekdays and at five on the weekend.
回答你的問題，圖書館平日九點關門，週末五點關門。
in reply to: I wrote a long email in reply to my friend's letter, and I told him about my school life.
我寫了一封長長的電子郵件回覆朋友的信，告訴他我的學校生活。
in favor of: Most students are in favor of a longer lunch break, but the teachers do not agree with them.
大多數學生贊成午休時間長一點，但老師們不同意。
in the habit of: My grandfather is in the habit of taking a walk after dinner, so he is still strong and healthy.
我爺爺有晚餐後散步的習慣，所以他仍然強壯又健康。
in memory of: The town built a small park in memory of the kind doctor who helped poor people for fifty years.
這個小鎮建了一座小公園，紀念那位幫助窮人五十年的好心醫生。
in the hands of: The future of the team is in the hands of the new coach, and everyone hopes he will do well.
球隊的未來由新教練掌控，每個人都希望他能做得好。
in the open air: We had our lunch in the open air by the lake, and the fresh wind made the food taste better.
我們在湖邊的戶外吃午餐，新鮮的風讓食物更好吃。
in the distance: From the top of the mountain, we could see the lights of the city in the distance at night.
從山頂上，我們可以在夜裡看見遠處城市的燈光。
in a group: The students worked in a group of five to make a report about how to save water at school.
學生們五人成群，一起製作一份關於如何在學校省水的報告。
in pairs: The teacher asked us to practice the new sentences in pairs, so I read them with my best friend.
老師要我們成對練習新句子，所以我和最好的朋友一起讀。
in line with: The new school rules are in line with what most parents want, so few people said no to them.
新的校規與大多數家長的期望一致，所以很少有人反對。
in order to: Kevin gets up at five every morning in order to practice the piano before he goes to school.
凱文每天早上五點起床，為了在上學前練鋼琴。
in that case: If it rains tomorrow, we cannot have a picnic, and in that case we will watch a movie at home.
如果明天下雨，我們就不能去野餐，那樣的話我們就在家看電影。
in business: The old bookstore near our school has been in business for over forty years, and my father shopped there as a boy.
我們學校附近的老書店已經營業超過四十年了，我爸爸小時候就在那裡買過書。
in (大範圍) / on (表面) / at (點): My cousin lives in Taichung, his house is on Park Road, and we will meet at the bus stop.
我表哥住在台中（範圍內），他家在公園路上（表面），我們會在公車站（點）見面。
in the tree (外來物) vs. on the tree (長出來的): A small bird is sitting in the tree, and there are many red apples on the tree too.
一隻小鳥停在樹上（外來物），而樹上也長了很多紅蘋果。
in the street (英) vs. on the street (美): My English friend says the kids are playing in the street, but my American friend says on the street.
我的英國朋友說孩子們在街上玩是 in the street，但我的美國朋友說是 on the street。
in the corner (室內) vs. at the corner (街角: The piano stands in the corner of our living room, and the bus stop is at the corner of the street.
鋼琴放在我們客廳的角落，而公車站在街角。
in the car vs. on the bus: My dad was waiting in the car, while my sister was still on the bus coming home from school.
我爸爸在車裡等著，而我妹妹還在放學回家的公車上。
in bed (睡) vs. on the bed (坐): Grandpa is sleeping in bed now, but the cat is just sitting on the bed and watching him quietly.
爺爺現在正在床上睡覺，但貓只是坐在床上安靜地看著他。
in the picture (圖中) vs. on the wall (牆上): The girl in the picture on the wall is my mother when she was a student in high school.
牆上那幅畫中的女孩是我媽媽讀高中時的樣子。
in time (及時) vs. on time (準時): Lily arrived at the station in time for the eight o'clock train, which left on time as usual.
莉莉及時趕到車站搭八點的火車，火車一如往常準時開走。
in the end (最後) vs. at the end of (在…末端): At the end of the movie, the little dog got lost, but in the end it found its way home.
在電影的結尾，小狗走失了，但最後它找到了回家的路。
in the morning vs. on Monday morning: I usually sleep late in the morning on weekends, but on Monday morning I have to get up at six.
我週末早上通常睡到很晚，但週一早上我必須六點起床。
in May vs. on May 5: My birthday is in May, and this year we are having a big party on May 5 at my house.
我的生日在五月，今年我們五月五日要在我家辦一場大派對。
in the way (擋路) vs. on the way (路上): A big truck was in the way, so we were late on the way to the train station this morning.
一輛大卡車擋路了，所以我們今天早上在去火車站的路上遲到了。
in the front of (內部前方) vs. in front of (: Our teacher stands in the front of the room, and a tall tree grows in front of the school gate.
我們老師站在教室內部的前方，而一棵高大的樹長在校門前方。
in hospital (住院) vs. in the hospital (在醫: My uncle is in hospital because he is sick, but my aunt is in the hospital because she works there as a nurse.
我叔叔因為生病而住院，但我阿姨在醫院裡是因為她在那裡當護士。
in school (就學) vs. at school (在學校): My sister is still in school, so she is at school from eight to four every weekday.
我姊姊還在就學中，所以她每個平日從八點到四點都在學校。
in the sky vs. in space: We can see the moon in the sky at night, and one day I hope to travel in space.
我們晚上可以在天空中看見月亮，而有一天我希望能在太空中旅行。
in the sun (曬太陽) vs. under the sun (天底下): The kids lay in the sun on the beach, and Grandma said it was the best place under the sun.
孩子們躺在海邊的陽光下，奶奶說這是天底下最棒的地方。
be interested in (非 about): My brother is interested in science, so he reads books about space and the stars every weekend.
我哥哥對自然科學有興趣，所以他每個週末都讀關於太空和星星的書。
be good at (非 in): Amy is good at drawing and is also interested in music, so she wants to join the art club.
艾咪擅長畫畫，也對音樂有興趣，所以她想加入美術社。
arrive in (大地方) vs. arrive at (小地方): After a long train ride, we finally arrived in Tainan at noon and then arrived at the hotel by taxi.
坐了很久的火車後，我們終於在中午到達台南這座大城市，然後搭計程車到達旅館這個小地點。
in two weeks (兩週後) vs. for two weeks (兩週: My cousin will come back from Japan in two weeks, so we are planning a big welcome dinner for him.
我表哥兩週後會從日本回來，所以我們正在為他計畫一場盛大的歡迎晚餐。
in cash vs. by credit card: The small shop near my school does not take cards, so my mother always pays in cash there.
我學校附近那家小店不收卡，所以我媽媽在那裡總是用現金付錢。
in pencil vs. with a pencil: Our teacher asks us to write the answers in pencil first, so we can fix our mistakes easily later.
我們老師要我們先用鉛筆寫答案，這樣之後才能輕鬆改正錯誤。
in English vs. by English (錯誤): The tour guide explained everything in English, and the students from Korea understood most of what she said.
導遊用英文解釋所有事情，而來自韓國的學生大部分都聽懂了她說的話。
in the rain (淋雨) vs. under the rain (錯誤): Peter forgot his umbrella and walked home in the rain, so his shirt and shoes were all wet.
彼得忘了帶傘，在雨中走回家，所以他的襯衫和鞋子全都溼了。
in the morning vs. at night: My grandfather goes for a walk in the morning, but he likes to read the newspaper quietly at night.
我爺爺在早上去散步，但他喜歡在晚上安靜地看報紙。
inside the box: When Mary opened the gift, she found a cute little bear inside the box and smiled happily.
瑪麗打開禮物時，發現盒子裡面有一隻可愛的小熊，開心地笑了。
inside the house: It was so hot outside that everyone stayed inside the house and watched a movie all afternoon.
外面太熱了，所以每個人整個下午都待在屋內看電影。
stay inside: The weather report says a typhoon is coming tonight, so please stay inside and keep the windows closed.
氣象報告說今晚颱風要來，所以請待在室內並把窗戶關好。
look inside: Before you buy the used bag, look inside carefully to make sure there are no holes or broken parts.
買那個二手包包之前，仔細看裡面，確定沒有破洞或壞掉的地方。
inside the car: Do not leave your dog inside the car on a sunny day, because it gets very hot very quickly.
晴天時不要把狗留在車內，因為車裡很快就會變得非常熱。
go inside: It started to rain hard during the picnic, so we picked up our food and went inside the house.
野餐時開始下大雨，所以我們收起食物，進去屋子裡面。
inside out: Jenny was in such a hurry this morning that she wore her sweater inside out to school.
珍妮今天早上太趕了，結果把毛衣裡外翻轉穿到學校去。
from the inside: The door of the old house can only be opened from the inside, so someone has to let you in.
這間老房子的門只能從內部打開，所以得有人讓你進去。
inside of an hour: If we take the MRT instead of the bus, we can get to the night market inside of an hour.
如果我們搭捷運而不是公車，一小時之內就能到夜市。
inside information: My brother says he has inside information about the test, but I think he is just joking with me.
我哥哥說他有關於考試的內部消息，但我覺得他只是在跟我開玩笑。
know sth. inside out: Our basketball coach knows every player inside out, so he always knows who should play in the last minute.
我們的籃球教練對每位球員都瞭若指掌，所以他總是知道最後一分鐘該讓誰上場。
on the inside: The cake looks plain on the outside, but on the inside it is very sweet and full of fresh fruit.
這個蛋糕外表看起來很普通，但裡面非常甜，而且滿滿都是新鮮水果。
inside a week: The doctor told my grandmother that her leg would feel much better inside a week if she rested.
醫生告訴我奶奶，如果她好好休息，一週之內腿就會好很多。
turn the shirt inside out: Mom asked me to turn the shirt inside out before washing it, so the colors would stay bright.
媽媽要我洗襯衫之前先把襯衫翻面，這樣顏色才會保持鮮亮。
inside and outside: The workers painted the school inside and outside during the summer, so it looks very new and clean this year.
工人暑假期間把學校內外都重新油漆，所以今年看起來非常新又乾淨。
deep inside: Tom said he did not care about the game, but deep inside he really wanted to win it.
湯姆說他不在乎這場比賽，但他內心深處其實很想贏。
walk into the room: When the teacher walked into the room, all the students stopped talking and quickly sat down in their seats.
當老師走進房間時，所有學生都停止說話，很快地坐回座位上。
jump into the pool: It was a very hot afternoon, so the children jumped into the pool one by one with happy shouts.
那是個很熱的下午，所以孩子們一個接一個開心地大叫著跳進游泳池。
put the book into the bag: Please put the book into the bag before you leave, or you will forget it again like last week.
離開前請把書放進包包，不然你會像上週一樣又忘了帶。
get into the car: Dad told us to get into the car quickly because we were already late for Grandma's birthday party.
爸爸叫我們快點上車，因為我們去奶奶的生日派對已經遲到了。
fall into the river: The little boy was running too fast on the bridge, and his new hat fell into the river.
那個小男孩在橋上跑得太快，他的新帽子掉進河裡了。
look into the box: Jack looked into the box and found some old photos of his parents when they were young.
傑克看盒子裡面，發現了一些他爸媽年輕時的舊照片。
run into the house: When it began to thunder, the frightened puppy ran into the house and hid under the kitchen table.
開始打雷時，受驚的小狗跑進屋裡，躲在廚房桌子底下。
turn into a frog: In the story, the prince turns into a frog after a bad old woman uses her magic on him.
在故事裡，一個壞老太婆對王子使用魔法，他就變成了青蛙。
change water into ice: If you put the bottle in the freezer for a few hours, the cold will change water into ice.
如果你把瓶子放進冷凍庫幾個小時，低溫會把水變成冰。
cut the cake into pieces: Mom cut the cake into pieces so that everyone at the party could have a sweet little bite.
媽媽把蛋糕切成小塊，好讓派對上的每個人都能吃一小口甜點。
divide into groups: Our teacher divided the class into groups of four, and each group had to give a short talk about Taiwan.
老師把全班分成四人一組的小組，每組都要做一段關於台灣的簡短報告。
grow into a man: The baby in this photo has grown into a tall man, and now he is a doctor in Taipei.
這張照片裡的寶寶已經長成高大的大人，現在是台北的一位醫生。
break into pieces: The glass fell off the table and broke into pieces, so be careful not to walk there without shoes.
玻璃杯從桌上掉下來碎成片，所以小心不要光著腳走過去。
make flour into bread: My grandmother showed me how to make flour into bread, and the whole kitchen smelled wonderful.
奶奶教我怎麼把麵粉做成麵包，整個廚房都香氣四溢。
get into trouble: If you keep forgetting your homework, you will get into trouble with the teacher sooner or later.
如果你一直忘記寫功課，遲早會跟老師惹上麻煩。
get into the habit of: Last year I got into the habit of reading English for ten minutes every night before going to bed.
去年我養成了每天晚上睡前讀十分鐘英文的習慣。
burst into tears: When the little girl could not find her mother at the market, she burst into tears right away.
小女孩在市場找不到媽媽時，馬上就突然大哭起來。
run into an old friend: Yesterday I ran into an old friend at the bookstore, and we talked for almost an hour about school days.
昨天我在書店偶然遇到一位老友，我們聊了快一個小時的學生時代。
look into the problem: The principal promised to look into the problem of the broken lights in the gym as soon as possible.
校長承諾會盡快調查體育館燈壞掉的問題。
be into music: My sister is really into music, so she spends most of her free time playing the piano and singing.
我姊姊很喜歡音樂，所以她大部分的空閒時間都在彈鋼琴和唱歌。
talk sb. into doing: Kevin did not want to join the club, but his friends finally talked him into joining the soccer team.
凱文本來不想加入社團，但他的朋友最後說服他加入了足球隊。
late into the night: The night before the big test, Lisa studied late into the night and felt very tired the next morning.
大考前一晚，麗莎讀書直到深夜，隔天早上覺得非常累。
far into the future: Nobody knows what life will be like far into the future, but we hope the earth will stay clean.
沒有人知道直到遙遠的未來生活會是什麼樣子，但我們希望地球能保持乾淨。
come into use: Cell phones came into use many years ago, and now almost everyone in Taiwan has one in their pocket.
手機在很多年前就開始被使用，現在台灣幾乎每個人口袋裡都有一支。
come into fashion: Short hair came into fashion last year, so many girls at my school cut their long hair off.
短髮去年開始流行，所以我們學校很多女生都把長髮剪掉了。
fall into bad habits: During the long summer vacation, some students fall into bad habits like sleeping late and playing games all day.
漫長的暑假期間，有些學生會養成壞習慣，像是睡到很晚、整天打電動。
get into college: Maggie studied very hard for three years, and finally she got into a good college in Taipei.
瑪姬非常努力地讀了三年書，最後進入台北一所好大學。
break into a house: Last night a thief tried to break into a house on our street, but the loud dog scared him away.
昨晚一個小偷想闖入我們這條街上的一戶住家，但大聲吠叫的狗把他嚇跑了。
two goes into eight four times: The math teacher explained that two goes into eight four times, and then she gave us a harder question.
數學老師解釋八除以二等於四，然後給了我們一道更難的題目。
in (靜態) vs. into (動態進入): The cat was sleeping in the basket, but when it heard the can open, it jumped into the kitchen.
那隻貓本來在籃子裡睡覺，但聽到罐頭打開的聲音，就跳進了廚房。
be in the room vs. walk into the room: My sister was already in the room doing her homework when I walked into the room with the pizza.
我拿著披薩走進房間時，我妹妹已經在房間裡寫功課了。
into (變成) vs. to (轉向): The weather turned cold suddenly, and the rain on the mountain turned into snow before we got to the top.
天氣突然變冷，我們到山頂前，山上的雨就變成了雪。
turn into (變成) vs. turn to (轉向): The sad little boy turned to his mother for help, and his tears soon turned into a big smile.
難過的小男孩轉向媽媽求助，他的眼淚很快就變成了大大的笑容。
get into the car vs. get on the bus: We got into the car to go to the beach, but our cousins decided to get on the bus instead.
我們上小車去海邊，但我們的表兄弟姊妹決定改搭公車。
look into (調查) vs. look at (看): The police did not just look at the broken window; they looked into the matter and found the thief.
警察不只是看那扇破窗；他們調查了這件事，並找到了小偷。
run into (偶遇) vs. run after (追): I ran into my old teacher at the park while I was running after my dog, and we laughed together.
我在公園追著我的狗跑時偶然遇到以前的老師，我們一起笑了出來。
look like your mother: Everyone says you look like your mother because you both have the same big eyes and sweet smile.
大家都說你長得像你媽媽，因為你們都有一樣的大眼睛和甜美的笑容。
sound like fun: A trip to the beach with hot dogs and swimming sounds like fun, so let's go this Saturday.
帶著熱狗去海邊游泳聽起來很有趣，所以我們這個星期六去吧。
taste like chicken: My brother tried frog legs for the first time in France and said they taste like chicken.
我哥哥在法國第一次吃青蛙腿，他說吃起來像雞肉。
smell like fish: The kitchen smelled like fish all afternoon because Grandpa cooked a big dinner for the whole family.
廚房整個下午都聞起來像魚，因為爺爺為全家煮了一頓豐盛的晚餐。
like this: Hold the baseball bat like this, with both hands close together, and then swing it slowly at the ball.
像這樣握棒球棒，雙手靠在一起，然後慢慢地朝球揮棒。
like that: Please do not talk to your grandmother like that; she only wants to help you with your homework.
請不要那樣跟奶奶說話；她只是想幫你寫功課。
something like that: I think the movie is about a boy who finds a lost dog, or something like that, but I am not sure.
我想這部電影是在講一個男孩找到一隻走失的狗，或類似那樣的情節，但我不確定。
a face like an angel: The baby in the picture has a face like an angel, and everyone who sees her wants to smile.
照片裡的寶寶有一張天使般的臉，每個看到她的人都想微笑。
run like the wind: When the bell rang for lunch, Jason ran like the wind to be the first one at the shop.
午餐鐘聲響起時，傑森跑得飛快，想成為第一個到商店的人。
work like a dog: My father works like a dog from Monday to Saturday, so on Sunday he just wants to rest at home.
我爸爸從星期一到星期六都像狗一樣辛苦工作，所以星期日他只想在家休息。
sleep like a baby: After the long hike up the mountain, I was so tired that I slept like a baby all night.
爬完那段漫長的山路後，我累到整晚睡得像寶寶一樣。
eat like a horse: My little brother eats like a horse after soccer practice, so Mom always cooks extra rice for him.
我弟弟足球練習後吃得很多，所以媽媽總是為他多煮一些飯。
like father, like son: Mr. Lin loves fishing, and his son spends every weekend by the river too; like father, like son.
林先生熱愛釣魚，他兒子也每個週末都待在河邊；真是有其父必有其子。
What is he like?: You said the new student sits next to you in class, so tell me, what is he like?
你說那個新同學在班上坐你旁邊，那告訴我，他是怎樣的人？
What does it look like?: I have never seen a dragon fruit before, so can you tell me what does it look like inside?
我以前從沒看過火龍果，所以你能告訴我它裡面看起來如何嗎？
What is the weather like?: Before we plan the picnic for Sunday, let's check the news and see what the weather is like.
我們計畫星期日的野餐之前，先看看新聞，瞭解一下天氣怎麼樣。
just like old times: The old friends sat in the same corner of the coffee shop, talking and laughing just like old times.
老朋友們坐在咖啡店同一個角落聊天說笑，就像以前一樣。
nothing like: Riding a real horse is nothing like riding the little horse at the park, and I was quite scared.
騎真的馬和騎公園裡的小馬一點也不像，我當時相當害怕。
and the like: The night market sells fried chicken, noodles, sweet drinks, and the like, so you will never go hungry there.
夜市賣炸雞、麵、甜飲料等等，所以你在那裡絕對不會餓到。
like crazy: When our team scored the last goal, the whole class jumped up and shouted like crazy in the gym.
我們隊踢進最後一球時，全班在體育館裡瘋狂地跳起來大叫。
The sky is getting dark and the wind is strong, so it looks like rain; bring your umbrella with you.
天空變暗、風也很強，看起來要下雨了；帶著你的傘吧。
feel like a cup of tea: After walking around the market for two hours, I feel like a cup of tea and a short rest.
在市場走了兩個小時後，我想喝杯茶，稍微休息一下。
feel like crying: When Amy saw her low score on the math test, she felt like crying, but her friend made her laugh.
艾咪看到數學考試的低分時想哭，但她的朋友讓她笑了出來。
like a dream: Our trip to Japan was like a dream, with beautiful snow, delicious food, and very kind people everywhere.
我們的日本之旅像夢一樣，有美麗的雪、美味的食物，到處都是非常親切的人。
more like: Dad said the walk would take ten minutes, but it was more like half an hour under the hot sun.
爸爸說這段路走十分鐘就到，但在大太陽底下其實更像是半個小時。
like (像) vs. as (身分): My aunt sings like a real singer at family parties, but she works as a nurse at the hospital.
我阿姨在家庭聚會上唱歌像真正的歌手一樣，但她的職業是醫院的護士。
like a teacher (像) vs. as a teacher (就是): Mr. Wang talks to us like a teacher, but he is not a teacher; he works as a doctor in town.
王先生跟我們說話像老師一樣，但他不是老師；他在鎮上當醫生。
What is he like? (個性) vs. What does he l: I know what your brother likes, such as basketball and ice cream, but what is he like as a person?
我知道你哥哥喜歡什麼，比如籃球和冰淇淋，但他本人是怎樣的人？
like (介係詞) vs. alike (形容詞): Judy looks like her younger sister, and when they wear the same dress, they really look alike.
茱蒂長得像她妹妹，當她們穿同樣的洋裝時，看起來真的很像。
The two brothers look alike, so many teachers at school still call them by the wrong names.
這兩兄弟看起來很像，所以學校裡很多老師仍然會叫錯他們的名字。
Everyone at the party said that little Ben looks like his dad, from his short nose to his big smile.
派對上每個人都說小班長得像爸爸，從短短的鼻子到大大的笑容都像。
such as vs. like: I enjoy sports like swimming and hiking, and my sister enjoys quiet games at home such as chess and cards.
我喜歡像游泳和健行這類運動，我姊姊則喜歡例如西洋棋和撲克牌等在家玩的安靜遊戲。
feel like + V-ing (想) vs. would like to: I feel like eating ice cream right now, so would you like to come to the shop with me?
我現在想吃冰淇淋，所以你想要跟我一起去那家店嗎？
like (喜歡, 動詞) vs. like (像, 介係詞): I like my new English teacher very much because she is friendly and talks to us like a good friend.
我很喜歡我的新英文老師，因為她很友善，而且跟我們說話像好朋友一樣。
be like (像) vs. be likely to (可能): My cousin is like a big sister to me, and she is likely to visit us again this winter vacation.
我表姊對我來說像個大姊姊，而且她這個寒假可能會再來拜訪我們。
near the station: There is a small bookstore near the station, and I often stop there to read before I take the train.
車站附近有一家小書店，我搭火車前常常停下來在那裡看書。
live near the school: Since we live near the school, my brother and I can walk there in five minutes every morning.
因為我們住在學校附近，我和哥哥每天早上五分鐘就能走到學校。
sit near the window: On the train to Taichung, I like to sit near the window so I can watch the green fields go by.
搭火車去台中時，我喜歡坐在窗邊附近，這樣就能看著綠色的田野飛過。
a park near here: Is there a park near here where we can play basketball after school and ride our bikes?
這附近有公園可以讓我們放學後打籃球和騎腳踏車嗎？
come near: Please do not come near the stove while I am cooking, because the hot oil can burn your hand.
我煮菜時請不要靠近爐子，因為熱油可能會燙傷你的手。
near the top: When we were near the top of the mountain, it got cold and windy, so we put on our jackets.
我們靠近山頂時，天氣變冷又颳風，所以我們穿上了外套。
nowhere near: My drawing is nowhere near as good as my sister's, but I still enjoy painting pictures on weekends.
我的畫遠遠不及我姊姊的好，但我週末還是很喜歡畫畫。
near the end of the book: Near the end of the book, the lost dog finally finds his way home, and the family cries with joy.
接近書的結尾時，走失的狗終於找到回家的路，全家人喜極而泣。
near the end of the year: Near the end of the year, many stores have big sales, so my mother buys new clothes for us then.
接近年底時，很多商店都有大特賣，所以我媽媽那時會幫我們買新衣服。
near Christmas: Near Christmas, the streets in our town are full of lights, and the shops play happy music all day.
接近聖誕節時，我們鎮上的街道滿是燈飾，商店整天播放歡樂的音樂。
the near future: The city plans to build a new MRT line in the near future, so going to school will be much easier.
市政府計畫在不久的將來蓋一條新的捷運線，這樣上學會方便很多。
near midnight: Jenny was still talking with her friends on the phone near midnight, so she was very sleepy in class today.
珍妮接近午夜時還在跟朋友講電話，所以她今天上課非常想睡。
draw near: As the final exams draw near, the library gets more crowded and the students become more and more nervous.
隨著期末考臨近，圖書館變得更擠，學生們也越來越緊張。
near the time: It was near the time for the school bus to leave, so Mark picked up his bag and ran to the gate.
校車快要開走的時間接近了，所以馬克拿起書包跑向校門。
near (接近, 無 to) vs. close to: The post office is near the bank, and the bakery is close to the bank too, so we can walk to both.
郵局靠近銀行，麵包店也靠近銀行，所以我們可以走路去這兩個地方。
near the school: We moved to an apartment near the school last month, so now I can sleep a little later every morning.
我們上個月搬到靠近學校的公寓，所以現在我每天早上可以多睡一點。
near (介係詞) vs. nearby (形／副): The restaurant near the station is always full, but there is a nearby shop that sells good noodles too.
車站附近的那家餐廳總是客滿，但附近也有一家店賣好吃的麵。
a nearby park: Every Sunday morning, Grandpa takes his little dog to a nearby park, and they walk slowly around the lake.
每個星期日早上，爺爺帶他的小狗去附近的公園，他們繞著湖慢慢散步。
near here: Excuse me, is there a bus stop near here, because I need to get to the hospital before noon?
不好意思，這附近有公車站牌嗎？因為我中午前得趕到醫院。
nearly: Alice nearly missed the train this morning because she spent too much time looking for her phone.
艾莉絲今天早上幾乎錯過火車，因為她花了太多時間找手機。
near vs. next to (緊鄰): The bank is near the library, but the bookstore is right next to it, so you cannot miss it.
銀行在圖書館附近，但書店就緊鄰著圖書館，所以你一定找得到。
a cup of tea: After dinner, my grandmother always makes herself a cup of tea and sits by the window to watch the moon.
晚餐後，奶奶總是幫自己泡一杯茶，坐在窗邊看月亮。
a piece of paper: The teacher gave each of us a piece of paper and asked us to write down three wishes for the new year.
老師給我們每個人一張紙，要我們寫下新年的三個願望。
a lot of friends: Since Peter is friendly and loves to help others, he has made a lot of friends at his new school.
因為彼得友善又樂於助人，他在新學校交了很多朋友。
a kind of fruit: A dragon fruit is a kind of fruit with pink skin, and it is very popular in Taiwan during the summer.
火龍果是一種外皮粉紅色的水果，夏天在台灣非常受歡迎。
a friend of mine: A friend of mine is coming to visit from Japan next week, so I will show her around the night market.
我的一個朋友下週要從日本來拜訪，所以我會帶她逛逛夜市。
the top of the hill: We walked for two hours to reach the top of the hill, and the view of the sea was wonderful.
我們走了兩個小時才到山頂，海景美得令人驚嘆。
the color of the sky: Just before the typhoon came, the color of the sky changed from blue to a strange dark gray.
颱風來臨前，天空的顏色從藍色變成奇怪的暗灰色。
the city of Taipei: The city of Taipei has many night markets, tall buildings, and a convenient MRT system for visitors to enjoy.
台北市有很多夜市、高樓，以及方便遊客使用的捷運系統。
a man of few words: My grandfather is a man of few words, but when he speaks, everyone in the family listens carefully.
我爺爺是個話不多的人，但當他開口時，全家人都會仔細聽。
die of cancer: Mr. Chen stopped smoking after his good friend died of cancer at the age of fifty last year.
陳先生在他的好朋友去年五十歲死於癌症後，就戒菸了。
be afraid of dogs: My little sister is afraid of dogs, so she always holds my hand when we walk past the pet shop.
我妹妹怕狗，所以我們走過寵物店時，她總是緊握我的手。
be proud of you: You practiced the piano every day for months, and now I am so proud of you for winning first place.
你好幾個月來每天練鋼琴，現在你得到第一名，我真為你驕傲。
be tired of waiting: We were tired of waiting for the late bus, so we decided to walk to the movie theater together.
我們厭倦等待遲來的公車，所以決定一起走路去電影院。
be sure of it: Sandy says she can finish the whole report tonight, and she seems quite sure of it.
珊蒂說她今晚能完成整份報告，而且她似乎對此很有把握。
be full of water: After the heavy rain last night, the small river behind our school was full of brown water this morning.
昨晚下大雨後，我們學校後面的小河今天早上裝滿了棕色的水。
think of a plan: We need to think of a plan for the class party, because it is only two weeks away now.
我們需要想到一個班級派對的計畫，因為現在距離派對只剩兩週了。
dream of flying: When I was a child, I often dreamed of flying over the city like a bird in the sky.
小時候，我常常夢想像天上的鳥一樣飛越城市。
hear of the news: Have you heard of the news about our school; the old library will become a new computer room next year.
你聽說過我們學校的消息了嗎？舊圖書館明年會變成新的電腦教室。
take care of: When my parents went to Japan for a week, my grandmother came to take care of my brother and me.
我爸媽去日本一週時，奶奶來照顧我和弟弟。
get rid of: It took me months to get rid of my bad habit of staying up late and playing phone games.
我花了好幾個月才擺脫熬夜打手機遊戲的壞習慣。
run out of: We ran out of milk this morning, so Dad went to the store on the corner to buy some before breakfast.
我們今天早上牛奶用完了，所以爸爸早餐前去街角的商店買了一些。
because of the rain: Because of the rain, the baseball game was put off, and the players went back home feeling very sad.
因為下雨，棒球比賽被延後了，球員們非常難過地回家。
instead of me: My brother is sick today, so could you please go to the store instead of me and buy some bread?
我哥哥今天生病了，所以可以請你代替我去商店買些麵包嗎？
out of order: The washing machine at home is out of order again, so Mom has to wash all our clothes by hand.
家裡的洗衣機又故障了，所以媽媽得用手洗我們所有的衣服。
out of date: This map is out of date, because many of the roads here have changed in the past ten years.
這張地圖已經過時了，因為這裡很多道路在過去十年都改變了。
out of work: Uncle Tom has been out of work since the factory closed, so he is looking for a new job now.
工廠關閉後湯姆叔叔就一直失業，所以他現在正在找新工作。
first of all: First of all, wash your hands before you touch any food, and then we can start making the cookies.
首先，碰任何食物之前先洗手，然後我們就可以開始做餅乾了。
most of all: I love the food and the beaches in Tainan, but most of all, I love the kind people there.
我喜歡台南的食物和海灘，但最重要的是，我喜歡那裡親切的人們。
of course: Of course you can borrow my umbrella; just remember to bring it back to school tomorrow morning.
當然你可以借我的傘；只要記得明天早上帶來學校還我就好。
all of a sudden: We were having a picnic in the park when, all of a sudden, it began to rain very hard.
我們正在公園野餐，突然開始下起大雨。
a waste of time: Watching TV for five hours every day is a waste of time, so why not read a good book instead?
每天看五小時電視是浪費時間，為什麼不改看一本好書呢？
a matter of time: Anna practices swimming every day after school, so it is only a matter of time before she wins a big race.
安娜每天放學後練習游泳，所以她贏得大型比賽只是時間問題。
the key to (非 of): Our coach often says the key to winning is working together, not the skill of one great player.
我們的教練常說獲勝的關鍵是一起合作，而不是某位厲害球員的技巧。
a photo of my family: I keep a photo of my family in my wallet, so I can look at it whenever I miss them.
我在皮夾裡放了一張我家人的照片，這樣想念他們時就能看一看。
the number of students: The number of students in our school has gone down this year, so two classes were put together.
我們學校今年學生的數量減少了，所以有兩個班被合併在一起。
a number of students: A number of students stayed after class to ask the teacher questions about the science homework for tomorrow.
許多學生下課後留下來問老師明天自然科作業的問題。
a bit of: This soup needs a bit of salt, so could you pass me the salt from the other side of the table?
這湯需要一點鹽，所以你能把桌子另一邊的鹽遞給我嗎？
a couple of days: My aunt will stay with us for a couple of days, and then she will fly back to America on Friday.
我阿姨會跟我們住幾天，然後星期五飛回美國。
a pair of shoes: I bought a new pair of shoes for the sports day, but they hurt my feet during the first race.
我為運動會買了一雙新鞋，但第一場賽跑時鞋子就磨痛了我的腳。
a glass of milk: Every morning before school, my mother gives me a glass of milk and an egg to keep me strong.
每天早上上學前，媽媽都給我一杯牛奶和一顆蛋，讓我保持強壯。
a bowl of rice: Grandma always puts a bowl of rice in front of me and tells me to eat more, even when I am full.
奶奶總是在我面前放一碗飯，叫我多吃點，就算我已經飽了也一樣。
a bottle of water: Remember to bring a bottle of water on the hike, because it will be very hot on the mountain.
記得健行時帶一瓶水，因為山上會非常熱。
a loaf of bread: Dad came home from the bakery with a loaf of bread, and we had warm toast with butter for breakfast.
爸爸從麵包店帶回一條麵包，我們早餐吃了塗奶油的熱吐司。
a slice of pizza: After the game, each player got a slice of pizza and a cold drink from the coach as a little gift.
比賽結束後，每位球員從教練那裡得到一片披薩和一杯冷飲作為小禮物。
a sheet of paper: Please take out a sheet of paper and write your name at the top before you start the test.
請拿出一張紙，在開始考試前先在最上面寫上你的名字。
a bar of chocolate: Linda shared a bar of chocolate with her friends at lunch, and everyone got two small sweet pieces.
琳達午餐時和朋友分享一條巧克力，每個人都拿到兩小塊甜甜的巧克力。
a box of apples: My uncle sent us a box of apples from his farm, so Mom made a big apple pie this weekend.
我叔叔從他的農場寄來一箱蘋果，所以媽媽這個週末做了一個大蘋果派。
It is kind of you to carry the heavy bags for the old lady while she walks up the stairs.
你真好心，在那位老太太上樓梯時幫她提沉重的袋子。
It is nice of you to stay after class and help me clean the room before the big meeting.
你真好，下課後留下來幫我在大會議之前打掃教室。
Two men robbed the old woman of her bag near the market, but the police caught them an hour later.
兩名男子在市場附近搶走老婦人的包包，但警察一小時後就抓到他們了。
remind me of my father: The tall man with the kind smile in the old photo reminds me of my father when he was young.
舊照片裡那位有著親切笑容的高個子男人讓我想起我父親年輕的時候。
a book of mine: I lent a book of mine to Jack last month, but he still has not given it back to me.
我上個月借了我的一本書給傑克，但他到現在還沒還我。
one of the best: This small noodle shop near the temple is one of the best places to eat in our town.
廟附近這家小麵店是我們鎮上最好的餐館之一。
some of them: Many students joined the school trip to the museum, but some of them had to stay home because they were sick.
很多學生參加了學校去博物館的旅行，但他們當中一些人因為生病得待在家。
none of us: None of us knew the answer to the last question, so the teacher explained it again on the board.
我們沒有人知道最後一題的答案，所以老師在黑板上再解釋了一次。
both of them: Both of them want to be the class leader, so the students will vote for one of them next Monday.
他們兩個都想當班長，所以學生們下週一會投票選出其中一人。
each of us: Before the trip, each of us had to bring a lunch box, a bottle of water, and a raincoat.
旅行前，我們每一個人都得帶便當盒、一瓶水和雨衣。
all of you: I want all of you to finish the reading by Friday, because we will have a short quiz on it.
我希望你們全部在星期五前讀完這篇文章，因為我們會針對它做一個小考。
half of the class: Half of the class went to the computer room, and the other half stayed to practice for the English speech.
半個班級去了電腦教室，另一半留下來為英文演講練習。
most of the time: My grandfather spends most of the time in his garden, planting flowers and talking to his old neighbors.
我爺爺大部分時間都待在花園裡，種花並跟老鄰居聊天。
the rest of the day: After we finished the housework, we spent the rest of the day at the beach swimming and eating ice cream.
做完家事後，我們把這天剩下的時間都花在海邊游泳和吃冰淇淋。
the end of the story: At the end of the story, the poor boy becomes a king, and everyone in the village is happy for him.
故事的結尾，那個窮男孩成了國王，村裡每個人都為他感到高興。
the beginning of May: At the beginning of May, the weather in Taiwan gets hot and wet, and the rainy season usually starts.
五月初，台灣的天氣變得又熱又溼，雨季通常就開始了。
a change of plan: There has been a change of plan; we will go to the zoo on Sunday instead of Saturday because of the rain.
計畫有變更；因為下雨，我們星期日去動物園，而不是星期六。
Everyone in the office speaks well of Miss Lee because she is helpful, honest, and always finishes her work on time.
辦公室裡每個人都稱讚李小姐，因為她樂於助人、誠實，而且總是準時完成工作。
make fun of: Some boys made fun of Tim because of his glasses, but the teacher told them to stop at once.
有些男生因為提姆戴眼鏡而取笑他，但老師叫他們立刻停止。
make use of: We should make use of the old boxes in the garage and turn them into a little house for the cat.
我們應該利用車庫裡的舊箱子，把它們做成貓的小屋。
make the most of: The sun is finally out after a week of rain, so let's make the most of it and ride our bikes.
下了一週的雨後太陽終於出來了，所以我們充分利用這好天氣去騎腳踏車吧。
make a fool of: Nobody likes it when someone makes a fool of them in front of the class, so please be kind to others.
沒有人喜歡在全班面前被人愚弄，所以請善待別人。
keep track of: My mother keeps track of everything she spends by writing it down in a small notebook every evening.
我媽媽每天晚上都把花的每一筆錢寫在小筆記本裡，以此記錄她的開銷。
lose track of time: We were playing video games at Ben's house and lost track of time, so we missed dinner at home.
我們在班的家裡打電動，玩到忘了時間，所以錯過了家裡的晚餐。
catch sight of: As the bus turned the corner, I caught sight of my old teacher waiting at the stop with a big bag.
公車轉過街角時，我看見我以前的老師提著一個大袋子在站牌等車。
lose sight of: We lost sight of our little brother in the crowded night market, but we found him at the ice cream stand.
我們在擠滿人的夜市看不見弟弟了，但後來在冰淇淋攤找到了他。
take hold of: When the boat moved suddenly, the little girl took hold of her father's arm and did not let go.
船突然晃動時，小女孩抓住爸爸的手臂不放。
take notice of: Nobody took notice of the small sign on the door, so several people walked into the wrong room.
沒有人注意到門上的小標示，所以好幾個人走進了錯的房間。
take the place of: Many people think that email has taken the place of letters, but my grandmother still writes to me by hand.
很多人認為電子郵件已經取代了信件，但我奶奶還是親手寫信給我。
think highly of: All the teachers think highly of Amy because she studies hard and always helps other students with their problems.
所有老師都高度評價艾咪，因為她用功讀書，而且總是幫其他學生解決問題。
be short of money: I am a bit short of money this month, so I will not see any movies until I get my pocket money.
我這個月有點缺錢，所以在拿到零用錢之前不會去看電影。
be free of charge: The museum is free of charge for students on Sundays, so let's bring our student cards and go together.
這間博物館星期日對學生免費，所以我們帶學生證一起去吧。
be in need of: The old man living alone next door is in need of help, so my family brings him dinner every evening.
隔壁獨居的老先生需要幫助，所以我家每天晚上都幫他送晚餐。
in case of: In case of fire, do not run or push; walk down the stairs quickly and wait outside the building.
如果發生火災，不要奔跑或推擠；快速走下樓梯，並在大樓外面等待。
in terms of: In terms of price, this phone is a good choice, but the camera is not as good as the other one.
就價格而言，這支手機是個好選擇，但相機不如另一支好。
on top of: The cat likes to sleep on top of the warm washing machine while it is running in the afternoon.
這隻貓喜歡在下午洗衣機運轉時，睡在溫暖的洗衣機上面。
at the cost of: Jason got high grades at the cost of his health, because he slept only four hours a night for months.
傑森以健康為代價換來高分，因為他好幾個月來每晚只睡四小時。
at the end of: At the end of the school year, our class will have a big party and say goodbye to our teacher.
在學年結尾，我們班會舉辦一場大派對，跟老師道別。
by means of: My grandmother cannot walk very far, so she gets to the market by means of a small blue bus every morning.
我奶奶不能走太遠，所以她每天早上藉由一輛藍色小巴士去市場。
by way of: We flew to Japan by way of Hong Kong, and the long trip took us almost ten hours in total.
我們經由香港飛到日本，整趟漫長的旅程總共花了我們將近十個小時。
for fear of: Jenny did not tell her mother about the broken window for fear of being punished before dinner.
珍妮因為怕在晚餐前被處罰，所以沒有告訴媽媽窗戶破掉的事。
a man of 50: Our new math teacher is a man of 50, but he runs faster than most students on the playground.
我們的新數學老師是個五十歲的男人，但他在操場上跑得比大多數學生還快。
a boy of ten: A boy of ten won the city chess game last weekend, and his proud parents cried with joy.
一個十歲的男孩上週末贏了市立象棋比賽，他驕傲的父母高興得哭了。
the 5th of May: The school sports day will be held on the fifth of May, so please wear your sports shoes that morning.
學校運動會將在五月五日舉行，所以那天早上請穿你的運動鞋。
of late: Of late, my little brother has been going to bed early because he wants to grow taller for basketball.
最近，我弟弟都很早上床睡覺，因為他想為了打籃球長得更高。
of one's own: After sharing a bedroom with two sisters for years, Lisa finally has a small room of her own.
和兩個姊妹共用房間好幾年之後，麗莎終於有了一間自己的小房間。
be of help: If you want to pass the English test, this little blue book will be of help to you every night.
如果你想通過英文考試，這本藍色小書每晚都會對你有幫助。
be of use: An old map of the city may still be of use when your phone has no power on the trip.
旅行時當你的手機沒電，一張舊的城市地圖可能仍然有用。
be of great value: This old watch from my grandfather is of great value to me, so I never wear it to school.
這支爺爺留下的舊手錶對我來說很有價值，所以我從不戴它去學校。
be of no use: Crying about the lost game is of no use now, so let us practice harder for the next one.
現在為輸掉的比賽哭是沒用的，所以我們為下一場更努力練習吧。
how kind of him: How kind of him to carry the heavy bags for the old lady all the way up the stairs!
他真好心，一路幫那位老太太把重重的袋子提上樓梯！
smell of smoke: When Dad came home from the party, his coat smelled of smoke, and Mom asked him to wash it.
爸爸從派對回家時，他的外套有煙味，媽媽叫他去洗一洗。
taste of lemon: This cold tea tastes of lemon, and it is the perfect drink on such a hot summer afternoon.
這杯冰茶有檸檬味，在這麼熱的夏日午後是最棒的飲料。
dream of: Since she was a little girl, Amy has dreamed of becoming a doctor and helping sick children in the mountains.
從小女孩的時候起，艾美就夢想成為醫生，幫助山上生病的孩子。
know of: I know of a cheap restaurant near the station, but I have never eaten there with my family.
我知道車站附近有一家便宜的餐廳，但我從來沒有和家人在那裡吃過飯。
the love of money: The love of money made the rich man in the story forget his old friends and his family.
故事裡對錢的愛讓那個有錢人忘了他的老朋友和家人。
fear of the dark: My little sister has a fear of the dark, so she always sleeps with a small light on.
我妹妹怕黑，所以她總是開著一盞小燈睡覺。
be made of (看得出材料) vs. be made from: This table is made of wood, but the paper in your notebook is made from wood too.
這張桌子是由木頭做的（看得出材料），但你筆記本裡的紙也是從木頭製成的（看不出）。
die of (疾病) vs. die from (外因): My grandfather died of cancer last year, and his old dog died from the cold a few months later.
我爺爺去年死於癌症，而他的老狗幾個月後死於寒冷。
think of (想到) vs. think about (思考): When I think of my grandmother, I smile, but I need to think about how to visit her this winter.
當我想到奶奶，我就會微笑，但我需要考慮這個冬天怎麼去看她。
hear of (聽說) vs. hear from (收到消息): I have heard of that famous singer, but I have never heard from my old friend who moved to Japan.
我聽說過那位有名的歌手，但我從來沒有收到搬去日本的老朋友的來信。
be tired of (厭倦) vs. be tired from (累): Tom is tired of eating the same lunch every day, and he is also tired from running so much at practice.
湯姆厭倦了每天吃同樣的午餐，而且他也因為練習時跑太多而疲累。
a number of (許多) vs. the number of (數量): A number of students were late this morning, and the number of late students is growing every week.
今天早上許多學生遲到了，而遲到學生的數量每週都在增加。
be afraid of sth. vs. be afraid to do: My brother is afraid of big dogs, so he is afraid to walk past the park alone at night.
我弟弟害怕大狗，所以他不敢晚上獨自走過公園。
dream of (夢想) vs. dream about (作夢): Kevin dreams of playing basketball in America, and last night he even dreamed about scoring the winning point.
凱文夢想在美國打籃球，昨晚他甚至夢到自己投進了致勝的一球。
It is kind of you (個性) vs. It is easy fo: It is kind of you to help me with my homework, but it is easy for me to finish the reading part.
你幫我做作業真好心，不過閱讀的部分對我來說很容易完成。
a friend of mine (不說 a my friend): A friend of mine is moving to Tainan next month, so we are having a goodbye party on Friday.
我的一個朋友下個月要搬去台南，所以我們星期五要辦一場送別派對。
the key to (非 of) the door: I could not find the key to the door of our house this morning, so I was late for school again.
今天早上我找不到我們家門的鑰匙，所以我又上學遲到了。
the answer to (非 of) the question: Nobody in our class knew the answer to the last question of the test, so the teacher explained it again.
我們班上沒有人知道考卷最後一題問題的答案，所以老師又解釋了一次。
the way to (非 of) the station: An old man kindly showed us the way to the station in the middle of the heavy rain.
在大雨之中，一位老先生親切地告訴我們去車站的路。
the reason for (非 of): The reason for his sad face yesterday was a fight with one of his best friends at lunch time.
他昨天一臉難過的原因是午餐時間和他的一個好朋友吵架了。
be good at (非 of): My sister is good at drawing, so she always helps me with the pictures of the school newspaper.
我姊姊擅長畫畫，所以她總是幫我畫學校報紙的圖。
be interested in (非 of): Ben is interested in old trains, and he spends most of his Sunday afternoons reading books about them.
班對老火車有興趣，他星期日下午大部分時間都在讀關於火車的書。
of course vs. off course: Of course we will come to your birthday party, unless our little boat goes off course on the lake!
我們當然會去你的生日派對，除非我們的小船在湖上偏離航線！
of (屬於) vs. off (離開): The handle of the cup broke off when it fell, and the hot tea ran all over the table.
杯子的把手（屬於杯子）掉下時斷開（脫離）了，熱茶流滿了整張桌子。
take off one's coat: It was very warm inside the restaurant, so Grandpa took off his coat and hung it on the chair.
餐廳裡很溫暖，所以爺爺脫下外套，把它掛在椅子上。
take off (plane): Our plane took off late because of the heavy rain, so we missed the first show in Japan.
因為大雨，我們的飛機起飛晚了，所以我們錯過了在日本的第一場表演。
put off the meeting: The teachers put off the meeting until Friday because many of them were sick with the flu this week.
老師們把會議延後到星期五，因為這週很多人得了流感生病。
turn off the light: Please turn off the light when you leave the room, because we need to save energy at school.
離開房間時請關燈，因為我們在學校需要節省能源。
get off the bus: You should get off the bus at the third stop, and then walk two blocks to the library.
你應該在第三站下公車，然後走兩個街區到圖書館。
fall off the bike: Little Mike fell off the bike on the wet road, but luckily he only hurt his left knee.
小麥克在濕滑的路上從腳踏車上掉下來，但幸運的是他只傷到左膝。
call off the game: The coach called off the game this afternoon because the field was full of water after the storm.
教練今天下午取消比賽，因為暴風雨後球場積滿了水。
set off: We set off for the mountains at five in the morning, so everyone slept on the bus.
我們早上五點出發去山上，所以大家都在巴士上睡著了。
see sb. off: The whole family went to the airport to see Uncle Jack off before his long trip to America.
全家人都到機場去送別傑克叔叔，然後他才踏上去美國的長途旅行。
show off: Peter likes to show off his new phone in class, but the teacher told him to put it away.
彼得喜歡在班上炫耀他的新手機，但老師叫他把手機收起來。
cut off: The strong wind cut off the power last night, so we ate dinner by candle light and told stories.
昨晚強風切斷了電力，所以我們在燭光下吃晚餐、說故事。
give off a smell: The old shoes under his bed give off a terrible smell, so his mother threw them away today.
他床底下的舊鞋子散發出可怕的氣味，所以他媽媽今天把鞋丟掉了。
go off (alarm): My alarm went off at six this morning, but I was so sleepy that I stayed in bed until seven.
今天早上六點我的鬧鐘響了，但我太睏了，一直躺到七點才起床。
keep off the grass: The sign in the park says keep off the grass, but some children still run and play there every afternoon.
公園裡的牌子寫著勿踐踏草地，但有些孩子每天下午還是在那裡跑來跑去玩。
kick off: The school festival will kick off with a short dance show at nine, so please arrive before that.
學校慶典將以一場短短的舞蹈表演在九點開始，所以請在那之前到。
lay off workers: The factory had to lay off thirty workers last month because people stopped buying its old-style radios.
那家工廠上個月不得不裁掉三十名員工，因為人們不再買它的老式收音機。
run off: The little dog ran off with my shoe, and I chased it around the garden for ten minutes.
那隻小狗帶著我的鞋子跑掉了，我在花園裡追了它十分鐘。
tell sb. off: Mom told Jack off for playing games all night, and now he has to study in the living room.
媽媽責罵傑克整晚玩遊戲，現在他必須在客廳念書。
wear off: The medicine helped at first, but the good feeling began to wear off after only two or three hours.
那個藥一開始有效，但舒服的感覺在短短兩三個小時後就開始逐漸消失。
write off: My uncle decided to write off the money his old friend had borrowed, because he cared more about the friendship.
我叔叔決定把老朋友借走的錢一筆勾銷，因為他更在乎這段友誼。
cool off: After running around the field in the hot sun, the players jumped into the pool to cool off.
在大太陽下繞著球場跑完後，球員們跳進游泳池涼快一下。
drop off: Grandpa dropped off in his chair while watching the news, and the cat slept on his knees.
爺爺看新聞時在椅子上睡著了，貓就睡在他的膝上。
back off: The police officer asked the crowd to back off so that the doctor could help the hurt man.
警察要求群眾退開，好讓醫生能幫助那位受傷的男子。
break off: Our phone call broke off in the middle of the story because the train went into a long tunnel.
我們的電話在故事講到一半時中斷了，因為火車開進了一條長長的隧道。
hold off: The farmers decided to hold off planting the rice until the heavy rain stops at the end of the week.
農民們決定推遲種稻，等到週末大雨停了再說。
let off: The teacher let Amy off this time because it was her first time to forget her homework all year.
老師這次放過艾美，因為這是她一整年第一次忘記帶作業。
sell off: Before moving to a smaller house, my parents sold off most of the old furniture at a low price.
搬去較小的房子之前，我爸媽以低價把大部分舊家具賣掉了。
shut off: Please shut off the water after you wash your hands, because the school is trying to save water.
洗完手請關掉水，因為學校正努力省水。
take a day off: Dad will take a day off next Friday so that he can watch my basketball game at school.
爸爸下週五會請一天假，這樣他就能看我在學校的籃球比賽。
be off to school: It is already seven thirty, so finish your milk quickly, because you are off to school in five minutes.
已經七點半了，所以快把牛奶喝完，因為你五分鐘後就要去上學了。
be off work: My mother is off work this week, so she is cooking a special dinner for us every evening.
我媽媽這週不上班，所以她每天晚上都為我們煮特別的晚餐。
be well off: The family next door is well off, but their children still ride old bikes to school like us.
隔壁那家人很富有，但他們的孩子仍然像我們一樣騎舊腳踏車上學。
be badly off: Many families in the story were badly off, so the children had to work instead of going to school.
故事裡許多家庭很貧窮，所以孩子們必須工作而不能上學。
take 10% off: The shop near our school will take 10% off all notebooks this week, so let us buy some tomorrow.
我們學校附近的商店這週所有筆記本都打九折，所以我們明天去買一些吧。
get off work: My father usually gets off work at six, and then he picks me up from the library on his way home.
我爸爸通常六點下班，然後他回家途中會去圖書館接我。
get off to a good start: Our team got off to a good start this season, winning the first three games by a lot.
我們的球隊這個球季有個好的開始，前三場比賽都大勝。
go off to sleep: The baby finally went off to sleep after Mom sang the same quiet song to her five times.
媽媽對寶寶唱了五遍同一首安靜的歌之後，寶寶終於睡著了。
run off with: In the movie, a clever monkey runs off with a visitor's camera and takes funny pictures of itself.
電影裡，一隻聰明的猴子帶著一位遊客的相機跑掉，還給自己拍了好笑的照片。
come off: One of the buttons came off my school jacket this morning, so my grandmother fixed it for me after dinner.
今天早上我校服外套的一顆鈕扣脫落了，所以晚餐後奶奶幫我把它修好。
have a day off: My mother has a day off tomorrow, so we are going to the night market together after dinner.
我媽媽明天休假一天，所以晚餐後我們要一起去逛夜市。
be off: I must be off now because the last bus leaves in ten minutes, and my mother is waiting at home.
我現在必須離開了，因為最後一班公車十分鐘後開走，而且媽媽在家等我。
The milk is off, so do not drink it, and please put the new bottle in the refrigerator right away.
牛奶壞了，所以不要喝，請馬上把新的那瓶放進冰箱。
The light in the kitchen is off, so I think everyone has already gone to bed for the night.
廚房的燈是關的，所以我想大家晚上都已經上床睡覺了。
Well, I'm off, so thank you for the lovely dinner, and I will call you when I get home.
好了，我走了，謝謝你美味的晚餐，我到家會打電話給你。
off and on: It rained off and on all day, so we could not finish our baseball game in the park.
整天斷斷續續地下雨，所以我們無法在公園打完棒球比賽。
off the coast: A small green island lies off the coast, and you can take a boat there from the beach in twenty minutes.
有一座綠色小島在離岸不遠處，你可以從海灘搭船二十分鐘到那裡。
a street off the main road: The best noodle shop in town is on a quiet street off the main road, right behind the post office.
鎮上最好吃的麵店在主幹道旁的一條安靜小街上，就在郵局後面。
fall off the wall: The old picture fell off the wall during the earthquake last night, but the glass did not break.
昨晚地震時那幅舊畫從牆上掉下來，但玻璃沒有破。
keep off the road: Children, please keep off the road and walk on the sidewalk, because the cars drive very fast here.
孩子們，請別走在路上，要走人行道，因為這裡的車開得很快。
jump off the bridge: In summer, some brave boys jump off the bridge into the river, but it is really dangerous.
夏天時，有些勇敢的男孩從橋上跳進河裡，但那真的很危險。
get off the plane: After we got off the plane in Japan, the cold air made us put on our coats right away.
我們在日本下飛機後，冷空氣讓我們馬上穿上外套。
take the book off the shelf: Mom asked me to take the book off the shelf and read a story to my little brother before bed.
媽媽叫我把書從架上拿下來，睡前讀一個故事給弟弟聽。
off the point: The teacher said my answer was off the point because I talked about my pet instead of the weather.
老師說我的答案離題了，因為我談的是我的寵物而不是天氣。
off the record: The player told the reporter something off the record, so it did not appear in the newspaper the next day.
那位球員私下告訴記者一些不公開的事，所以第二天報紙上並沒有刊出來。
off duty: The nurse is off duty now, so you can find her having lunch at the little shop across the street.
那位護士現在下班了，所以你可以在街對面的小店找到她在吃午餐。
off season: Hotels near the beach are much cheaper in the off season, so my family likes to travel in winter.
海邊的旅館在淡季便宜很多，所以我家喜歡冬天去旅行。
off the top of my head: Off the top of my head, I can name five countries in Asia, but I need a map for the rest.
一時想到的，我可以說出亞洲五個國家的名字，但其餘的我需要看地圖。
off (離開表面) vs. of (屬於): The cat jumped off the roof of the house and landed quietly on the grass in the garden.
那隻貓從房子的屋頂（屬於房子）上跳下來（脫離），安靜地落在花園的草地上。
turn off (關) vs. turn down (關小): Please turn off the TV before you sleep, or at least turn down the sound so Grandma can rest.
睡前請把電視關掉，或者至少把聲音調小，讓奶奶可以休息。
get off (下大車) vs. get out of (下小車): We get off the bus at the school gate, but Lisa gets out of her father's car across the street.
我們在校門口下公車，而麗莎則是在街對面從她爸爸的車上下來。
