take off (脫) vs. put on (穿): Take off your wet shoes at the door and put on these warm socks before you catch a cold.
在門口脫下你的濕鞋子，穿上這些溫暖的襪子，免得你感冒。
put off (延後) vs. call off (取消): The school put off the sports day because of the rain, but it did not call off the music show.
學校因為下雨把運動會延後了，但並沒有取消音樂表演。
off (離開) vs. from (來自): The boy jumped off the bus quickly, because the letter from his grandmother in Japan had finally arrived.
男孩很快地從公車上跳下來，因為來自日本奶奶的信終於寄到了。
take it off the table (非 from): Please take the dirty plates off the table and bring the fruit from the kitchen for everyone.
請把髒盤子從桌上拿走，然後從廚房把水果拿來給大家。
be off (休假) vs. be out (外出): Mr. Lin is off today because it is his holiday, but Miss Chen is just out for lunch.
林先生今天休假，因為是他的假日，但陳小姐只是外出吃午餐。
off work (下班) vs. out of work (失業): My father is off work every evening at six, but my uncle has been out of work since March.
我爸爸每天晚上六點下班，但我叔叔從三月起就一直失業。
on Monday: On Monday our class has a big English test, so most of us studied at the library this weekend.
星期一我們班有一個重要的英文考試，所以我們大部分人這個週末都在圖書館念書。
on May 5: My grandmother will visit us on May 5, and my mother is planning a big dinner for the whole family.
我奶奶會在五月五日來看我們，媽媽正在為全家計畫一頓豐盛的晚餐。
on the weekend: On the weekend, my family often rides bikes along the river and then eats noodles at a small shop.
在週末，我家常常沿著河邊騎腳踏車，然後在一家小店吃麵。
on Monday morning: The students were very sleepy on Monday morning because they all stayed up late watching the ball game.
學生們在週一早上都很睏，因為他們都熬夜看球賽。
on Christmas Day: On Christmas Day, we open our presents first and then eat a big breakfast with Grandpa and Grandma.
在聖誕節當天，我們先打開禮物，然後和爺爺奶奶一起吃豐盛的早餐。
on my birthday: On my birthday, my friends surprised me with a chocolate cake and a card signed by the whole class.
在我生日那天，朋友們用巧克力蛋糕和一張全班簽名的卡片給我驚喜。
on New Year's Eve: On New Year's Eve, we stayed up until midnight to watch the lights over the tall building in Taipei.
在除夕夜，我們熬夜到午夜，看台北高樓上空的燈光。
on time: Our school bus always arrives on time, so I never have to run to class in the morning.
我們的校車總是準時到，所以我早上從來不必跑著去上課。
on the first day: On the first day of high school, Tina was nervous, but she made two new friends at lunch time.
在高中的第一天，蒂娜很緊張，但她在午餐時間交到了兩個新朋友。
on a cold night: On a cold night last winter, a small white cat came to our door, and we gave it some warm milk.
去年冬天一個寒冷的夜晚，一隻小白貓來到我們家門口，我們給了它一些溫牛奶。
on arriving home: On arriving home, Mary took off her shoes, washed her hands, and ran to the kitchen for a snack.
瑪麗一到家就脫掉鞋子、洗手，然後跑到廚房找點心吃。
on Sundays: On Sundays, my father and I go to the park early and play basketball before the sun gets too hot.
每逢星期日，我和爸爸會早早去公園，在太陽變得太熱之前打籃球。
on the morning of May 1: On the morning of May 1, the whole school went to the mountains to plant young trees together.
在五月一日早上，全校一起到山上種小樹。
on holiday: Our English teacher is on holiday in Japan this week, so a new teacher is reading stories with us.
我們的英文老師這週在日本度假，所以一位新老師在和我們一起讀故事。
on the hour: The trains to Tainan leave on the hour, so we should get to the station a little before ten.
往台南的火車每逢整點發車，所以我們應該在十點前一點到車站。
on the table: Your lunch box is on the table, and please do not forget your water bottle this time.
你的便當盒在桌上，這次請不要忘了你的水壺。
on the wall: There is a large map of the world on the wall, and we often look for new countries on it.
牆上有一張很大的世界地圖，我們常常在上面找新的國家。
on the floor: The baby dropped her toy on the floor, and the dog picked it up and ran away with it.
寶寶把玩具掉在地板上，狗狗撿起來就帶著它跑走了。
on the bus: I usually read a book on the bus to school, but today it was too crowded to open my bag.
我通常在上學的公車上看書，但今天太擠了，連書包都打不開。
on the train: We ate rice balls and drank tea on the train while watching the green fields go by outside.
我們在火車上吃飯糰、喝茶，一邊看著窗外綠色的田野經過。
on the plane: On the plane to Japan, my little brother watched three movies and did not sleep at all.
在去日本的飛機上，我弟弟看了三部電影，完全沒有睡覺。
on the second floor: The music room is on the second floor, right next to the library, so you can hear the piano from there.
音樂教室在二樓，就在圖書館旁邊，所以你可以從那裡聽到鋼琴聲。
on the left: Walk straight for two blocks, and you will see the post office on the left, next to the bank.
直走兩個街區，你會看到郵局在左邊，就在銀行旁邊。
on the right: The bookstore is on the right when you come out of the station, so you cannot miss it.
當你走出車站時，書店就在右邊，所以你不會錯過它。
on the corner: There is a small store on the corner, and we often buy cold drinks there after school on hot days.
街角有一家小商店，天熱的日子我們放學後常常在那裡買冷飲。
on the beach: On the beach, the children built a big sand castle while their parents rested under a tree.
在海灘上，孩子們堆了一座大沙堡，而他們的父母在樹下休息。
on the farm: My cousins live on the farm with many cows and chickens, so they get up at five every day.
我的表兄弟姊妹住在農場，那裡有很多牛和雞，所以他們每天五點起床。
on the island: Only about two hundred people live on the island, and most of them are fishermen or farmers.
島上只住了大約兩百人，他們大多數是漁民或農民。
on the page: The answers to the questions are on the page after the story, so do not look before you finish.
問題的答案在故事後面那一頁上，所以做完前不要先看。
on the road: There were many cars on the road this morning because of the rain, so Dad was late for work.
今天早上因為下雨，路上車很多，所以爸爸上班遲到了。
on the river: Several small boats were on the river, and the people in them were catching fish for dinner.
河上有幾艘小船，船上的人正在捕魚當晚餐。
on the way to school: On the way to school, I saw an old woman drop her bag, so I helped her pick everything up.
在上學途中，我看到一位老太太掉了袋子，所以我幫她把東西全部撿起來。
on the top of the mountain: On the top of the mountain, the wind was very strong, but the view of the sea was beautiful.
在山頂上，風很強，但海景非常美麗。
on the ceiling: There is a small brown spider on the ceiling of my room, and I am too afraid to sleep.
我房間的天花板上有一隻棕色小蜘蛛，我怕得不敢睡覺。
on the back of the card: Write your name and class on the back of the card, and then give it to your teacher tomorrow.
在卡片背面寫上你的名字和班級，然後明天交給老師。
on the other side: My best friend lives on the other side of the river, so we meet at the bridge every Saturday.
我最好的朋友住在河的另一邊，所以我們每個星期六在橋上見面。
on the ground: After the storm, there were many leaves and small branches on the ground all around the school.
暴風雨過後，學校周圍的地上有許多樹葉和小樹枝。
on the moon: Many years ago, people first walked on the moon, and my grandfather watched it on a small TV.
許多年前，人類第一次在月球上行走，而我爺爺在一台小電視上看到了。
on the phone: My sister has been on the phone with her friend for an hour, so I cannot call Grandma.
我姊姊已經和朋友講電話講了一個小時，所以我沒辦法打給奶奶。
on the Internet: You can find many free English lessons on the Internet, but be careful about what you believe there.
你可以在網路上找到許多免費的英文課程，但要小心你在那裡相信的內容。
on TV: We watched the baseball game on TV last night, and my father jumped up when our team won.
我們昨晚在電視上看棒球比賽，我們的隊贏時爸爸跳了起來。
on the radio: Grandpa likes to listen to old songs on the radio while he waters the plants in the morning.
爺爺早上澆花時喜歡聽廣播中的老歌。
on the screen: The words on the screen were too small to read, so the teacher made them bigger for us.
螢幕上的字太小看不清楚，所以老師把字放大給我們看。
on the map: Can you find our school on the map, and then show me the shortest way to the train station?
你能在地圖上找到我們的學校，然後告訴我去火車站最短的路嗎？
on the list: My name is on the list for the school trip, but my best friend has to wait for another chance.
我的名字在學校旅行的名單上，但我最好的朋友得等下一次機會。
on the menu: There are only a few vegetable dishes on the menu, so my mother ordered a salad and some soup.
菜單上只有幾道蔬菜料理，所以我媽媽點了沙拉和一些湯。
on the news: The big fire at the old factory was on the news this morning, and nobody was hurt luckily.
舊工廠的大火今天早上出現在新聞上，幸運的是沒有人受傷。
on the computer: My brother spends too much time playing games on the computer, so Mom only lets him use it on weekends.
我哥哥花太多時間在電腦上玩遊戲，所以媽媽只讓他週末用電腦。
on a farm: Last summer we stayed on a farm for a week and learned how to feed the pigs and pick fruit.
去年夏天我們在農場住了一週，學習怎麼餵豬和採水果。
on the tree: The oranges on the tree in our yard are turning yellow, so we can pick them next week.
我們院子裡樹上的橘子正在變黃，所以我們下週就能採了。
on the first page: Please write your name on the first page of the notebook so that nobody will take it by mistake.
請在筆記本的第一頁寫上你的名字，這樣就不會有人拿錯。
on the wall of the room: My little sister drew a big yellow sun on the wall of the room, and Mom was not happy at all.
我妹妹在房間牆上畫了一個大大的黃色太陽，媽媽一點也不高興。
on the edge: Do not put your glass on the edge of the table, or it will fall and break into pieces.
不要把你的杯子放在桌子邊緣，否則它會掉下來摔成碎片。
on the back seat: My grandmother always sits on the back seat of the car because she feels safer there on long trips.
我奶奶總是坐在車子的後座，因為長途旅行時她覺得那裡比較安全。
on the back: The little girl rode on the back of her father all the way home from the night market.
小女孩從夜市一路騎在爸爸的背上回家。
on one's knees: The farmer was on his knees in the field, planting small green vegetables one by one in the warm sun.
農夫在田裡跪著，在溫暖的陽光下一株一株地種下綠色小蔬菜。
on foot: The school is only ten minutes away, so I go there on foot every morning with my neighbor.
學校只有十分鐘的距離，所以我每天早上和鄰居走路去學校。
on sale: These sports shoes are on sale this week, so Dad bought a pair for me and one for my brother.
這些運動鞋這週特價中，所以爸爸買了一雙給我，一雙給我哥哥。
for sale (非 on): The old house on our street has been for sale for months, but nobody wants to buy it yet.
我們這條街上的那間老房子已經出售好幾個月了，但還沒有人想買。
on fire: The kitchen was on fire when we came home, so we called for help and waited outside the house.
我們回家時廚房著火了，所以我們打電話求助，然後在房子外面等。
on purpose: I did not break your pencil on purpose, so please do not be angry with me anymore.
我不是故意弄斷你的鉛筆的，所以請不要再生我的氣了。
on duty: My mother is a nurse, and she is on duty tonight, so Dad is cooking dinner for us.
我媽媽是護士，她今晚值班，所以爸爸在煮晚餐給我們吃。
on business: My father is away on business in Japan this week, but he promised to bring us some candy.
我爸爸這週在日本出差，但他答應帶一些糖果回來給我們。
on vacation: Our neighbors are on vacation in Tainan, so we are feeding their cat and watering their plants.
我們的鄰居在台南度假，所以我們幫他們餵貓和澆花。
on a trip: Grandpa is on a trip to the mountains with his old friends, and he sends us pictures every day.
爺爺和老朋友們在山上旅行中，他每天都傳照片給我們。
on a diet: My aunt is on a diet, so she only had a small salad while we all enjoyed the pizza.
我阿姨正在節食中，所以當我們都大吃披薩時，她只吃了一小份沙拉。
on one's own: For the first time, Kevin cooked dinner for his family on his own, and everyone said it was delicious.
凱文第一次獨自為家人煮晚餐，大家都說很好吃。
on the whole: The trip had some problems, but on the whole we had a great time and made many good friends.
這次旅行有一些問題，但整體而言我們玩得很開心，也交了許多好朋友。
on the other hand: Living in the city is convenient, but on the other hand, it is noisy and the air is not clean.
住在城市很方便，但另一方面，它很吵，而且空氣不乾淨。
on one hand: On one hand, I want to join the basketball team, but I also need more time for my studies.
一方面，我想加入籃球隊，但我也需要更多時間念書。
on the spot: When the boy fell off his bike, a kind doctor who was passing by helped him on the spot.
當男孩從腳踏車上摔下來時，一位路過的好心醫生當場幫助了他。
on the go: My mother is always on the go, working at the office in the day and taking care of us at night.
我媽媽總是忙碌不停，白天在辦公室工作，晚上照顧我們。
on the run: The thief has been on the run for three days, and the police are looking for him everywhere in the city.
那個小偷已經逃跑了三天，警察正在城市各處找他。
on the move: The soldiers were on the move all night, so they were very tired when they reached the river.
士兵們整夜都在移動中，所以他們到達河邊時非常疲倦。
on strike: The bus drivers are on strike this week, so many students have to ride their bikes to school.
公車司機這週罷工中，所以許多學生必須騎腳踏車上學。
on a team: Amy is on a team with five other girls, and they practice volleyball together every Tuesday afternoon.
艾美和另外五個女孩在同一隊上，她們每週二下午一起練排球。
on the team: Jack has been on the team for two years, and he hopes to become the captain next spring.
傑克成為隊上一員已經兩年了，他希望明年春天能當上隊長。
on hand: Always keep some water and a flashlight on hand in case the power goes out during a typhoon.
手邊要隨時準備一些水和手電筒，以防颱風期間停電。
on and on: The baby cried on and on for an hour, and nothing we did could make her stop.
寶寶不停地哭了一個小時，我們做什麼都無法讓她停下來。
on and off: It rained on and off during the picnic, so we kept running under the big tree for cover.
野餐時斷斷續續地下雨，所以我們一直跑到大樹下躲雨。
on show: The students' pictures are on show in the school hall this week, and parents are welcome to visit.
學生們的畫作這週在學校禮堂展出中，歡迎家長來參觀。
on offer: Fresh strawberries are on offer at the market today, so Mom bought three boxes to make jam.
今天市場的新鮮草莓特價供應，所以媽媽買了三盒來做果醬。
on the market: This new phone has been on the market for only a month, but many people have already bought it.
這款新手機上市只有一個月，但已經有許多人買了。
on the air: The school radio show is on the air every Friday at noon, and students can send in their favorite songs.
學校廣播節目每週五中午播出中，學生可以寄來他們最喜歡的歌。
on the increase: The number of people riding bikes to work is on the increase because the roads are so crowded.
騎腳踏車上班的人數正在增加中，因為道路太擁擠了。
on the rise: Food prices are on the rise this year, so my mother is cooking more vegetables from our own garden.
今年食物價格正在上升中，所以我媽媽更常煮我們自家花園種的蔬菜。
on the way: Do not worry, Dad is already on the way, and he will pick us up at the gate in ten minutes.
別擔心，爸爸已經在路上了，他十分鐘後會在大門口接我們。
on the point of: We were on the point of leaving the house when the phone rang and Grandma invited us to lunch.
我們即將出門時，電話響了，奶奶邀請我們去吃午餐。
on the basis of: The teacher chose the team captain on the basis of hard work, not on how tall or fast the players were.
老師基於努力程度來選隊長，而不是看球員多高或多快。
on the edge of: Our small house stands on the edge of the forest, so we hear birds singing every morning.
我們的小房子位在森林的邊緣，所以我們每天早上都聽到鳥兒唱歌。
on a daily basis: My grandfather walks for thirty minutes on a daily basis, and that is why he is still so healthy.
我爺爺每天走路三十分鐘，這就是他仍然這麼健康的原因。
on earth: What on earth are you doing with my new bike in the rain at nine o'clock at night?
你究竟在晚上九點的雨中拿我的新腳踏車做什麼？
on the side: Besides teaching at school, Mr. Wang sells bread on the side to help pay for his son's college.
除了在學校教書，王老師另外兼職賣麵包，來幫忙付兒子的大學學費。
on the house: The owner of the noodle shop said the drinks were on the house because it was his birthday today.
麵店老闆說飲料店家招待，因為今天是他的生日。
on me: Lunch is on me today because you helped me carry all those heavy boxes up the stairs.
今天午餐我請客，因為你幫我把那些重重的箱子全部搬上樓。
on second thought: I wanted to buy the red shoes, but on second thought, the blue ones go better with my clothes.
我原本想買那雙紅鞋，但再想一想，藍色那雙比較配我的衣服。
on the tip of my tongue: The name of that actor is on the tip of my tongue, but I just cannot say it right now.
那位演員的名字我快想起來了，但我現在就是說不出來。
on the same page: Before we start the group report, let us talk first so that everyone is on the same page about the plan.
在我們開始小組報告之前，先來談一談，好讓大家對計畫的看法一致。
on good terms with: Although they fought a lot when they were little, Amy is now on good terms with her older brother.
雖然他們小時候常常吵架，Amy 現在和哥哥的關係很好。
be on the ball: Our new class leader is really on the ball, so she always knows what we need to do next.
我們的新班長真的很機靈，所以她總是知道我們接下來該做什麼。
Jack gets on well with his new friends at school because he is kind and likes to share his snacks.
Jack 和學校的新朋友相處得很好，因為他很善良，也喜歡分享他的零食。
keep on doing: Even though the rain was getting heavier, the boys kept on playing basketball on the school playground.
即使雨越下越大，男孩們還是繼續在學校操場上打籃球。
go on doing: The teacher went on talking about the test, but most of the students were already thinking about lunch.
老師繼續談著考試的事，但大多數學生已經在想午餐了。
carry on: After a short break for some water, the students carried on and finished the long race together.
短暫休息喝了點水之後，學生們繼續跑，一起完成了這場長跑。
hold on: Hold on a second, Mom, I just need to find my school bag before we leave the house.
媽，稍等一下，我們出門前我只需要找到我的書包。
come on: Come on, Peter, the bus leaves in five minutes and we cannot be late for school again.
快點，Peter，公車五分鐘後就開了，我們不能再上學遲到了。
put on weight: My uncle put on a lot of weight last winter because he ate too much and never exercised.
我叔叔去年冬天變胖了很多，因為他吃太多又從不運動。
put on a show: The students in Class 302 will put on a show for their parents at the end of this school year.
三年二班的學生將在這學年結束時為他們的父母演出一場表演。
put on your shoes: It is cold outside this morning, so please put on your shoes and a warm jacket before you leave.
今天早上外面很冷，所以離開前請穿上鞋子和一件暖和的夾克。
try on the dress: Lisa tried on the blue dress in the store, but it was too big for her, so she chose another one.
Lisa 在店裡試穿了那件藍色洋裝，但對她來說太大了，所以她選了另一件。
turn on the TV: As soon as Grandpa got home from his walk, he turned on the TV to watch the baseball game.
爺爺散步回家後，馬上就開電視看棒球比賽。
get on the bus: We got on the bus at the train station and found two empty seats near the back door.
我們在火車站上了公車，在後門附近找到兩個空位。
move on: Losing the game made us sad, but our coach told us to move on and get ready for the next one.
輸了比賽讓我們很難過，但教練告訴我們要繼續前進，為下一場做好準備。
hang on: Hang on a minute, I cannot find my keys, and I think I left them in the kitchen.
稍等一下，我找不到我的鑰匙，我想我把它們留在廚房了。
You can always count on Mary when you need help with math because she is patient and smart.
當你數學需要幫忙時，你永遠可以依賴 Mary，因為她很有耐心又聰明。
depend on: Whether we go to the beach tomorrow depends on the weather, so let us check the news tonight.
我們明天是否去海邊要依賴天氣而定，所以今晚來看一下新聞吧。
live on rice: Many families in Asia live on rice, and they eat it with vegetables and meat almost every day.
亞洲許多家庭以米飯為主食，他們幾乎每天都配著蔬菜和肉一起吃。
live on 100 dollars a day: During his trip to Japan, my cousin had to live on 100 dollars a day, so he cooked his own meals.
我表哥在日本旅行期間，一天只能靠一百元過活，所以他自己煮飯。
spend money on books: Instead of buying video games, Kevin spends most of his money on books about space and animals.
Kevin 沒有買電動遊戲，而是把大部分的錢花在關於太空和動物的書上。
spend time on homework: Every evening after dinner, Jenny spends about two hours on her homework before she watches any TV.
每天晚餐後，Jenny 都會先花大約兩小時在作業上，然後才看電視。
work on a project: Our group is working on a science project about plants, so we water them and write notes every day.
我們這組正在進行一個關於植物的科學專案，所以我們每天澆水並寫筆記。
focus on: It is hard to focus on my studies when my little brother plays loud music in the next room.
當我弟弟在隔壁房間大聲播放音樂時，我很難專注於我的學業。
insist on: My grandmother always insists on cooking dinner for the whole family, even when she is very tired.
我奶奶總是堅持為全家煮晚餐，即使她很累的時候也一樣。
agree on a plan: After talking for an hour, the five of us finally agreed on a plan for the class trip next month.
談了一個小時後，我們五個人終於就下個月班級旅行的計畫達成一致。
decide on a date: The club members have not decided on a date for the party yet, but it will probably be next Friday.
社團成員還沒決定派對的日期，但很可能是下週五。
be based on: This movie is based on a true story about a dog that waited for its owner for ten years.
這部電影是根據一個真實故事改編的，講述一隻狗等了主人十年。
Do not be too hard on yourself for failing the test; you can study harder and do better next time.
不要因為考試不及格就對自己太嚴厲；你可以更努力讀書，下次做得更好。
be on good terms: Our family is on good terms with the neighbors, so we often share food and help each other out.
我們家和鄰居關係良好，所以我們常常分享食物並互相幫忙。
take pity on: The old woman took pity on the hungry cat outside her door and gave it some fish every morning.
老婦人同情門外那隻飢餓的貓，每天早上都給它一些魚。
play a joke on: On April Fools' Day, Tom played a joke on his sister by putting salt in her cup of tea.
愚人節那天，Tom 在姊姊的茶杯裡放鹽，開了她一個玩笑。
play a trick on: The naughty boys played a trick on their teacher by hiding her chalk before the English class began.
那些調皮的男孩在英文課開始前把老師的粉筆藏起來捉弄她。
have an influence on: My music teacher has had a big influence on me, and now I want to play the piano every day.
我的音樂老師對我有很大的影響，現在我每天都想彈鋼琴。
cheat on a test: The teacher caught a student cheating on the test, so he got a zero and had to see the principal.
老師抓到一個學生考試作弊，所以他得了零分，還得去見校長。
wait on tables: During the summer vacation, my older sister waited on tables at a restaurant to make some extra money.
暑假期間，我姊姊在一家餐廳當服務生為客人服務，為了多賺一點錢。
look on the bright side: We missed the last train, but let us look on the bright side; now we can enjoy the night market.
我們錯過了最後一班火車，但讓我們看光明面；現在我們可以好好逛夜市了。
be on one's side: When everyone laughed at my idea, only my best friend Lily was on my side and said it was great.
當大家都笑我的想法時，只有我最好的朋友 Lily 支持我，說這個想法很棒。
on one's mind: Something has been on my mind all week, so I could not sleep well or pay attention in class.
這整個星期我一直掛念著一件事，所以我睡不好，上課也無法專心。
My little sister does not get on with our new neighbor's son because he is always rude to her.
我妹妹和我們新鄰居的兒子相處不來，因為他總是對她很沒禮貌。
put on: The weather suddenly turned cold, so Ben put on his coat and a hat before he rode his bike to school.
天氣突然變冷，所以 Ben 騎腳踏車上學前穿上了外套和帽子。
take on a job: My father took on a second job at night so that he could pay for my sister's college.
我爸爸晚上接下第二份工作，好讓他能支付我姊姊的大學學費。
turn on: Please turn on the light in the kitchen because it is too dark for me to find the cups.
請把廚房的燈打開，因為太暗了我找不到杯子。
try on: You should try on the shoes before you buy them because different stores can have different sizes.
你買鞋之前應該先試穿，因為不同的店尺寸可能不一樣。
go on: Nobody knows what is going on outside, but we can hear people shouting and running down the street.
沒有人知道外面發生了什麼事，但我們聽得到人們在街上大喊和奔跑。
keep on: If you keep on practicing the guitar for thirty minutes every day, you will play very well by summer.
如果你每天繼續練習吉他三十分鐘，到夏天你就會彈得很好。
pass on the message: Mr. Lin is not here right now, but I will pass on the message to him as soon as he comes back.
林先生現在不在，但他一回來我就會把話傳給他。
catch on: The new dance from the music video caught on quickly, and soon everyone at school was trying it.
音樂影片裡的新舞步很快就流行起來，不久學校裡每個人都在嘗試跳。
cheer on the team: Hundreds of students stood in the rain to cheer on the team during the final baseball game.
數百名學生站在雨中，在最後一場棒球賽中為球隊加油。
count on: We are counting on you to bring the cake to the party, so please do not forget it tomorrow.
我們指望你把蛋糕帶來派對，所以明天請不要忘了。
Every Sunday afternoon, my mother and I call on Grandma and Grandpa and bring them fresh fruit from the market.
每個星期天下午，我和媽媽都會去拜訪爺爺奶奶，並從市場帶新鮮的水果給他們。
bring on: Eating too much ice cream on a hot day can bring on a stomachache, so be careful at the night market.
在炎熱的日子吃太多冰淇淋可能引起胃痛，所以在夜市要小心。
look on: When two boys started fighting near the school gate, most students just looked on and nobody stopped them.
當兩個男孩在校門口附近開始打架時，大多數學生只是旁觀，沒有人去阻止他們。
sign on: My brother signed on with the city basketball team last week, and he will start practicing with them on Monday.
我哥哥上週和市籃球隊簽約，他星期一就會開始和他們一起練習。
lead sb. on: The man in the store led Grandpa on with sweet words, so he bought a watch that did not even work.
店裡的男人用甜言蜜語誤導爺爺，所以他買了一支根本不會動的手錶。
live on: Although the famous singer died many years ago, her beautiful songs still live on in the hearts of many people.
雖然這位著名的歌手多年前就過世了，她美麗的歌曲仍然繼續活在許多人的心中。
run on time: The trains in Japan almost always run on time, so people there can plan their trips to the minute.
日本的火車幾乎總是準時運行，所以那裡的人可以把行程計畫到分鐘。
push on: We were tired and hungry after five hours of walking, but we pushed on until we reached the top of the mountain.
走了五個小時後我們又累又餓，但我們繼續前進，直到抵達山頂。
set on fire: Someone set the old house on fire last night, and it took three hours to put out the big fire.
昨晚有人放火燒了那間老房子，花了三個小時才把大火撲滅。
on (表面) vs. in (內部) vs. at (點): The cat is sleeping on the sofa, the milk is in the refrigerator, and Dad is waiting at the door.
貓在沙發上睡覺，牛奶在冰箱裡，而爸爸正在門口等著。
on the bus (在車上) vs. in the car (在車裡): We usually talk loudly on the bus, but in Dad's small car we have to sit quietly in the back.
我們在公車上通常講話很大聲，但在爸爸的小車裡我們得安靜地坐在後座。
on the wall (牆面) vs. in the wall (牆內): There is a big clock on the wall of our music room, and a small hole in the wall under it.
我們音樂教室的牆面上有一個大時鐘，它下面的牆內有一個小洞。
on the tree (長出來) vs. in the tree (外來): Red apples are growing on the tree, and a little bird is singing in the tree right above them.
樹上長著紅蘋果，一隻小鳥就停在它們上方的樹上唱歌。
on time (準時) vs. in time (及時): Peter was not on time for the movie, but he arrived in time to see the exciting ending.
Peter 看電影沒有準時到，但他及時趕到看到了精彩的結局。
on the way (路上) vs. in the way (擋路): I was on the way to school when a big truck in the way made all the cars stop.
我在上學途中時，一輛擋路的大卡車讓所有車子都停了下來。
on the corner (街角) vs. at the corner / i: The new bakery is on the corner of our street, and inside, a cat sleeps in the corner by the window.
新開的麵包店在我們那條街的街角，店裡有一隻貓睡在窗邊的屋角。
on the weekend (美) vs. at the weekend (英: In America people say they rest on the weekend, but my English teacher from London says at the weekend.
美國人說週末休息時用 on the weekend，但我那位來自倫敦的英文老師說 at the weekend。
on Monday vs. in the morning vs. at 9:00: Our English test is on Monday, in the morning, and it starts at 9:00, so do not be late.
我們的英文考試在星期一早上，九點開始，所以不要遲到。
on the beach (沙灘上) vs. at the beach (去海邊: We spent the whole day at the beach, and the kids built a sand castle on the beach near the water.
我們在海邊玩了一整天，孩子們在靠近水邊的沙灘上堆了一座沙堡。
on the phone (講電話) vs. by phone (用電話): Mom is on the phone with Aunt Mary right now, so please order the pizza by phone yourself.
媽媽現在正在和 Mary 阿姨講電話，所以請你自己用電話訂披薩。
on TV (電視節目) vs. on the TV (電視機上): My favorite cartoon is on TV at six, but Dad left his glasses on the TV and cannot find them.
我最喜歡的卡通六點在電視上播，但爸爸把眼鏡放在電視機上面，現在找不到了。
on sale (特價) vs. for sale (出售): These shoes are on sale for only 500 dollars this week, and the old bike next to them is also for sale.
這雙鞋這週特價只要五百元，旁邊那輛舊腳踏車也待售。
on foot (非 by foot): Since the MRT station is only ten minutes away, I go there on foot instead of taking a taxi.
因為捷運站只有十分鐘的路程，我走路去那裡而不搭計程車。
on the Internet (非 in): Many students look for information on the Internet when they write reports, but not everything there is correct.
很多學生寫報告時會在網路上找資料，但那裡並不是所有東西都正確。
on the farm vs. in the field: Grandpa and Grandma raise chickens on the farm, and every morning they work in the field behind their house.
爺爺奶奶在農場養雞，每天早上他們都在屋後的田裡工作。
on the left vs. to the left: The post office is on the left side of the road, so turn to the left at the second traffic light.
郵局在馬路的左邊，所以在第二個紅綠燈向左轉。
on earth (究竟) vs. on the earth (地球上): Grandpa, what on earth are those bright lights, and are we really the only people living on the earth?
爺爺，那些亮光究竟是什麼，而我們真的是地球上唯一的人嗎？
get on (上大車) vs. get in (上小車): We get on the school bus at the corner every morning, but on rainy days we get in Dad's car.
我們每天早上在街角上公車，但下雨天我們就上爸爸的汽車。
spend on (花在…上) vs. spend doing: Jenny spends too much money on comic books and spends every evening reading them instead of studying.
Jenny 花太多錢在漫畫書上，而且每天晚上都花時間看漫畫，而不是讀書。
agree on (事) vs. agree with (人): I agree with Tom that we need a trip, but we still cannot agree on the place to go.
我同意 Tom 說我們需要一次旅行，但我們還是無法就要去的地點達成一致。
depend on (非 of): Children depend on their parents for food and love, and good parents never let them down.
孩子依賴父母獲得食物和愛，而好的父母從不讓他們失望。
be on a diet vs. go on a diet: My aunt is on a diet now, and she says I should go on a diet too because of all my cookies.
我阿姨現在正在節食，她說因為我吃了那麼多餅乾，也應該開始節食。
turn on (開) vs. turn up (調大): Please turn on the radio and turn it up a little because Grandma cannot hear very well.
請把收音機打開，再把音量調大一點，因為奶奶聽不太清楚。
put on (穿上) vs. wear (穿著): Tom put on his new jacket quickly this morning, and he wore it all day because the school was cold.
Tom 今天早上快速穿上新夾克，因為學校很冷，他整天都穿著它。
on holiday vs. on vacation: My British friend says her family is on holiday, but my American cousin says they are on vacation in Japan.
我的英國朋友說她的家人在度假 (on holiday)，而我的美國表哥說他們正在日本度假 (on vacation)。
go out: My parents go out for dinner every Friday night, so my sister and I order pizza and watch movies at home.
我爸媽每個星期五晚上都會出去吃晚餐，所以我和姊姊就在家訂披薩看電影。
come out: The new comic book comes out next Saturday, and Kevin plans to wait outside the bookstore early that morning.
新的漫畫書下週六出版，Kevin 打算那天早上提早在書店外面等。
get out: Get out of the pool now, kids, because the sky is dark and it may start to thunder soon.
孩子們，現在就從游泳池出來，因為天色很暗，可能很快就要打雷了。
find out the truth: The teacher talked to each student alone until she found out the truth about the broken window.
老師單獨和每個學生談話，直到她查明了窗戶破掉的真相。
figure out the answer: After trying for twenty minutes, Mark could finally figure out the answer to the hard math problem by himself.
試了二十分鐘後，Mark 終於自己想出了那道數學難題的答案。
work out the problem: Our teacher gave us some time to work out the problem in groups before she explained it on the board.
老師在黑板上講解之前，給我們一些時間分組解決那個問題。
work out at the gym: My older brother works out at the gym three times a week because he wants to be stronger for basketball.
我哥哥每週去健身房健身三次，因為他想為了籃球變得更強壯。
put out the fire: The fire trucks arrived in ten minutes, and the men put out the fire before it spread to the next house.
消防車十分鐘內就到了，那些人在火蔓延到隔壁房子之前把火撲滅了。
turn out well: We were worried about the rain, but the school picnic turned out well and everyone had a great time.
我們擔心會下雨，但學校的野餐結果很好，大家都玩得很開心。
give out the papers: The teacher asked Linda to give out the test papers while she wrote the rules on the board.
老師請 Linda 發考卷，同時她把規則寫在黑板上。
hand out: Some students stood at the school gate and handed out free water to the players on that hot afternoon.
那個炎熱的下午，一些學生站在校門口向球員分發免費的水。
run out of money: Jack ran out of money on the third day of his trip, so he had to call his parents for help.
Jack 旅行的第三天就把錢用完了，所以他只好打電話向父母求助。
look out!: Look out, there is a big hole in the road right in front of you, and you might fall in.
小心！你前面的路上有一個大洞，你可能會跌進去。
watch out for cars: Always watch out for cars when you cross the street, even if the light is green for you.
過馬路時一定要小心車輛，即使你這邊是綠燈也一樣。
point out the mistake: The teacher kindly pointed out the mistake in my English report, so I fixed it before I handed it in.
老師親切地指出我英文報告裡的錯誤，所以我在交出去之前把它改好了。
pick out a gift: It took Amy an hour at the mall to pick out a gift for her mother's birthday this Sunday.
Amy 在購物中心花了一個小時，為媽媽這星期天的生日挑選禮物。
try out the new bike: Dad let me try out the new bike in the park on Saturday, and it rode much faster than my old one.
星期六爸爸讓我在公園試用新腳踏車，它騎起來比我的舊車快多了。
take out the trash: It is my job to take out the trash every evening before the truck comes at seven o'clock.
每天晚上七點垃圾車來之前倒垃圾是我的工作。
eat out: My family eats out only once a month because my mother thinks home-cooked food is healthier and cheaper.
我們家一個月只外食一次，因為媽媽認為家裡煮的食物比較健康又便宜。
hang out with friends: After the exam, I want to hang out with friends at the night market and eat lots of delicious snacks.
考完試後，我想和朋友去夜市出去玩，吃很多好吃的小吃。
help out: When my mother was sick last week, my aunt came over every day to help out with the cooking and the housework.
上週媽媽生病時，阿姨每天都過來幫忙煮飯和做家事。
check out of the hotel: We have to check out of the hotel before eleven, so let us pack our bags right after breakfast.
我們必須在十一點前退房，所以吃完早餐馬上來整理行李吧。
check out the book: You can check out the book from the school library for two weeks, but you must return it on time.
你可以從學校圖書館借出這本書兩個星期，但必須準時歸還。
carry out the plan: The class decided to carry out the plan for the clean-up day, so everyone brought gloves and big bags.
全班決定執行清掃日的計畫，所以每個人都帶了手套和大袋子。
break out (fire, war): A fire broke out in the kitchen of the restaurant last night, but luckily nobody was hurt at all.
昨晚那家餐廳的廚房爆發了火災，但幸好完全沒有人受傷。
cut out sugar: The doctor told my father to cut out sugar, so now he drinks black coffee and eats no cake.
醫生要我爸爸戒糖，所以他現在喝黑咖啡，也不吃蛋糕。
fill out the form: Please fill out the form with your name, phone number, and address before you join the swimming class.
加入游泳班之前，請在表格上填上你的姓名、電話和地址。
leave out a word: When I copied the sentence from the board, I left out a word, so it did not make any sense.
我從黑板上抄句子時漏掉了一個字，所以句子完全說不通。
set out: Our family set out for Taichung early in the morning so that we could get there before the traffic got heavy.
我們家一大早就出發前往台中，好在交通變擁擠之前抵達。
stand out: Lily's red dress really stood out at the party because everyone else was wearing black or white.
Lily 的紅色洋裝在派對上真的很突出，因為其他人都穿黑色或白色。
speak out: If you think the new rule is not fair, you should speak out at the class meeting instead of saying nothing.
如果你覺得新規定不公平，應該在班會上大聲說出來，而不是什麼都不說。
sell out: The tickets for the singer's show sold out in ten minutes, so many of her fans were very sad.
那位歌手演出的門票十分鐘內就賣完了，所以她的許多粉絲都很難過。
sold out: We got to the bakery at noon, but the chocolate cake was already sold out, so we bought cookies instead.
我們中午到了麵包店，但巧克力蛋糕已經售完，所以我們改買了餅乾。
wear out: Peter plays basketball every day, so he wears out a pair of shoes in only three or four months.
Peter 每天打籃球，所以他三、四個月就會穿壞一雙鞋。
burn out: My cousin studied until two every night for a year, and in the end he burned out and got sick.
我表哥一整年每晚都讀到兩點，最後他累垮了，還生了病。
die out: Many kinds of animals may die out if people keep cutting down the forests they live in.
如果人們繼續砍伐動物居住的森林，許多種動物可能會絕種。
drop out of school: Grandpa had to drop out of school at fifteen to help his family, but he never stopped reading.
爺爺十五歲時為了幫忙家裡不得不輟學，但他從未停止閱讀。
keep out: The sign on the door says Keep Out, so we should not go into that room without a teacher.
門上的牌子寫著「禁止進入」，所以沒有老師陪同我們不該進那間房間。
lock out: I forgot my keys this morning and locked myself out, so I waited outside until Mom came home.
今天早上我忘了帶鑰匙，把自己鎖在外面，所以我在外面等到媽媽回家。
let out the dog: Every morning before school, I let out the dog so that it can run around in the yard for a while.
每天早上上學前，我都會放狗出去，讓它在院子裡跑一會兒。
let out a cry: The little girl let out a cry when she saw a big spider on her bed in the dark room.
小女孩在黑暗的房間裡看到床上有一隻大蜘蛛時大叫了一聲。
make out: It was so dark in the forest that we could hardly make out the path in front of us.
森林裡太暗了，我們幾乎看不清前面的小路。
pass out: It was so hot at the sports meet that one student passed out and had to be carried to the nurse.
運動會當天太熱了，有一個學生昏倒，必須被抬去保健室護士那裡。
rule out: The doctor ruled out a cold after checking my throat, and said I just needed more sleep.
醫生檢查了我的喉嚨後排除了感冒的可能，說我只是需要多睡一點。
shut out: Jenny closed the window and shut out the noise from the street so that she could study for the test.
Jenny 關上窗戶，把街上的噪音隔絕在外，好讓她能準備考試。
sort out: My desk was full of old papers, so on Sunday afternoon I had to sort out everything and throw some away.
我的桌子堆滿了舊紙張，所以星期天下午我得整理所有東西，並丟掉一些。
spread out: The teacher told us to spread out across the playground so that we would have enough space to dance.
老師叫我們在操場上散開，這樣我們才有足夠的空間跳舞。
stay out late: My parents do not let me stay out late on school nights, so I must be home by nine.
我爸媽不讓我上學日晚歸，所以我九點前必須回家。
stick out: A piece of paper sticks out of your book, so be careful or it might fall out on the bus.
有一張紙從你的書裡突出來，小心一點，否則它可能會在公車上掉出來。
take sb. out to dinner: On Mother's Day, my brother and I took Mom out to dinner at her favorite Japanese restaurant.
母親節那天，我和哥哥帶媽媽到她最愛的日本餐廳吃晚餐。
think out: Before you answer the question, think it out carefully, because you only have one chance to get it right.
回答問題之前，先仔細想清楚，因為你只有一次答對的機會。
throw out: Mom asked me to throw out the old shoes in the closet because nobody has worn them for years.
媽媽叫我把衣櫃裡的舊鞋丟掉，因為已經好幾年沒有人穿了。
clean out the room: Before the new student moves in, we need to clean out the room and take away all the old boxes.
在新學生搬進來之前，我們需要清空房間，把所有的舊箱子搬走。
read out loud: The teacher asked each of us to read out loud one part of the story in front of the class.
老師請我們每個人在全班面前大聲讀出故事的一段。
cry out: The boy cried out in pain when the heavy ball hit him on the nose during the game.
比賽時那顆重球打到男孩的鼻子，他痛得大叫。
back out: Tom said he would join our team for the race, but he backed out at the last minute because he was scared.
Tom 說他會加入我們的隊伍參加比賽，但在最後一刻因為害怕退出了。
branch out: The small bakery on our street used to sell only bread, but now it has branched out into cakes and coffee.
我們這條街上的小麵包店以前只賣麵包，但現在已經擴展到賣蛋糕和咖啡了。
bring out: The phone company will bring out a new phone next month, and my brother already wants to buy it.
那家手機公司下個月將推出新手機，我哥哥已經想買了。
call out: The teacher called out my name three times before I finally heard her and stood up.
老師大喊了我的名字三次，我才終於聽到並站起來。
count out: Do not count me out of the game just because I am short; I can run faster than anyone here.
別因為我矮就把我從比賽中排除；我跑得比這裡任何人都快。
dry out: Leave your wet shoes near the window so that they can dry out before school tomorrow morning.
把你的濕鞋子放在窗邊，讓它們在明天早上上學前乾掉。
Kevin fell out with his best friend over a video game, and they did not talk for two whole weeks.
Kevin 因為一個電動遊戲和他最好的朋友吵翻了，他們整整兩個星期沒有說話。
get out of the car: When we got out of the car at the top of the mountain, we could see the whole city below us.
當我們在山頂下車時，可以看到整座城市在我們下方。
get out of doing: My little brother always tries to get out of doing the dishes by saying he has too much homework.
我弟弟總是說他有太多作業，想藉此逃避洗碗。
grow out of one's clothes: My little brother grows so fast that he grew out of his clothes again, and Mom had to buy new ones.
我弟弟長得太快了，他又長大穿不下他的衣服，媽媽只好買新的。
hold out: The small team held out until the last minute of the game, even though the other team was much stronger.
這支小隊伍堅持到比賽的最後一分鐘，即使對手強多了。
knock out: In the movie, the hero knocked out the bad man with one hit and then saved the little girl.
電影裡，英雄一拳就擊倒了壞人，然後救了小女孩。
lay out: Before the party, Mom laid out all the plates, cups, and snacks on the long table in the living room.
派對前，媽媽把所有的盤子、杯子和點心擺放在客廳的長桌上。
look out for: My older sister always looks out for me at school, and she tells me which students are not friendly.
我姊姊在學校總是照顧我，她會告訴我哪些學生不友善。
miss out on: If you stay home playing video games all weekend, you will miss out on the fun at the beach with us.
如果你整個週末都待在家裡玩電動，就會錯過和我們在海邊的樂趣。
move out: My cousin moved out of his parents' house last month and now lives in a small apartment near his office.
我表哥上個月從父母家搬出去，現在住在他辦公室附近的小公寓。
play out: Nobody knew how the final game would play out, because both teams were strong and had never lost this year.
沒有人知道決賽會怎麼進行，因為兩隊都很強，今年都還沒輸過。
print out: I need to print out my report before class because our teacher wants a paper copy, not an email.
我上課前需要把報告印出來，因為老師要紙本，不要電子郵件。
reach out: When Lisa felt lonely at her new school, she reached out to the girl next to her and asked to be friends.
Lisa 在新學校感到孤單時，她主動聯繫坐在旁邊的女孩，問她能不能當朋友。
ring out: The school bell rang out at four, and hundreds of happy students ran out through the front gate.
四點時學校鐘聲響起，數百名開心的學生從大門跑了出去。
run out: When we heard the fire bell, everyone ran out of the building and waited quietly on the playground.
聽到火警鈴聲時，所有人都跑出大樓，安靜地在操場上等待。
see sb. out: After the party ended, Grandma saw each guest out and gave everyone a small box of cookies.
派對結束後，奶奶送每位客人到門口，還給每個人一小盒餅乾。
show sb. out: The meeting was over, so the manager thanked us and asked a worker to show us out of the office.
會議結束了，所以經理向我們道謝，並請一位員工送我們出辦公室。
single out: The teacher singled out Mary for her hard work and asked the class to give her a big hand.
老師特別挑出 Mary 來稱讚她的努力，並請全班給她熱烈的掌聲。
sit out: Because of his hurt leg, Jack had to sit out the soccer game and watch his team from the side.
因為腿受傷，Jack 只能坐著不參加足球賽，在場邊看他的隊伍比賽。
sleep out: Last summer my friends and I slept out under the stars in Grandpa's yard and talked until midnight.
去年夏天，我和朋友在爺爺家的院子裡在外過夜，睡在星空下，聊到半夜。
start out: Our teacher started out as a nurse, but she later found that she loved teaching children much more.
我們的老師一開始是護士，但她後來發現自己更喜歡教小孩。
talk sb. out of doing: Jenny wanted to cut her long hair short, but her best friend talked her out of doing it.
Jenny 想把長髮剪短，但她最好的朋友說服她不要剪。
turn out the light: Please turn out the light when you leave the bathroom because we need to save energy this month.
你離開浴室時請關燈，因為我們這個月需要省電。
walk out: The workers at the factory walked out this morning because they have not been paid for two months.
工廠的工人今天早上罷工走出去了，因為他們已經兩個月沒有領到薪水。
wash out: Some orange juice got on my white shirt, but luckily it washed out after I used some cold water.
我的白襯衫沾到了一些橘子汁，但幸好用冷水沖一沖就沖掉了。
win out: In the end, hard work won out over good luck, and the small school team took home the big prize.
最後，努力勝過了好運，這支小學校的隊伍帶回了大獎。
out of breath: After running up the stairs to the top floor, I was so out of breath that I could not speak.
跑上樓梯到頂樓之後，我喘不過氣，連話都說不出來。
out of sight: The little boy waved to his mother until her bus turned the corner and was out of sight.
小男孩向媽媽揮手，直到她的公車轉過街角看不見為止。
out of mind: Out of sight, out of mind, as people say, so I put the candy on a shelf I cannot see.
人們常說眼不見就忘記，所以我把糖果放到看不到的最上層架子。
out of control: The kids got out of control at the birthday party, running around and shouting while the parents talked.
孩子們在生日派對上失控，爸媽聊天時他們到處奔跑大叫。
out of danger: The doctor told us that Grandpa was out of danger after a long night, and we all cried with joy.
醫生告訴我們爺爺經過漫長的一夜後已經脫離危險，我們都高興地哭了。
out of fashion: Those jeans were very popular five years ago, but now they are out of fashion, so nobody wears them.
那種牛仔褲五年前很流行，但現在退流行了，所以沒有人穿。
out of money: I am out of money this week because I spent it all on a new pair of basketball shoes.
我這星期沒錢了，因為我把錢全部花在一雙新的籃球鞋上。
out of time: We are out of time for today, so please finish the last two questions at home and bring them tomorrow.
今天時間不夠了，所以請在家把最後兩題寫完，明天帶來。
out of place: In his heavy winter coat, Tom looked out of place at the beach, where everyone else was in T-shirts.
Tom 穿著厚重的冬天外套，在大家都穿 T 恤的海邊看起來很不合適。
out of reach: Mom keeps the medicine on a high shelf so that it is out of reach of my little brother.
媽媽把藥放在高的架子上，好讓我弟弟拿不到。
out of the question: Going to the late movie on a school night is out of the question, so do not even ask Dad again.
上學日晚上去看晚場電影是不可能的，所以別再問爸爸了。
out of town: My father will be out of town on business this week, so Mom and I will eat dinner alone.
我爸爸這星期出城辦事，所以媽媽和我要單獨吃晚餐。
out of the way: Please move your bike out of the way because the old lady cannot get past it with her bags.
請把你的腳踏車移開別礙事，因為那位老太太提著袋子過不去。
out of the blue: Out of the blue, my old friend from Taipei called me last night, and we talked for two hours.
昨晚我在台北的老朋友突然打電話給我，我們聊了兩個小時。
out of shape: After a winter of sitting on the sofa, Dad is really out of shape and gets tired after a short walk.
在沙發上坐了一個冬天後，爸爸的身體真的走樣了，走一小段路就累。
out of luck: You are out of luck today because the last two tickets for the movie were sold a minute ago.
你今天運氣不好，因為電影的最後兩張票一分鐘前剛賣掉。
out of practice: I used to play the piano well, but I am out of practice now, so my fingers feel slow.
我以前鋼琴彈得很好，但現在久未練習，所以手指感覺很遲鈍。
out of print: The book I wanted is out of print now, so I have to look for a used copy in old bookstores.
我想要的那本書現在絕版了，所以我得去二手書店找舊的。
out of trouble: Grandma always tells me to stay out of trouble at school and to be kind to my teachers.
奶奶總是叮嚀我在學校要遠離麻煩、不要惹事，並對老師友善。
out of kindness: The old man fixed our bike out of kindness and would not take any money from us for his help.
那位老先生出於善意幫我們修腳踏車，不肯收我們任何錢。
out of respect: Out of respect for their teacher, all the students stood up and bowed when she walked into the room.
出於對老師的尊敬，老師走進教室時全體學生都站起來行禮。
out of fear: The little dog hid under the bed out of fear when it heard the loud thunder outside.
小狗聽到外面響亮的雷聲時，出於恐懼躲到床底下。
out of habit: Even on Sunday, Dad gets up at six out of habit and makes coffee for everyone in the family.
即使在星期天，爸爸也出於習慣六點起床，為家裡每個人煮咖啡。
out of pity: Out of pity, the girl bought a sandwich for the hungry man sitting outside the train station.
女孩出於同情，買了一個三明治給坐在火車站外的飢餓男子。
three out of ten: Three out of ten students in our class wear glasses, and most of them read too much on their phones.
我們班十分之三的學生戴眼鏡，而且他們大多在手機上看太多東西。
one out of five: Only one out of five students in our school eats breakfast every day, which worries the school nurse.
我們學校只有五分之一的學生每天吃早餐，這讓校護很擔心。
out loud: When I read the funny story out loud, my whole family laughed so hard that Grandma had tears in her eyes.
當我大聲地讀出那個有趣的故事時，全家人笑得很厲害，奶奶都笑出眼淚了。
out there: It is raining hard out there, so please take an umbrella with you before you leave for school.
外面在那裡下著大雨，所以你出門上學前請帶把傘。
be out: My mother is out right now because she went to the supermarket, but she will be back before dinner.
我媽媽現在外出了，因為她去超市，不過晚餐前她就會回來。
After three days of heavy rain, the sun is out at last, and the children are running happily in the park.
下了三天大雨之後，太陽終於出來了，孩子們開心地在公園裡奔跑。
The fire is out now, so we can leave the camp safely and walk back to the hotel together.
火現在熄了，所以我們可以安全地離開營地，一起走回飯店。
When school is out at four o'clock, Jenny usually buys a cup of milk tea before she goes home.
四點放學的時候，珍妮通常會先買一杯奶茶再回家。
Time is out, so please put down your pens and hand in your test papers to the teacher now.
時間到了，所以請放下你們的筆，現在把考卷交給老師。
be out of school: When we are out of school this afternoon, let's go to the night market and try some new food.
我們今天下午放學後，一起去夜市試試一些新食物吧。
be out of bed: On Sunday mornings, Peter is never out of bed before ten, because he likes to sleep late on weekends.
星期天早上，彼得十點前從不起床，因為他喜歡在週末睡晚一點。
be out of hospital: My grandfather has been out of hospital for a week, and he already feels strong enough to take short walks.
我爺爺已經出院一星期了，他已經覺得身體夠好，可以散散步了。
be out of town: Mr. Lin will be out of town for three days next week, so another teacher will teach our English class.
林老師下星期將有三天不在城裡，所以會有另一位老師來教我們的英文課。
out and about: After a long week of tests, it feels great to be out and about in the warm sun with my friends.
經過一整週的考試後，和朋友們在陽光下外出活動，感覺真棒。
out of my way: Get out of my way, please, because I am carrying a heavy box and I cannot see the stairs clearly.
請別擋路，因為我正抱著一個很重的箱子，看不清楚樓梯。
get out of here: The movie was so boring that my brother said we should get out of here and buy some ice cream instead.
這部電影太無聊了，我哥哥說我們應該離開這裡，改去買些冰淇淋。
way out: When the lights went off in the shopping mall, everyone looked for the way out and walked slowly to the door.
購物中心的燈熄滅時，大家都在找出口，然後慢慢走向門口。
look out of the window: During the long math class, Amy often looks out of the window and watches the birds in the trees.
在漫長的數學課上，艾咪常常看窗外，看著樹上的小鳥。
out of the window: I could see the whole city out of the window of the train, and the lights at night were beautiful.
我可以從火車的窗外看到整個城市，夜晚的燈光很美。
out of nowhere: A big dog came out of nowhere and ran across the street, so the driver had to stop the car quickly.
一隻大狗突然冒出來，跑過街道，所以駕駛必須趕快停車。
out of (離開內部) vs. off (離開表面): Tom walked out of the kitchen with a plate of cookies and then took a book off the shelf for me.
湯姆拿著一盤餅乾從廚房走出去，然後從架上拿了一本書給我。
get out of the car vs. get off the bus: Mom told me to get out of the car at the station, and then we got off the bus near the museum.
媽媽叫我在車站下汽車，然後我們在博物館附近下了公車。
out of work (失業) vs. off work (下班): Uncle Ted has been out of work since March, but he plays basketball with us when we are off work.
泰德叔叔從三月起就失業了，但我們下班後，他會和我們打籃球。
out of order (故障) vs. in order (有序): The school printer is out of order again, but the books in the library are in order, so we found ours quickly.
學校的印表機又故障了，但圖書館的書井然有序，所以我們很快就找到我們要的書。
out of date (過時) vs. up to date (最新): This map is out of date, so let's check the map on my phone, which is up to date, before we leave.
這張地圖過時了，所以我們出發前先查一下我手機上最新的地圖吧。
out of (用完) vs. without (沒有): We are out of milk at home, so Dad had to drink his coffee without any milk this morning.
我們家的牛奶用完了，所以爸爸今天早上只好喝沒有牛奶的咖啡。
run out of (用完) vs. run out (跑出去): We ran out of rice at dinner, so my little brother ran out to the store on the corner to buy some.
晚餐時我們的米用完了，所以我弟弟跑出去到轉角的商店買了一些。
look out (小心) vs. look out of (往外看): Look out, there is a car coming, so stop looking out of the window and move back to the sidewalk!
小心，有車來了，別再往窗外看，退回到人行道上！
find out (查明) vs. find (找到): I could not find my keys anywhere, but later I found out that my sister had put them in her bag.
我到處都找不到鑰匙，不過後來我查明是我姊姊把它們放進了她的包包。
turn out (結果是) vs. turn on: We were worried about the picnic, but it turned out to be sunny, so Mom turned on the radio and we sang.
我們很擔心野餐，但結果是晴天，所以媽媽開了收音機，我們一起唱歌。
put out (撲滅) vs. put off (延後): The workers put out the fire in the old factory quickly, but the school still put off the sports meeting until Friday.
工人們很快撲滅了舊工廠的火，但學校仍然把運動會延後到星期五。
out (副詞) vs. out of (介係詞): It was hot inside, so we went out for a walk and then sat out of the sun under a big tree.
裡面很熱，所以我們出去散步，然後坐在一棵大樹下避開太陽。
go out (非 go out of the door 省略): It is a beautiful evening, so let's go out and take a walk by the river after we finish dinner.
今晚天氣很好，所以我們吃完晚餐後出去到河邊散散步吧。
out of the window (非 out the window): From my seat on the plane, I looked out of the window and saw the mountains covered with white snow.
我從飛機上的座位往窗外看，看見覆蓋著白雪的山脈。
outside the school: Every morning, a kind old man sells hot breakfast outside the school, and many students buy sandwiches from him.
每天早上，一位親切的老先生在學校外面賣熱早餐，很多學生向他買三明治。
wait outside the door: Please wait outside the door for a few minutes, because the doctor is still talking with another patient inside.
請在門外等幾分鐘，因為醫生還在裡面和另一位病人談話。
play outside: When the weather is warm and sunny, my little cousins love to play outside until it gets dark.
天氣溫暖晴朗時，我的小表弟妹喜歡在外面玩，直到天黑。
outside the city: My grandfather and grandmother live on a quiet farm outside the city, and we visit them every Chinese New Year.
我的祖父母住在城外一座安靜的農場，我們每年農曆新年都去拜訪他們。
outside the box: Mom wrote my name outside the box so that nobody would take my lunch by mistake at school.
媽媽把我的名字寫在盒子外面，這樣在學校就不會有人誤拿我的午餐。
from outside: We heard a loud noise from outside, so Dad opened the door to see what was happening on the street.
我們聽到從外面傳來很大的聲音，所以爸爸開門看看街上發生了什麼事。
go outside: The room was too hot, so the teacher let us go outside and read our books under the trees.
房間太熱了，所以老師讓我們出去外面，在樹下看書。
the outside of the house: The outside of the house looks old and gray, but inside it is clean, bright, and very comfortable.
這棟房子的外側看起來又舊又灰，但裡面乾淨、明亮，而且非常舒適。
outside school hours: Students may use the computer room outside school hours, but they must sign their names on the list first.
學生可以在非上課時間使用電腦教室，但必須先在名單上簽名。
outside of work: Outside of work, my father likes to go fishing with his friends and cook what he catches for us.
工作以外，我爸爸喜歡和朋友去釣魚，然後把他釣到的魚煮給我們吃。
think outside the box: Our teacher told us to think outside the box, so our group made a short movie instead of writing a report.
我們老師叫我們跳脫框架思考，所以我們這組拍了一部短片，而不是寫報告。
an outside chance: Our team has only an outside chance of winning the final game, but we will still try our best on Saturday.
我們隊贏得決賽的機會微小，但星期六我們仍然會盡力。
outside help: The small school could not fix the broken roof by itself, so it asked for outside help from the city.
這所小學校無法自己修好破損的屋頂，所以向市政府請求外部援助。
on the outside: The cake looks a little dark on the outside, but when you cut it open, it is light and sweet inside.
這個蛋糕在外面看起來有點黑，但切開後裡面又鬆軟又甜。
outside the law: In the story, the thief thinks he can live outside the law, but the police finally catch him in the end.
在故事裡，小偷以為自己可以不受法律管束，但警察最後還是抓到了他。
outside my experience: Cooking a big dinner for twenty people is outside my experience, so I asked my aunt to help me.
為二十個人煮一頓大餐超出我的經驗，所以我請阿姨來幫我。
fly over the city: When the airplane began to fly over the city, we could see the tall buildings and the long river below.
飛機開始飛越城市時，我們可以看到下方高高的建築和長長的河。
jump over the fence: The ball went into the neighbor's yard, so my brother had to jump over the fence to get it back.
球飛進鄰居的院子，所以我哥哥必須跳過圍籬去把它撿回來。
a bridge over the river: There is a long bridge over the river near my school, and I ride my bicycle across it every day.
我學校附近有一座河上的長橋，我每天騎腳踏車經過它。
climb over the wall: The boys tried to climb over the wall to get their kite, but the teacher told them it was dangerous.
男孩們想爬過牆去拿他們的風箏，但老師告訴他們那樣很危險。
over the hill: My grandmother's village is just over the hill, so we can walk there in about twenty minutes.
我奶奶的村子就在翻過山丘的地方，所以我們走大約二十分鐘就能到。
all over the world: People all over the world love to eat noodles, and each country cooks them in a different way.
全世界的人都愛吃麵，而且每個國家煮麵的方式都不同。
all over the floor: When my baby sister dropped the bag of rice, there was rice all over the floor of the kitchen.
我的小妹妹把那袋米掉在地上時，廚房的地上滿地都是米。
over there: The bus stop is over there, next to the post office, so you only need to cross the street.
公車站在那邊，就在郵局旁邊，所以你只需要過馬路。
over here: Come over here and sit next to me, because there is enough space on this bench for two people.
過來這邊坐在我旁邊，因為這張長椅上有足夠的空間坐兩個人。
look over the wall: The little boy stood on a chair to look over the wall and watch the children playing next door.
小男孩站在椅子上從牆上往那邊看，看著隔壁的孩子們玩耍。
a roof over my head: After the typhoon, many families lost their houses, and they were happy just to have a roof over their heads.
颱風過後，許多家庭失去了房子，他們只要有地方住就很開心了。
put a blanket over him: My little brother fell asleep on the sofa, so Mom put a blanket over him and turned off the light.
我弟弟在沙發上睡著了，所以媽媽給他蓋上毯子，然後關了燈。
a lamp over the table: There is a bright lamp over the table in the kitchen, so we can see our food clearly at dinner.
廚房的桌子上方有一盞明亮的燈，所以我們晚餐時可以清楚看到食物。
hang over the city: Dark clouds began to hang over the city in the afternoon, and soon heavy rain fell on the streets.
下午烏雲開始籠罩城市，很快大雨就落在街道上。
the sky over the sea: The sky over the sea turned orange and pink in the evening, and everyone on the beach took pictures of it.
傍晚時海上的天空變成橙色和粉紅色，海灘上的每個人都拍了照。
over the road: The new bakery is just over the road from our school, so we often buy fresh bread there after class.
新的麵包店就在我們學校的馬路對面，所以我們放學後常去那裡買新鮮麵包。
live over the shop: My aunt and uncle live over the shop where they sell fruit, so they never need to drive to work.
我阿姨和姨丈住在他們賣水果的店面樓上，所以他們從不需要開車上班。
fall over: The floor was wet after the rain, and the old man almost fell over when he walked into the store.
雨後地板是濕的，老先生走進店裡時差點跌倒。
knock over the glass: Be careful with your arm, or you will knock over the glass of juice next to your plate again.
小心你的手臂，否則你又會打翻你盤子旁邊那杯果汁。
turn over the page: When you finish reading this page, turn over the page and answer the ten questions on the other side.
你讀完這一頁後，翻頁並回答另一面的十個問題。
roll over: The puppy likes to roll over on the grass when we come home, because it wants us to rub its stomach.
我們回家時，小狗喜歡在草地上翻身，因為它想要我們摸摸它的肚子。
cross over the street: Always look both ways before you cross over the street, even when the light is green for you.
過馬路穿越街道前一定要左右看，即使你的燈是綠燈。
spread over the land: After many years, the farmer's small apple trees spread over the land and covered the whole hill with flowers.
多年後，農夫的小蘋果樹散布於整片土地，讓整座山丘開滿了花。
over the weekend: Over the weekend, my family drove to Taichung to visit my grandmother and eat her famous dumplings.
在週末期間，我們全家開車去台中拜訪奶奶，吃她有名的水餃。
over the years: Over the years, the small fishing village has changed into a busy town with hotels and tall buildings.
這些年來，這個小漁村已經變成一個有飯店和高樓的熱鬧城鎮。
over lunch: We talked about our summer plans over lunch, and everyone agreed to go camping by the lake in July.
我們在午餐時聊到暑假計畫，大家都同意七月去湖邊露營。
over the holidays: Over the holidays, Lisa read five books and learned to make three kinds of cookies with her mother.
假期期間，麗莎讀了五本書，還和媽媽學會做三種餅乾。
over night: The weather changed over night, and when we woke up, the mountains were covered with white snow.
天氣一夜之間變了，我們醒來時，山上覆蓋著白雪。
over a cup of coffee: My parents like to talk about their day over a cup of coffee after my sister and I go to bed.
我和姊姊上床睡覺後，我爸媽喜歡邊喝咖啡邊聊他們的一天。
over the past week: Over the past week, I have practiced the piano every evening, so I feel ready for the piano show tomorrow.
過去一週，我每天晚上都練鋼琴，所以我覺得已準備好明天的鋼琴表演。
over time: Learning a language is hard at first, but over time you will understand more and speak with less fear.
學語言一開始很難，但隨著時間過去，你會聽懂更多，說話也比較不怕。
over the next few days: The weather report says it will rain over the next few days, so we may need to change our picnic plans.
天氣預報說接下來幾天會下雨，所以我們可能需要改變野餐計畫。
over the summer: Over the summer, my cousin worked at a tea shop and saved enough money to buy a new bicycle.
暑假期間，我表哥在茶飲店打工，存了足夠的錢買一輛新腳踏車。
over 100 people: Over 100 people came to the school music show last night, and there were not enough chairs for everyone.
昨晚有超過一百人來參加學校的音樂表演，椅子不夠讓每個人坐。
over ten years old: Children over ten years old must buy a full ticket, but younger kids can enter the zoo for free.
十歲以上的孩童必須買全票，但更小的孩子可以免費進動物園。
over 60 kilometers an hour: Dad never drives over 60 kilometers an hour on this road, because there is a school and many children nearby.
爸爸在這條路上從不開到時速超過六十公里，因為附近有學校和很多小孩。
talk over the phone: My grandmother lives far away in Tainan, so we usually talk over the phone every Sunday evening.
我奶奶住在很遠的台南，所以我們通常每個星期天晚上透過電話聊天。
hear it over the radio: We heard about the big typhoon over the radio while we were driving home from the beach.
我們從海邊開車回家時，從廣播聽到了大颱風的消息。
over the Internet: During the summer, our teacher taught the class over the Internet, and we asked questions by typing them.
暑假期間，我們老師透過網路上課，我們用打字的方式提問。
over and over again: The little girl watched the same cartoon over and over again, and she could sing every song in it.
小女孩一再地看同一部卡通，她能唱出裡面的每一首歌。
be over: The test will be over at eleven, and after that we can finally enjoy our long winter vacation.
考試十一點會結束，之後我們終於可以享受漫長的寒假了。
The game is over, and our school team won by two points, so all the students are cheering loudly.
比賽結束了，我們的校隊以兩分獲勝，所以所有學生都在大聲歡呼。
When the last song finished and the lights came on, the singer smiled and said that it's all over.
最後一首歌結束、燈亮起時，歌手微笑著說全都結束了。
get over a cold: Drink a lot of warm water and sleep early, and you will get over your cold in a few days.
多喝溫開水並早點睡，幾天後你的感冒就會痊癒。
get over the shock: It took my mother several days to get over the shock of seeing our car hit by a truck.
我媽媽花了好幾天才從看到我們的車被卡車撞到的驚嚇中恢復。
think it over: You do not have to answer today, so think it over carefully and tell me your decision next week.
你不必今天回答，所以仔細考慮後，下星期再告訴我你的決定。
talk it over: Instead of being angry with each other, you and your brother should sit down and talk it over calmly.
你和你弟弟不要互相生氣，應該坐下來好好冷靜談談。
look over the report: Could you look over the report for me before I give it to the teacher this afternoon?
在我今天下午把報告交給老師之前，你可以幫我瀏覽一下報告嗎？
go over the notes: Before the big test, Kevin spent two hours going over the notes he took in science class.
大考前，凱文花了兩個小時複習他在自然課上做的筆記。
take over the business: When my grandfather got too old to work, my father decided to take over the business and run the restaurant.
我爺爺年紀太大無法工作時，我爸爸決定接管生意，經營餐廳。
hand over the money: In the movie, the robber told the bank clerk to hand over the money, but the police arrived just in time.
電影裡，搶匪叫銀行職員交出錢，但警察及時趕到。
come over to my house: Why don't you come over to my house after school, and we can play video games and eat pizza together?
你放學後何不來我家，我們可以一起打電動、吃披薩？
run over the dog: The driver almost ran over the dog that suddenly ran into the road, but he stopped the car just in time.
那隻狗突然跑到路上，駕駛差點撞到它，但他及時停下了車。
turn over a new leaf: After he failed the test, Jack decided to turn over a new leaf and study for one hour every night.
考試不及格後，傑克決定改過自新，每天晚上讀書一小時。
over my dead body: Dad said that my brother would ride a motorcycle to school over his dead body, so my brother takes the bus.
爸爸說除非他死，否則我哥哥別想騎機車上學，所以我哥哥搭公車。
over the moon: Mary was over the moon when she heard that she had won first prize in the English speech game at school.
瑪麗聽到自己在學校英語演講比賽得到第一名時，非常高興。
over the top: The birthday party with three cakes and a hundred balloons was a little over the top for a two-year-old.
有三個蛋糕和一百個氣球的生日派對，對一個兩歲小孩來說有點太過頭了。
over the limit: The driver was over the limit and drove too fast, so the police stopped him and gave him a ticket.
那位駕駛超過限度、開得太快，所以警察把他攔下來並開了罰單。
fight over money: It is sad when brothers fight over money, because family is much more important than a few dollars.
兄弟為錢爭吵很令人難過，因為家人比幾塊錢重要得多。
argue over a small thing: My sisters often argue over a small thing like who gets the bigger piece of cake after dinner.
我的姊妹們常為小事爭論，像是晚餐後誰拿到比較大塊的蛋糕。
worry over: Please do not worry over the test too much, because you have studied hard and you are ready for it.
請不要太擔心考試，因為你已經很用功了，而且你已經準備好了。
be over the hill: Grandpa says he is over the hill now, but he still rides his bicycle to the park every morning.
爺爺說他現在已過壯年，但他每天早上仍然騎腳踏車去公園。
do it over: My writing on the card was so bad that Mom asked me to do it over on a new piece of paper.
我在卡片上的字寫得太醜了，媽媽要我在一張新的紙上重做一次。
start over: The computer stopped working and I lost my report, so I had to start over from the first sentence.
電腦停止運作，我的報告也不見了，所以我必須從第一句重新開始。
stay over: It was raining too hard to go home, so my aunt let me stay over at her apartment for the night.
雨太大無法回家，所以我阿姨讓我在她的公寓過夜。
sleep over: On Friday night, my best friend will sleep over at my house, and we plan to watch three movies together.
星期五晚上，我最好的朋友會在我家過夜，我們打算一起看三部電影。
pull over: When the baby started crying in the back seat, Dad decided to pull over and check what was wrong.
寶寶在後座開始哭時，爸爸決定把車停到路邊，看看出了什麼問題。
win sb. over: At first my parents said no to a pet, but my little sister finally won them over with her sweet smile.
一開始我爸媽不同意養寵物，但我妹妹最後用甜甜的笑容贏得了他們的支持。
hand it over: The teacher saw Tom playing with his phone in class and told him to hand it over until the bell rang.
老師看見湯姆在課堂上玩手機，叫他把手機交出來，直到下課鐘響。
take it over: My father was too tired to finish cooking dinner, so my mother decided to take it over and make soup.
我爸爸太累了，煮不完晚餐，所以我媽媽決定接手，做了湯。
all over again: I pushed the wrong button and lost the whole game, so now I have to play all over again from level one.
我按錯按鍵，整個遊戲都沒了，所以現在我必須從第一關再重來一遍。
left over: There was a lot of rice and chicken left over after the party, so we ate it for lunch the next day.
派對後剩下很多飯和雞肉，所以我們隔天午餐就吃那些。
head over heels: My cousin is head over heels in love with a girl in his class, and he talks about her all day long.
我表哥對班上的一個女孩神魂顛倒，他整天都在談她。
over the long run: Riding a bicycle to school may seem slow, but over the long run it will save you money and keep you healthy.
騎腳踏車上學可能看起來很慢，但長遠來看，它能幫你省錢並保持健康。
over the edge: Losing his job and then his car almost pushed the poor man over the edge, but his friends helped him.
失去工作後又失去車子，差點讓這個可憐的人失控，但他的朋友幫助了他。
over (跨越上方／覆蓋) vs. above (較高處): The plane flew over the mountains, and far above the plane, the moon shone brightly in the dark sky.
飛機越過山脈，而在飛機上方很高的地方，月亮在黑暗的天空中明亮地照耀。
jump over the wall (越過): The thief tried to jump over the wall behind the house, but a big dog in the yard started to bark.
小偷想跳過房子後面的牆，但院子裡的大狗開始叫了起來。
the clouds above us (上方): We lay on the grass after the picnic and watched the clouds above us, while birds flew over the lake.
野餐後我們躺在草地上，看著頭頂的雲，同時鳥兒飛越湖面。
over (越過) vs. across (橫越表面) vs. through: We walked over the small hill, went across the wide field, and finally ran through the dark woods to the lake.
我們越過小山丘，橫越寬闊的田野，最後穿過黑暗的森林到了湖邊。
over the bridge: Every morning, hundreds of people walk over the bridge to get to the train station on the other side.
每天早上，數百人走過橋，到另一邊的火車站。
over (超過) vs. more than: Over two hundred students joined the school trip, which means more than half of the school went to the museum.
超過兩百名學生參加了校外教學，也就是說學校超過一半的人去了博物館。
over 100: Over 100 kinds of fish live in this lake, and the fishermen there catch more than fifty of them for food.
有超過一百種魚住在這座湖裡，那裡的漁夫捕捉其中超過五十種來當食物。
over the phone vs. on the phone: Grandma told me the whole story over the phone, and she was still on the phone when Dad came home.
奶奶透過電話把整個故事告訴我，爸爸回家時她還在講電話中。
over the weekend vs. at the weekend: We painted the whole house over the weekend, and at the weekend my friends also came to visit us.
我們整個週末期間都在粉刷房子，而週末時我朋友也來拜訪我們。
over (結束) vs. finished: The movie was over at nine, and when we had finished our popcorn, we walked home under the stars.
電影九點結束，我們吃完爆米花後，就在星空下走回家。
get over (克服) vs. get through (完成；度過): It took me a month to get over my fear of water, but now I can get through a whole swimming lesson.
我花了一個月才克服對水的恐懼，但現在我可以撐過一整堂游泳課了。
look over (瀏覽) vs. look after (照顧): Could you look over my homework for mistakes while I look after my baby brother for a few minutes?
我照顧小弟弟幾分鐘的時候，你可以幫我瀏覽一下作業找找錯誤嗎？
run over (撞到) vs. run into (偶遇): Dad almost ran over a cat on the way home, and later he ran into an old friend at the gas station.
爸爸在回家的路上差點撞到一隻貓，後來他又在加油站偶遇一位老朋友。
over (介係詞) vs. above (副詞也可): A bird flew over the house, and when I looked up, I saw a plane high above in the blue sky.
一隻鳥飛越房子，當我往上看時，我看見一架飛機高高地在藍天上方。
all over (到處) vs. over (結束): There were toys all over the bedroom floor, but after the kids put them away, the hard work was finally over.
臥室地板上到處都是玩具，但孩子們把它們收好後，辛苦的工作終於結束了。
half past six: My alarm clock rings at half past six every morning, and I usually leave for school half an hour later.
我的鬧鐘每天早上六點半響，而我通常半小時後出門上學。
ten past nine: The movie starts at ten past nine, so we have twenty minutes to buy popcorn and find our seats.
電影九點十分開始，所以我們有二十分鐘可以買爆米花和找座位。
a quarter past three: School finishes at a quarter past three on Wednesdays, and then I have piano lessons until five o'clock.
星期三學校三點十五分放學，然後我上鋼琴課直到五點。
past midnight: My brother stayed up past midnight to finish his science project, so he was very sleepy in class today.
我哥哥熬夜到午夜過後才完成他的自然作業，所以他今天上課非常想睡。
It is past ten already, so please turn off the TV and brush your teeth before you go to bed.
已經十點多了，所以請關掉電視，上床睡覺前先刷牙。
for the past two weeks: For the past two weeks, it has rained every single day, and the soccer field is now full of water.
過去兩週每天都下雨，足球場現在積滿了水。
past one's best: The old basketball player is past his best now, but young fans still love to watch him play.
這位老籃球員現在巔峰已過，但年輕的粉絲仍然喜歡看他打球。
walk past the bank: Every day I walk past the bank on my way to school, and I say good morning to the guard there.
每天我上學途中都會走過銀行，並向那裡的警衛說早安。
drive past the school: Please slow down when you drive past the school, because many children cross the street at this time.
開車經過學校時請放慢速度，因為這個時候有很多小孩在過馬路。
run past me: Two boys ran past me so fast that I almost dropped my ice cream on the ground in the park.
兩個男孩從我身邊跑過，速度快得讓我差點把冰淇淋掉在公園的地上。
go past the post office: To get to the library, go past the post office and turn left at the first traffic light.
要去圖書館，先經過郵局，然後在第一個紅綠燈左轉。
just past the corner: The night market is just past the corner, so you will see the bright lights after you turn there.
夜市就在剛過轉角的地方，所以你在那裡轉彎後就會看到明亮的燈光。
the house past the church: My piano teacher lives in the house past the church, the white one with a red door and a big garden.
我的鋼琴老師住在教堂過去那間房子，就是有紅色門和大花園的白色那間。
march past: On Sports Day, every class will march past the teachers and parents before the first race begins.
運動會那天，每個班級會在第一場賽跑開始前列隊經過老師和家長面前。
the bus went past: I was still putting on my shoes when the bus went past, so I had to wait another twenty minutes.
公車開過去的時候，我還在穿鞋，所以我只好再等二十分鐘。
past (經過, 介係詞) vs. passed (動詞過去式): Jenny walked past the gym with a big smile because she had just passed her difficult math test.
珍妮笑容滿面地經過體育館，因為她剛通過了困難的數學考試。
walk past the shop: Grandma likes to walk past the shop every afternoon and look at the new dresses in the window.
奶奶喜歡每天下午走過那家商店，看看櫥窗裡的新洋裝。
He passed the test with a high score, and he walked past the teacher's desk with a big smile.
他以高分通過了考試，然後笑容滿面地走過老師的桌子。
past (時間) vs. to (差幾分): The first bus leaves at twenty past seven, and the next one comes at ten to eight, so hurry up.
第一班公車七點二十分出發，下一班七點五十分來，所以快一點。
ten past six (6:10) vs. ten to six (5:50: I told Tom to meet me at ten past six, but he came at ten to six and waited twenty minutes.
我叫湯姆六點十分和我碰面，但他五點五十分就來了，等了二十分鐘。
past (超過) vs. after (之後): It is already past nine and the shop is closed, so we will have to buy the milk after breakfast tomorrow.
已經超過九點了，商店關門了，所以我們得明天早餐後再去買牛奶。
It's past ten and my sister is still not home, so Mom keeps looking at the clock and calling her phone.
已經十點多了，我姊姊還沒回家，所以媽媽一直看時鐘，打她的手機。
past (經過身邊) vs. by (經過): A tall man hurried past me without a word, while an old lady walked slowly by and said hello.
一個高個子男人一言不發地匆匆從我身邊越過，而一位老太太慢慢經過並打了招呼。
pass by: Every evening, many people pass by our front door, and some of them wave when they go past my dog.
每天傍晚，很多人經過我們家前門，有些人經過我的狗時還會揮手。
since last week: Mr. Wang has been sick since last week, so a new teacher is teaching our English class this week.
王老師自上週起就生病了，所以這星期由新老師教我們的英文課。
since then: I met Lily at summer camp three years ago, and we have been best friends since then.
我三年前在夏令營認識莉莉，自那時起我們就一直是最好的朋友。
since childhood: My uncle has loved baseball since childhood, and he still plays with his friends every Sunday morning.
我叔叔從小就愛棒球，現在仍然每個星期天早上和朋友一起打球。
since morning: The students have been painting the school walls since morning, so they are tired but very proud.
學生們從早上起就一直在粉刷學校牆壁，所以他們很累但很自豪。
since I was ten: I have played the violin since I was ten, and now I play with the school band at every big show.
我從十歲起就開始拉小提琴，現在每場大型表演我都和校樂隊一起演奏。
ever since: Kevin fell off his bicycle last year, and ever since he has been very careful on the road.
凱文去年從腳踏車上摔下來，從那以後他在路上就一直非常小心。
long since: The old factory by the river has long since closed, and now the building is a popular art center.
河邊的那座舊工廠很久以前就已關閉，現在這棟建築是一個受歡迎的藝術中心。
since when?: Since when have you liked eating vegetables, because last month you would not even touch a carrot?
你從什麼時候開始喜歡吃蔬菜的，因為上個月你連紅蘿蔔都不碰呢？
since the beginning: Since the beginning of the school year, Amy has sat in the front row and asked the most questions.
從學年一開始，艾咪就一直坐在第一排，而且問的問題最多。
since (起點) vs. for (長度): We have lived in this apartment since 2015, so we have known our kind neighbors for many years.
我們自 2015 年起就住在這間公寓，所以我們已認識親切的鄰居很多年了。
since 9 o'clock vs. for three hours: My father has been working in the garden since 9 o'clock, so he has been outside for three hours.
我爸爸從九點起就在花園工作，所以他已經在外面三小時了。
since (時間, 用完成式) vs. from (起點, 不限時態): Grandma has lived in Tainan since she was born, and she walks to the same market from her home every day.
奶奶從出生起就一直住在台南，她每天從家裡走到同一個市場。
have lived here since 2010: My family has lived here since 2010, and my little brother was born in this house two years later.
我們家從 2010 年起就住在這裡，而我弟弟兩年後在這間房子出生。
from 2010 to 2015: My father worked in Japan from 2010 to 2015, and he has taught Japanese at our school since then.
我爸爸從 2010 到 2015 年在日本工作，從那時起他就在我們學校教日語。
since (因為, 連接詞) vs. since (自從): Since it is raining so hard, let's stay inside and play cards, because we have played outside since lunch anyway.
既然雨下得這麼大，我們就待在室內玩牌吧，反正我們從午餐後就一直在外面玩了。
Since you are here, help me carry these heavy boxes up the stairs, and then we can have some cake.
既然你在這，幫我把這些很重的箱子搬上樓，然後我們可以吃點蛋糕。
since vs. ago: My grandfather bought this old radio forty years ago, and it has been in our living room since then.
我爺爺四十年前買了這台舊收音機，從那時起它就一直在我們的客廳。
It has been ten years since…: It has been ten years since my family moved to Taipei, but my mother still misses her old town.
自從我們家搬到台北已經十年了，但我媽媽仍然想念她的老家小鎮。
since vs. after: After the game, my brother went home, but I have been studying in the library since the game ended.
比賽後我哥哥回家了，但我從比賽結束後就一直在圖書館讀書到現在。
walk through the forest: We walked through the forest for two hours, and the tall trees kept us cool under the hot summer sun.
我們穿過森林走了兩個小時，高大的樹木讓我們在炎熱的夏日陽光下保持涼爽。
go through the door: When you go through the door on the left, you will see the teachers' office at the end of the hall.
當你穿過左邊那扇門，就會看到走廊盡頭的教師辦公室。
look through the window: On rainy days, I like to look through the window and watch people hurrying along the street with umbrellas.
下雨天時，我喜歡透過窗戶看著人們拿著傘匆匆走在街上。
drive through the tunnel: It was dark when we drove through the tunnel, but the bright lights inside helped Dad see the road.
我們開車穿過隧道時很暗，但隧道裡明亮的燈光幫助爸爸看清路面。
through the hole: A small mouse came through the hole in the kitchen wall and ran under the table to look for food.
一隻小老鼠穿過廚房牆上的洞，跑到桌子下面找食物。
run through the park: Every morning before school, my father and I run through the park and say hello to the old people exercising.
每天早上上學前，我和爸爸會穿過公園跑步，和運動的老人打招呼。
the river runs through the city: A long river runs through the city, and on weekends many families ride bicycles along its green banks.
一條長河貫穿城市，週末時很多家庭沿著綠色的河岸騎腳踏車。
swim through the water: The brave boy swam through the cold water to reach the small boat and bring his little sister back to shore.
勇敢的男孩在冰冷的水中游過去，抵達小船，把妹妹帶回岸邊。
see through the glass: You can see through the glass of the big fish tank and watch the colorful fish swimming around the rocks.
你可以透過大魚缸的玻璃看進去，看著色彩鮮豔的魚在石頭周圍游來游去。
through the crowd: At the night market, we had to push through the crowd to get to the famous stand that sells fried chicken.
在夜市，我們必須穿過人群才能到那家賣炸雞的有名攤位。
pass through Taichung: The train from Taipei to Kaohsiung will pass through Taichung at noon, so we can see my aunt waving from the station.
從台北到高雄的火車中午會經過台中，所以我們可以看見阿姨在車站揮手。
a path through the woods: There is a narrow path through the woods behind our school, and it leads to a quiet little pond.
我們學校後面有一條穿過森林的小路，通往一個安靜的小池塘。
cut through the paper: The knife was so sharp that it cut through the paper easily, and I made a pretty paper flower.
這把刀很鋭利，輕鬆就切穿紙張，我做了一朵漂亮的紙花。
the wind blew through the trees: The wind blew through the trees all night, and in the morning the garden was covered with yellow leaves.
風整夜穿過樹林，早上花園裡覆滿了黃色的落葉。
through the night: The baby cried through the night, so my parents looked very tired at breakfast the next morning.
寶寶整夜哭鬧，所以我爸媽隔天早餐時看起來非常疲倦。
all through the year: In Taiwan, you can buy fresh fruit all through the year, because the weather is warm in most months.
在台灣，你整年都能買到新鮮水果，因為大部分的月份天氣都很溫暖。
through the winter: The old man kept a small fire burning through the winter to keep his little house warm and dry.
這位老人整個冬天都讓小火爐持續燃燒，好讓他的小房子溫暖乾燥。
from Monday through Friday: The school library is open from Monday through Friday, but it is closed on weekends and national holidays.
學校圖書館從週一到週五（含週五）開放，但週末和國定假日休館。
sleep through the class: Jack was so tired after the basketball game that he slept through the class and missed the whole lesson.
傑克打完籃球賽後太累了，整堂課都在睡，錯過了整個課程內容。
through the ages: Through the ages, people have looked up at the stars and told stories about the pictures they saw in them.
歷代以來，人們仰望星空，講述他們在星星中看到的圖案的故事。
work through lunch: Mr. Lin was so busy with the reports that he had to work through lunch and only ate an apple.
林先生忙著處理報告，所以午餐時間也在工作，只吃了一顆蘋果。
right through the day: It rained right through the day, so we stayed home and played cards instead of going to the beach.
雨下了一整天，所以我們留在家裡玩牌，沒有去海邊。
get through the exam: Amy studied hard every night, and she finally got through the exam with a very good grade.
艾美每晚用功讀書，最後以很好的成績通過考試。
go through hard times: My family went through hard times when Dad lost his job, but we helped each other and never gave up.
爸爸失業時我們家經歷了困難時期，但我們互相幫忙，從不放棄。
go through the papers: The teacher went through the papers on her desk carefully because one student's homework was missing.
老師仔細翻閱桌上的文件，因為有一位學生的作業不見了。
I called my brother five times last night, but I could not get through to him because his phone was off.
我昨晚打了五次電話給哥哥，但因為他手機關機，我一直打不通他的電話。
look through the book: Before buying it, Kevin looked through the book for a few minutes to see if the stories were interesting.
買之前，凱文翻閱書本幾分鐘，看看裡面的故事有不有趣。
read through the letter: Grandma read through the letter from her old friend twice, and then she smiled and put it in a box.
奶奶把老朋友寄來的信讀完兩遍，然後微笑著把它放進盒子裡。
think through the plan: We should think through the plan for the school trip before we tell the whole class about it.
在告訴全班之前，我們應該先把校外教學的計畫想透。
see through his lies: Tom said he was sick, but his mother saw through his lies at once because he was still laughing.
湯姆說他生病了，但他媽媽馬上看穿他的謊言，因為他還在笑。
live through the war: My great-grandfather lived through the war when he was a boy, and he often tells us how hard life was.
我的曾祖父小時候經歷過戰爭，他常常告訴我們那時生活多麼辛苦。
break through: The sun finally broke through the dark clouds in the afternoon, and the children ran outside to play.
下午太陽終於突破烏雲，孩子們跑到外面玩。
come through: Jenny was very ill last winter, but she came through and is now back on the school swimming team.
珍妮去年冬天病得很重，但她度過難關，現在回到學校游泳隊了。
pull through: The doctor said my grandfather was very weak, but he pulled through after two weeks in the hospital.
醫生說我爺爺很虛弱，但他在醫院住了兩週後康復了。
put sb. through to: When I called the hotel, the woman at the front desk put me through to the manager right away.
我打電話到飯店時，櫃檯的女士馬上為我接通電話給經理。
run through the list: Before we leave for the camping trip, let's run through the list and make sure we have packed everything.
出發去露營前，我們快速瀏覽一下清單，確認所有東西都打包好了。
sit through the movie: The movie was so boring that Peter could hardly sit through the movie without falling asleep in his seat.
那部電影太無聊了，彼得幾乎無法坐著看完電影而不在座位上睡著。
talk through the problem: Instead of shouting at each other, the two friends sat down and talked through the problem calmly.
兩個朋友沒有互相大吼，而是坐下來冷靜地把問題談透。
be through with: After he lied to me three times, I told Jack that I was through with him and walked away.
在他騙了我三次之後，我告訴傑克我要跟他斷絕關係，然後走開了。
Mom, I'm through with my homework, so can I go to the park and ride my bike with Linda now?
媽，我作業做完了，現在可以去公園跟琳達騎腳踏車嗎？
After the big fight on Saturday night, Lisa cried and told Mike that they were through for good.
週六晚上大吵一架後，麗莎哭著告訴麥克他們分手了，而且是永遠分手。
through and through: My grandfather has lived in Tainan all his life, and he is a Tainan person through and through.
我爺爺一輩子都住在台南，他是個徹頭徹尾的台南人。
through the roof: After the typhoon, the price of vegetables went through the roof, so my mother bought more eggs instead.
颱風過後，蔬菜價格暴漲，所以我媽媽改買比較多雞蛋。
through thick and thin: Mary and Jane have been best friends since they were five, and they stay together through thick and thin.
瑪莉和珍從五歲起就是最好的朋友，她們一直同甘共苦、彼此相伴。
learn through practice: You cannot learn to swim just by reading a book; you learn through practice in the water every week.
光看書是學不會游泳的，你要透過每週在水裡練習來學習。
through hard work: Through hard work and many early mornings, Jason finally made the school basketball team this year.
透過努力和許多個早起的早晨，傑森今年終於進入學校籃球隊。
through a friend: My sister found her first job through a friend who worked at the same restaurant near the station.
我姊姊透過一位在車站附近同一間餐廳工作的朋友找到她的第一份工作。
go through with the plan: Even though it started to rain, the class decided to go through with the plan and held the picnic.
雖然開始下雨了，全班還是決定把計畫執行到底，舉辦了野餐。
carry through: It is easy to make a New Year plan, but it is hard to carry it through for a whole year.
訂新年計畫很容易，但要完成並堅持一整年卻很難。
follow through: Ben always says he will exercise every morning, but he never follows through, and his mother is tired of hearing it.
班總是說他每天早上要運動，但他從不貫徹到底，他媽媽都聽膩了。
fall through: Our plan to visit the zoo on Sunday fell through because Dad suddenly had to go to work.
我們週日去動物園的計畫落空了，因為爸爸突然得去上班。
through no fault of mine: The bus was late and I missed the first class through no fault of mine, but the teacher was still angry.
公車晚了，我錯過第一堂課，這不是我的錯，但老師還是很生氣。
through (穿過內部) vs. across (橫越表面) vs. ove: We walked through the dark tunnel, ran across the wide field, and then climbed over the old wall.
我們穿過黑暗的隧道，橫越寬闊的田野，然後翻越那道老牆。
through (介係詞／副詞) vs. throughout (遍及): The river runs through the city, and you can find small bridges throughout the whole town.
這條河穿過這座城市，整個小鎮遍布著小橋。
through the night (整夜) vs. throughout th: The baby slept through the night for the first time, but his mother woke up throughout the night to check.
寶寶第一次睡了整夜，但他媽媽整夜每時每刻都醒來查看。
Monday through Friday (美, 含) vs. Monday: The library is open Monday through Friday from nine to five, so you can return books after school.
圖書館週一到週五（含週五）九點到五點開放，所以你放學後可以還書。
through (完成) vs. finished: When you are through with the dishes, please tell me, because I have already finished my work in the living room.
你把碗洗完時請告訴我，因為我已經打掃完客廳了。
get through (通過／完成) vs. get over (克服): It took Amy a month to get over her cold, but she still got through all her exams.
艾美花了一個月才克服感冒，但她還是通過了所有的考試。
look through (翻閱) vs. look over (瀏覽): I looked through the whole magazine for the cake story, and then Mom looked over my homework quickly.
我翻閱整本雜誌找那篇蛋糕的文章，然後媽媽快速瀏覽了我的作業。
see through (看穿) vs. see about (處理): Dad saw through my excuse right away and said he would see about my broken bike later.
爸爸馬上看穿我的藉口，並說他晚點會處理我壞掉的腳踏車。
through (憑藉) vs. by (方式): Lily got the job through her uncle, and she goes to the office by bus every morning.
莉莉透過她叔叔得到這份工作，她每天早上搭公車去辦公室。
through: We traveled to Kaohsiung through Taichung, and we stopped there for a bowl of beef noodles.
我們經由台中去高雄，並在那裡停下來吃一碗牛肉麵。
throughout the country: Night markets are popular throughout the country, and every city has its own famous snacks to try.
夜市在全國各地都很受歡迎，每個城市都有自己值得一試的名小吃。
throughout the world: Soccer is loved by people throughout the world, so the World Cup is watched by millions of fans.
全世界的人都愛足球，所以世界盃有數百萬球迷觀看。
throughout the house: The smell of Grandma's chicken soup filled the air throughout the house, and everyone felt hungry at once.
奶奶雞湯的香味充滿了整間屋子，大家馬上都覺得餓了。
throughout the city: During the festival, there were lanterns throughout the city, and visitors took pictures on every street.
慶典期間，全市到處都是燈籠，遊客在每條街上拍照。
throughout the school: The news about the new swimming pool spread throughout the school in one morning, and everyone was excited.
新游泳池的消息在一個早上就傳遍全校，大家都很興奮。
throughout the year: The weather in Taitung is warm throughout the year, so many people like to go there in winter.
台東一年到頭天氣都很溫暖，所以很多人喜歡冬天去那裡。
throughout the day: It was so hot that the students drank water throughout the day and kept the fans on in class.
天氣熱到學生們一整天都在喝水，教室裡的電風扇也一直開著。
throughout the night: The loud music from the party next door went on throughout the night, so nobody in my family slept well.
隔壁派對的大聲音樂整夜不停，所以我們家沒有人睡得好。
