throughout history: Throughout history, people have built bridges over rivers so that they could trade with their neighbors.
整個歷史上，人們在河上建橋，好跟鄰近的人做買賣。
throughout one's life: My grandmother was a teacher, and she kept reading and learning new things throughout her life.
我奶奶是老師，她一生中都不斷閱讀和學習新事物。
throughout the summer: Jack worked at his uncle's ice cream shop throughout the summer to save money for a new bike.
傑克整個夏天都在叔叔的冰淇淋店工作，為了存錢買新腳踏車。
throughout the game: The fans cheered loudly throughout the game, even when our team was losing by ten points.
球迷整場比賽都大聲加油，即使我們的球隊落後十分也一樣。
throughout the lesson: Peter kept looking out of the window throughout the lesson, so the teacher asked him a difficult question.
彼得整堂課都一直看著窗外，所以老師問了他一個難題。
till now: I have lived in this small town till now, and I have never seen snow in my life.
我直到現在都住在這個小鎮，一生中從沒看過雪。
till then: The school play is next Friday, so we have to practice every day till then after class.
學校話劇在下週五演出，所以直到那時我們每天放學後都得練習。
wait till Friday: Mom said I have to wait till Friday to open the present, but I really want to see what is inside.
媽媽說我得等到週五才能打開禮物，但我真的很想看看裡面是什麼。
not till tomorrow: The new shoes will not arrive till tomorrow, so I have to wear my old ones to the game today.
新鞋要到明天才會送到，所以今天比賽我得穿舊鞋。
till the end: Even though our team was losing, we did not give up and played hard till the end of the game.
雖然我們的球隊落後，我們還是沒有放棄，努力打到比賽的最後。
till late: Dad often works till late at the office, so he usually eats dinner alone after we go to bed.
爸爸常在辦公室工作到很晚，所以他通常在我們睡覺後獨自吃晚餐。
till death: In the old story, the prince promised to love the princess till death, and he never broke his word.
在那個古老故事裡，王子承諾愛公主至死，而他從未違背諾言。
from nine till five: My mother works at the bank from nine till five, so my grandmother picks me up after school.
我媽媽在銀行從九點工作到五點，所以奶奶放學後來接我。
until now: Until now, I did not know that my quiet friend Helen could sing so beautifully on stage.
直到現在，我才知道我安靜的朋友海倫能在舞台上唱得這麼好聽。
until then: The movie starts at seven, and until then we can have some noodles at the shop around the corner.
電影七點開始，直到那時我們可以先在轉角的店吃點麵。
until midnight: Jenny stayed up until midnight to finish her science report, so she was very tired at school today.
珍妮熬夜到午夜才完成自然科學報告，所以今天在學校很累。
until the end of the month: My brother has no money left, so he cannot buy any new games until the end of the month.
我哥哥沒錢了，所以直到月底他都不能買新遊戲。
not until ten: The shopping mall does not open until ten, so we had breakfast first and walked around the park.
購物中心直到十點才開門，所以我們先吃早餐，再在公園散步。
wait until the rain stops: Let's wait until the rain stops before we ride our bikes home, or our books will get wet.
我們等到雨停再騎腳踏車回家吧，不然書會濕掉。
up until last year: Up until last year, my little sister was afraid of dogs, but now she wants one for her birthday.
直到去年，我妹妹還很怕狗，但現在她想要一隻狗當生日禮物。
until late at night: On Chinese New Year's Eve, my whole family stays up until late at night to play cards and eat snacks.
除夕夜，我們全家會熬夜到深夜玩牌、吃點心。
until next time: The teacher said goodbye and until next time, and told us to practice the new words at home.
老師說再見、下次見，並叫我們在家練習新的單字。
stay until Sunday: Our cousins from Japan will stay until Sunday, so we are taking them to the night market tonight.
我們從日本來的表親會待到週日，所以今晚我們要帶他們去夜市。
until (持續到) vs. by (期限前): You can play outside until six, but you must be home by six thirty because dinner will be ready.
你可以在外面玩到六點，但六點半以前必須回家，因為晚餐就準備好了。
wait until six: Dad is still at work, so we will wait until six to eat dinner together as a family.
爸爸還在上班，所以我們會等到六點全家一起吃晚餐。
be here by six: Please be here by six for the team photo, but you do not have to stay until the game is over.
請六點前到這裡拍團體照，但你不必待到比賽結束。
not…until (直到…才) vs. until (直到): I did not go to bed until eleven last night, and then I slept until seven this morning.
我昨晚直到十一點才上床睡覺，然後一直睡到今天早上七點。
Because of the loud thunder, my little brother didn't sleep until midnight and was very sleepy at breakfast.
因為雷聲很大，我弟弟直到半夜才睡，早餐時很想睡。
It was a holiday, so I turned off my alarm and slept until noon for the first time in months.
那天是假日，所以我關掉鬧鐘，幾個月來第一次睡到中午。
until: The two words mean the same, so you can wait until Friday or wait till Friday for the big sale.
這兩個字意思相同，所以你可以說 wait until Friday 或 wait till Friday，都是「等到週五」大特賣。
Not until then did I know that my best friend was moving to Taichung at the end of the summer.
直到那時我才知道，我最好的朋友夏天結束時要搬去台中。
until (時間) vs. as far as (距離): We walked as far as the old bridge and waited there until the sun went down behind the hills.
我們一路走到遠處那座老橋，然後在那裡等到太陽落到山丘後面。
until (介係詞 + 名詞) vs. until (連接詞 + 子句): The shop stays open until nine, but we will not go until Dad comes home from work.
那家店開到九點，但我們要等到爸爸下班回家才會去。
go to school: Every morning, Emma goes to school by bike with her best friend, and they talk about their favorite songs.
每天早上，艾瑪和她最好的朋友騎腳踏車去上學，她們聊著最喜歡的歌。
the way to the station: A foreign woman stopped me on the street and asked me the way to the station in slow English.
一位外國女士在街上攔住我，用緩慢的英文問我去車站的路。
turn to the left: Walk two blocks and turn to the left at the post office, and you will see the library.
走兩個街區，在郵局向左轉，你就會看到圖書館。
to the north: The birds fly to the north every spring, and my grandfather likes to watch them from the roof.
每年春天鳥兒往北飛，我爺爺喜歡在屋頂上看它們。
the door to the kitchen: Please close the door to the kitchen, because the smell of fish is getting into the living room.
請關上通往廚房的門，因為魚的味道飄進客廳了。
next to the bank: The new milk tea shop is next to the bank, so we can stop there after we finish shopping.
新開的奶茶店在銀行旁邊，所以我們購物結束後可以在那裡停一下。
close to the park: My grandfather and grandmother live close to the park, so they take a walk there every morning before breakfast.
我的祖父母住在靠近公園的地方，所以他們每天早餐前都去那裡散步。
face to face: We have written to each other for a year, but tomorrow I will finally meet my pen friend face to face.
我們互相寫信一年了，但明天我終於要和筆友面對面見面了。
back to back: The two boys stood back to back so that their mother could see which one of them was taller.
兩個男孩背對背站著，好讓媽媽看看他們誰比較高。
from door to door: Before the vote, the man went from door to door to talk to people about his ideas for the town.
投票前，那位男士挨家挨戶拜訪，跟大家談他對這個小鎮的想法。
to the end of the road: Walk to the end of the road and you will see a small temple with a big tree in front.
走到路的盡頭，你會看到一座小廟，前面有一棵大樹。
to the east of Taipei: Keelung is to the east of Taipei, and it is famous for its night market and rainy weather.
基隆在台北東邊，它以夜市和多雨的天氣聞名。
point to the sky: The little girl pointed to the sky and shouted happily when she saw a rainbow after the rain.
小女孩看到雨後的彩虹時，指向天空開心地大叫。
a visit to Japan: During our visit to Japan last winter, we saw snow for the first time and ate a lot of good food.
去年冬天去日本旅行時，我們第一次看到雪，也吃了很多好吃的東西。
a trip to Tainan: Our class is planning a trip to Tainan next month, and we want to try the famous beef soup there.
我們班正在計畫下個月去台南旅行，我們想試試那裡有名的牛肉湯。
the road to success: My coach always says that the road to success is long and hard, so we must practice every day.
教練總是說通往成功的路漫長又艱辛，所以我們必須每天練習。
on the way to work: Dad buys a cup of coffee and a newspaper at the same shop on the way to work every morning.
爸爸每天早上上班途中都在同一家店買一杯咖啡和一份報紙。
ten to six: It is ten to six now, so hurry up, or we will miss the bus to the night market.
現在是五點五十，快一點，不然我們會錯過去夜市的公車。
a quarter to three: The math test starts at a quarter to three, so let's go back to the class after we drink some water.
數學考試兩點四十五分開始，所以我們喝點水之後就回教室吧。
to this day: My grandmother gave me a small blue cup when I was five, and I still use it to this day.
我五歲時奶奶給了我一個小藍杯子，直到今天我還在用它。
to date: This is the best score our basketball team has had to date, so the coach bought us all ice cream.
這是我們籃球隊至今最好的成績，所以教練買冰淇淋給我們大家。
count to ten: When you are angry, close your eyes and count to ten slowly before you say anything to anyone.
生氣的時候，先閉上眼睛慢慢數到十，再跟任何人說話。
give it to me: That is my notebook on your desk, so please give it to me before the class begins.
你桌上那本是我的筆記本，所以上課前請把它給我。
say hello to him: If you see my brother at the bus stop this afternoon, please say hello to him for me.
如果你今天下午在公車站看到我哥哥，請替我向他問好。
talk to the teacher: Lucy was worried about her grades, so she stayed after class to talk to the teacher about it.
露西擔心她的成績，所以放學後留下來和老師談這件事。
listen to music: My sister likes to listen to music while she does her homework, but I need a quiet room.
我姊姊喜歡邊聽音樂邊做功課，但我需要安靜的房間。
write to a friend: Instead of sending a short message on his phone, Grandpa still writes to a friend in America by hand every month.
爺爺不用手機傳簡訊，而是每個月仍然親手寫信給在美國的朋友。
belong to me: The red umbrella by the door does not belong to me; I think someone left it here yesterday.
門邊那把紅傘不屬於我，我想是有人昨天留在這裡的。
Something strange happened to Mark on his way home, and he could not stop talking about it at dinner.
馬克回家路上發生了奇怪的事，晚餐時他一直講個不停。
lead to success: Hard work and a good plan usually lead to success, so do not give up when things get difficult.
努力和好的計畫通常會導致成功，所以事情變難時不要放棄。
get to the point: We only have five minutes before the bell rings, so please get to the point and tell us your idea.
鐘響前我們只有五分鐘，所以請講重點，告訴我們你的想法。
come to an end: When the summer vacation came to an end, the students were sad but also happy to see their friends again.
暑假結束時，學生們很難過，但也很高興能再見到朋友。
the answer to the question: Nobody in the class knew the answer to the question, so the teacher gave us a little help with it.
班上沒有人知道問題的答案，所以老師給了我們一點幫助。
the key to the door: I lost the key to the door, so I had to wait outside until my mother came home from work.
我弄丟了門的鑰匙，所以得在外面等到媽媽下班回家。
an invitation to the party: Kelly got an invitation to the party on Saturday, and now she is looking for a nice dress to wear.
凱莉收到了週六的派對邀請，現在她正在找一件漂亮的洋裝穿。
a ticket to the show: My uncle gave me a ticket to the show, so I can finally see my favorite singer this weekend.
我叔叔給了我一張表演的票，所以這週末我終於能看到最喜歡的歌手了。
a reply to the letter: Amy waited for two weeks, but she never got a reply to the letter she sent to the writer.
艾美等了兩個星期，但她寄給那位作家的信一直沒收到回信。
the way to do it: My dad showed me the way to do it, and now I can cook rice without burning it.
我爸爸教我做這件事的方法，現在我煮飯不會燒焦了。
be kind to animals: My teacher always tells us to be kind to animals, so we feed the street cats near the school.
老師總是告訴我們要對動物友善，所以我們會餵學校附近的流浪貓。
be nice to me: My older brother is usually nice to me, but he gets angry when I touch his computer games.
我哥哥通常對我很好，但我碰他的電腦遊戲時他會生氣。
My grandmother was always good to the children on our street, and they still visit her today.
我奶奶一直對我們這條街的孩子很好，他們今天仍然會來看她。
The boy was rude to the old lady on the bus, and everyone around him looked very unhappy.
那個男孩在公車上對老太太沒禮貌，他周圍的每個人看起來都很不高興。
be polite to: Please be polite to the guests from Japan tomorrow and help them when they cannot understand something.
明天請對來自日本的客人有禮貌，他們聽不懂時要幫助他們。
be friendly to: The students in my new class were friendly to me on the first day, so I was not nervous anymore.
新班級的同學在第一天就對我很友善，所以我不再緊張了。
be close to: Jenny is very close to her grandmother, and she visits her every weekend to cook dinner together.
珍妮跟她奶奶很親近，她每個週末都去探望奶奶，一起煮晚餐。
be next to: The bakery is next to my school, so I can smell fresh bread every morning when I arrive.
麵包店在我學校旁邊，所以我每天早上到校時都能聞到新鮮麵包的味道。
be used to doing: My father is used to getting up at five every morning, so he never needs an alarm clock.
我爸爸習慣每天早上五點起床，所以他從來不需要鬧鐘。
be similar to: Your new phone is similar to mine, but yours has a bigger screen and a better camera.
你的新手機跟我的很相似，但你的螢幕比較大、相機也比較好。
be married to: My English teacher is married to a doctor, and they have two cute children and a small dog.
我的英文老師和一位醫生結婚，他們有兩個可愛的孩子和一隻小狗。
be new to the job: Sam is still new to the job at the coffee shop, so he sometimes gets the orders wrong.
山姆對咖啡店的工作還很生，所以他有時會弄錯點單。
be true to one's word: Dad was true to his word and took us to the beach on Sunday, even though he was tired.
爸爸守信，週日帶我們去海邊，即使他很累。
be late to class: I missed the bus this morning and was late to class, so the teacher asked me to stay after school.
我今天早上錯過公車，上課遲到了，所以老師叫我放學後留下來。
be important to me: This old watch is very important to me because my grandfather gave it to me before he died.
這支舊手錶對我很重要，因為是爺爺過世前送給我的。
be helpful to: The map on your phone is very helpful to visitors who do not know the streets of Taipei.
你手機上的地圖對不認識台北街道的觀光客很有幫助。
be known to everyone: It is known to everyone in school that Mr. Wang gives a quiz every Friday afternoon.
王老師每週五下午都有小考，這件事全校眾所皆知。
be open to all: The new city library is open to all, so you do not need a card just to read there.
新的市立圖書館對所有人開放，所以只是在那裡看書不需要借書證。
be ready to go: The bags are in the car and the kids are ready to go, so let's leave for the mountains now.
行李已經放在車上，孩子們也準備出發了，我們現在就去山上吧。
to one's surprise: To her surprise, Linda found a birthday cake and a card from her friends in class on her desk.
令琳達驚訝的是，她在桌上發現班上朋友們送的生日蛋糕和卡片。
to my joy: To my joy, the teacher said our class could have a party on the last day of school.
令我高興的是，老師說我們班可以在學期最後一天開派對。
to be honest: To be honest, I did not like the movie very much because the story was too slow and long.
老實說，我不太喜歡那部電影，因為故事太慢又太長。
to tell the truth: To tell the truth, I forgot to do my homework last night because I was playing games with my cousin.
說實話，我昨晚忘了做功課，因為我在跟表哥玩遊戲。
to begin with: To begin with, let's write down the things we need for the picnic, and then we can go shopping.
首先，我們把野餐需要的東西寫下來，然後再去買東西。
to the point: The teacher likes Mary's answers because they are always short and to the point, with no extra words.
老師喜歡瑪莉的回答，因為總是簡短又切中要點，沒有多餘的字。
to one's taste: The new restaurant was not to my taste, because the food was too sweet and the music was too loud.
那家新餐廳不合我的口味，因為食物太甜、音樂又太大聲。
to the best of my knowledge: To the best of my knowledge, the school bus leaves at seven thirty, but you should check with the office.
就我所知，校車七點半出發，但你應該跟辦公室確認一下。
to this end: Our class wants to win the singing game at school, and to this end we practice every day after school.
我們班想贏得學校的歌唱比賽，為此我們每天放學後都練習。
to no end: I waited for the bus in the rain for an hour to no end, because the bus never came that day.
我在雨中白白地等了一小時公車，因為那天公車根本沒來。
one to one: After class, the teacher helped me one to one with the math problems I did not understand.
放學後，老師一對一地幫我解決我不懂的數學題。
ten to one: Ten to one, Tom will forget his umbrella again today, because he never checks the weather report.
很可能湯姆今天又會忘記帶傘，因為他從不看天氣預報。
a mother to three children: Mrs. Chen is a mother to three children, and she still finds time to run every morning.
陳太太是三個孩子的母親，她仍然找得出時間每天早上跑步。
dance to the music: At the party, everyone danced to the music, and even my shy brother moved his feet a little.
派對上大家隨著音樂起舞，就連我害羞的弟弟也稍微動了動腳。
sing to the guitar: My uncle played and we all sang to the guitar around the fire at the beach last night.
昨晚在海邊的火堆旁，叔叔彈吉他，我們大家伴著吉他唱歌。
add sugar to the tea: Grandpa likes to add sugar to the tea, but the doctor told him to drink it without sugar.
爺爺喜歡在茶裡加糖，但醫生叫他喝茶不要加糖。
compare A to B: My father often compares life to a long trip, because you never know what you will see next.
我爸爸常把人生比作一段長途旅行，因為你永遠不知道接下來會看到什麼。
look forward to seeing you: I am looking forward to seeing you at the school fair next week, so please do not forget.
我期待下週在校園園遊會見到你，所以請不要忘記。
pay attention to: Please pay attention to the traffic lights when you ride your bike, because the road is very busy here.
騎腳踏車時請注意紅綠燈，因為這裡的路很繁忙。
get used to: It took me two months to get used to the cold weather after we moved to the mountains.
我們搬到山上後，我花了兩個月才習慣寒冷的天氣。
Jack broke his sister's toy, so he wants to make up to her by buying her a new one.
傑克弄壞了妹妹的玩具，所以他想買一個新的補償她。
up to you: We can eat pizza or noodles tonight; it is up to you, because you cooked dinner yesterday.
今晚我們可以吃披薩或麵，由你決定，因為昨天是你煮晚餐。
up to 100: The hall can hold up to one hundred people, so every student in our grade can watch the show.
這個大廳最多可容納一百人，所以我們年級的每個學生都能看表演。
down to the last cent: Lisa spent all her birthday money on books, down to the last cent, and still wanted more.
麗莎把生日的錢全花在書上，直到最後一分錢，而且還想要更多。
to a certain degree: I agree with you to a certain degree, but I still think we need more time to finish the project.
我某種程度上同意你，但我還是認為我們需要更多時間完成這個專題。
to the last: The old soldier stayed brave to the last and never told the enemy where his friends were hiding.
那位老士兵直到最後都很勇敢，從未告訴敵人他的朋友藏在哪裡。
to death: The little boy was scared to death when the lights went out during the storm last night.
昨晚暴風雨中燈熄滅時，小男孩嚇得要死。
be bored to death: We were bored to death during the long speech, and some students even fell asleep in their seats.
聽那場長長的演講時我們無聊得要死，有些學生甚至在座位上睡著了。
to pieces: The glass fell off the table and broke to pieces, so Mom told us to stay away from the kitchen.
玻璃杯從桌上掉下來摔成碎片，所以媽媽叫我們離廚房遠一點。
tear it to pieces: My little brother got angry at his drawing and tore it to pieces before I could stop him.
我弟弟對自己的畫生氣，在我阻止他之前就把它撕碎了。
to one's face: If you have a problem with Kevin, tell him to his face instead of talking behind his back.
如果你對凱文有意見，就當面告訴他，不要在背後說他。
to the letter: Follow the steps in the cookie book to the letter the first time you bake, and they will come out just right.
第一次烤東西時要一絲不苟地照著餅乾書上的步驟做，餅乾就會剛剛好。
to the full: Grandpa says we should enjoy every holiday to the full, because time with family passes very quickly.
爺爺說我們應該充分地享受每個假期，因為和家人相處的時間過得很快。
to the minute: The train in Japan arrived at the station at nine fifteen, right to the minute, which surprised us all.
日本的火車九點十五分一分不差地到站，讓我們都很驚訝。
from place to place: My father's job takes him from place to place, so we have lived in four cities in six years.
我爸爸的工作讓他到處跑，所以我們六年內住過四個城市。
from bad to worse: Our team's season went from bad to worse after our best player hurt his knee in the second game.
我們球隊這一季在最佳球員第二場比賽傷了膝蓋後，情況越來越糟。
from start to finish: The movie was exciting from start to finish, so nobody in the theater looked at their phone.
那部電影從頭到尾都很刺激，所以電影院裡沒有人看手機。
room to room: The little puppy ran from room to room looking for its ball, and we all laughed at it.
小狗一間接一間地跑來跑去找它的球，我們全都笑了。
cheek to cheek: In the old photo, Grandpa and Grandma are dancing cheek to cheek at their wedding fifty years ago.
在那張舊照片裡，爺爺和奶奶五十年前在婚禮上臉貼臉跳舞。
hand to hand: In the movie, the hero fought the robber hand to hand on the roof of a tall building.
電影裡，英雄在高樓屋頂上和搶匪肉搏。
heart to heart: After the fight, the two sisters had a heart to heart talk and promised to be honest with each other.
吵架之後，兩姊妹坦誠地談了一次，並承諾要對彼此誠實。
side by side (非 to): The two friends walked side by side to the station, talking and laughing all the way there.
兩個朋友並肩走到車站，一路上有說有笑。
turn to sb. for help: When I could not understand the science homework, I turned to my older sister for help.
我看不懂自然科學作業時，就向姊姊求助。
turn to page 10: The teacher asked us to turn to page ten and read the first story quietly for five minutes.
老師叫我們翻到第十頁，安靜地讀第一篇故事五分鐘。
My dog took to our new neighbor right away, and now he runs to her whenever she comes home.
我的狗馬上喜歡上新鄰居，現在她一回家，狗就跑向她。
get to know: It took a few weeks to get to know the new students in my class, but now we eat lunch together.
我花了幾週才逐漸認識新同學，但現在我們每天一起吃午餐。
come to think of it: Come to think of it, I left my umbrella on the bus this morning, so I need to call the bus company.
想起來，我今天早上把傘留在公車上了，所以我得打電話給公車公司。
come to one's senses: After losing all his pocket money on games, Peter finally came to his senses and started saving.
把零用錢都輸在遊戲上之後，彼得終於恢復理智，開始存錢。
see to it that: Please see to it that all the windows are closed before you leave, because a typhoon is coming tonight.
離開前請確保所有窗戶都關好，因為今晚颱風要來了。
drink to your health: At Grandma's birthday dinner, we all raised our glasses and drank to her health and a long happy life.
奶奶生日晚餐時，我們都舉起杯子為她的健康和長壽幸福乾杯。
Here's to you!: At the party, my uncle stood up, raised his glass to Grandma, and said Here's to you with a big smile.
派對上，叔叔站起來，向奶奶舉杯，帶著大大的笑容說：敬你一杯！
be about to do: We were about to leave for the beach when it suddenly began to rain hard, so we stayed home.
我們正要出發去海邊時，突然下起大雨，所以我們留在家裡。
be yet to come: The coach told us the hardest part of the training is yet to come, so we should rest well tonight.
教練告訴我們訓練最難的部分尚未來到，所以今晚我們應該好好休息。
to go: I would like two chicken sandwiches and a large milk tea to go, because I am eating on the train.
我要兩個雞肉三明治和一杯大杯奶茶外帶，因為我要在火車上吃。
two to go: I have finished eight math problems, and there are only two to go before I can watch TV.
我已經做完八題數學，還剩兩題做完就可以看電視了。
the week to come: The weather report says the week to come will be cold and rainy, so bring a jacket to school.
天氣預報說即將來的一週會又冷又多雨，所以帶件夾克去學校吧。
to and from school: Many students ride their bikes to and from school, so the road is very busy at eight and four.
很多學生騎腳踏車往返學校，所以八點和四點時路上很繁忙。
to the last drop: The soup was so delicious that my brother finished it to the last drop and asked for more.
湯太好喝了，我弟弟喝到最後一滴，還要再來一碗。
to the touch: The stone wall felt cold to the touch, even though the sun had been shining on it all afternoon.
雖然太陽整個下午都照在上面，石牆摸起來還是很冰。
soft to the touch: The baby's new blanket is soft to the touch, and she falls asleep as soon as she holds it.
寶寶的新毯子摸起來很軟，她一抱著就睡著了。
to the eye: The cake looked beautiful to the eye, but when we ate it, the taste was too sweet for everyone.
這個蛋糕看起來很美，但我們吃的時候，味道對大家來說都太甜了。
to the ear: Her English sounds pleasing to the ear because she practices speaking with a foreign friend every weekend.
她的英文聽起來很悅耳，因為她每個週末都和一位外國朋友練習說話。
music to my ears: When my mother said we would go to Japan this summer, the news was music to my ears.
當媽媽說今年夏天我們要去日本時，這個消息對我來說真是悅耳的消息。
to my knowledge: To my knowledge, the school library closes at five on Fridays, so we should hurry up and finish our homework.
據我所知，學校圖書館星期五五點關門，所以我們應該快一點把作業寫完。
to my mind: To my mind, playing basketball after school is a better way to rest than watching TV for hours.
依我看，放學後打籃球比看好幾個小時的電視更能休息。
to my cost: Tom learned to his cost that eating too much ice cream before a race makes your stomach hurt badly.
湯姆付出代價後才知道，比賽前吃太多冰淇淋會讓肚子很痛。
lend money to: My brother did not want to lend money to his friend because the boy never paid him back last time.
我弟弟不想借錢給他的朋友，因為那個男孩上次從來沒有還他錢。
sell it to him: Mary has an old bike that she does not ride anymore, so she decided to sell it to him for a low price.
瑪麗有一台不再騎的舊腳踏車，所以她決定用低價把它賣給他。
show it to me: If you drew a picture of our class trip, please show it to me before you hand it to the teacher.
如果你畫了我們班級旅行的圖，請在交給老師之前先拿給我看。
teach English to kids: On Saturday mornings, my aunt teaches English to kids at a small school near the train station.
每個星期六早上，我阿姨在火車站附近的一間小學校教小孩英文。
send a card to: Every year on her birthday, I send a card to my grandmother because she lives far away in Tainan.
每年她生日時，我都會寄卡片給奶奶，因為她住在遙遠的台南。
bring it to the party: Grandma made a big chocolate cake, and she asked me to bring it to the party at Lisa's house.
奶奶做了一個大巧克力蛋糕，並且請我把它帶來麗莎家的派對。
explain it to me: I did not understand the math question, so I asked my sister to explain it to me slowly after dinner.
我不懂這道數學題，所以我請姊姊晚餐後慢慢向我解釋。
introduce A to B: At the party, Peter was happy to introduce his new friend to his parents, who liked her at once.
在派對上，彼得很開心地把新朋友介紹給他的父母，他們馬上就喜歡她了。
describe it to me: The police officer asked the woman to describe the thief to him, and she said he was tall and thin.
警察請那位女士向他描述小偷，她說他又高又瘦。
suggest it to him: I have a good idea for the school festival, and I will suggest it to him at the class meeting tomorrow.
我對校慶有一個好點子，明天班會時我會向他建議。
report to the teacher: When the students saw a broken window in the hall, they went to report it to the teacher right away.
當學生們看到大廳裡有一扇破窗，他們馬上去向老師報告。
After he broke his friend's glasses by accident, Ben went to apologize to her and offered to buy new ones.
班不小心弄壞朋友的眼鏡後，他去向她道歉，並主動要買新的給她。
reply to the email: My teacher sent me a question about my report last night, so I need to reply to the email this morning.
老師昨晚寄給我一個關於報告的問題，所以我今天早上必須回信。
object to: Many parents object to the plan for a longer school day because their children already have too much homework.
許多家長反對延長上課時間的計畫，因為他們的孩子已經有太多作業了。
agree to a plan: After talking for an hour, everyone in the club agreed to the plan to hold a bake sale next month.
討論了一小時後，社團裡的每個人都同意下個月舉辦義賣會的計畫。
stick to the plan: Even though it started raining, we decided to stick to the plan and go hiking in the mountains anyway.
雖然開始下雨了，我們還是決定堅持計畫，無論如何都去山上健行。
belong to: This blue umbrella does not belong to me; I think it belongs to the girl who sat beside me on the bus.
這把藍色雨傘不屬於我；我想它屬於公車上坐在我旁邊的那個女孩。
go to bed: My little brother always goes to bed at nine o'clock because he has to get up early for school.
我的小弟弟總是九點去睡覺，因為他必須早起上學。
go to work: My father goes to work by bus every day, but on rainy days my mother drives him to the office.
我爸爸每天搭公車去上班，但下雨天我媽媽會開車送他到辦公室。
go to sleep: The baby could not go to sleep last night because the dogs outside kept barking loudly until midnight.
昨晚寶寶一直無法入睡，因為外面的狗狗大聲叫到半夜。
go to the movies: On Friday night, my cousins and I like to go to the movies and share a big box of popcorn.
星期五晚上，我和表兄弟姊妹喜歡去看電影，一起分享一大盒爆米花。
go to church: Every Sunday morning, Mrs. Lin goes to church with her family, and then they have lunch at a noodle shop.
每個星期天早上，林太太和家人去教堂，然後他們在一家麵店吃午餐。
get to school: It takes me about twenty minutes to get to school by bike, so I always leave home before seven.
我騎腳踏車到學校大約需要二十分鐘，所以我總是在七點前出門。
get to work: We have only one hour to finish this picture, so let's stop talking and get to work right now.
我們只有一小時可以完成這張圖畫，所以我們別再聊了，現在就開始工作吧。
back to school: Summer vacation is almost over, and the stores are full of parents buying bags and pens for back to school.
暑假快結束了，商店裡滿是為了返校而買書包和筆的家長。
back to normal: After the big storm passed, it took three days for the trains in the city to get back to normal.
大風暴過去之後，市區的火車花了三天才恢復正常。
back to the point: We were talking about the weekend, but then the teacher said we should get back to the point and finish the lesson.
我們本來在聊週末的事，但老師說我們應該回到正題，把課上完。
to (方向／對象) vs. for (目的／對象): I walked to the post office this morning and bought a stamp for my friend's letter to Canada.
我今天早上走到郵局，為我朋友寄去加拿大的信買了一張郵票。
give it to me vs. buy it for me: Please give the pen to me now, and later I will buy a new notebook for you at the bookstore.
請現在把筆給我，之後我會在書店買一本新筆記本給你。
go to school (非 go to the school): My sister goes to school by bus every morning, but today she went to the school to meet her old teacher.
我姊姊每天早上搭公車去上學，但今天她去學校的建築見她以前的老師。
go to bed (非 the bed): I usually go to bed at ten, and I never read under the bed covers because it hurts my eyes.
我通常十點去睡覺，而且我從不在被子底下看書，因為那會傷眼睛。
go home (無 to): After the game ended, the tired players went home quickly instead of going to the restaurant with their coach.
比賽結束後，疲倦的球員們很快就回家了，而沒有和教練去餐廳。
go there (無 to): My aunt and uncle live near the beach, and we go there every summer to swim and play in the sand.
我的阿姨和姨丈住在海邊附近，我們每年夏天都去那裡游泳和玩沙。
arrive at/in (非 to): We arrived at the station late, so we did not get to Taipei until nine instead of eight o'clock.
我們晚到達車站，所以我們九點才到台北，而不是八點。
reach the station (無 to): We walked fast and reached the station just in time, but the bus to the beach had already left.
我們走得很快，剛好及時到達車站，但去海邊的公車已經開走了。
get to the station: If you take the number ten bus, you can get to the station in fifteen minutes without changing buses.
如果你搭十號公車，不用換車就可以在十五分鐘內到達車站。
listen to (非 listen): On the way to school, I like to listen to music on my phone, but I always turn it off in class.
上學的路上，我喜歡用手機聽音樂，但在課堂上我總是把它關掉。
talk to (對人) vs. talk about (談論): I want to talk to my teacher after class, because I need to talk about my low test score with her.
我想在下課後對老師說話，因為我需要和她談論我很低的考試分數。
say to sb. (非 say sb.): Before the game, the coach said to the players that they should enjoy playing and not worry about winning.
比賽前，教練對球員們說，他們應該享受比賽，不要擔心輸贏。
explain to me (非 explain me): The new game rules are hard, so could you explain them to me again before we start playing?
新的遊戲規則很難，所以在我們開始玩之前，你可以再向我解釋一次嗎？
be married to (非 with): My English teacher is married to a doctor, and they have two cute children who go to our school.
我的英文老師與一位醫生結婚，他們有兩個可愛的小孩在我們學校上學。
be used to + V-ing (習慣) vs. used to + V: I used to hate getting up early, but now I am used to waking up at six for morning practice.
我以前討厭早起，但現在我已經習慣六點醒來參加早上的練習了。
be similar to (非 with): Your new jacket is similar to mine, so people might think we bought them at the same store.
你的新夾克與我的很相似，所以人們可能會以為我們是在同一家店買的。
the answer to (非 of): Nobody in our class knew the answer to the last question, so the teacher explained it on the board.
我們班上沒有人知道最後一題的答案，所以老師在黑板上解釋了。
pay attention to (非 on): The teacher told us to pay attention to the signs on the road when we ride our bikes to school.
老師告訴我們騎腳踏車上學時要注意路上的標誌。
look forward to + V-ing: My whole family is looking forward to visiting Japan next winter because we all want to see the snow.
我全家都期待明年冬天去日本玩，因為我們都想看雪。
to the left (向左) vs. on the left (在左邊): Turn to the left at the corner, and you will see the bank on the left next to the bakery.
在轉角向左轉，你就會看到銀行在左邊，麵包店旁邊。
ten to six (5:50) vs. ten past six (6:10: The movie starts at ten to six, not ten past six, so we must leave home before five thirty.
電影五點五十分開始，不是六點十分，所以我們必須在五點半之前出門。
be kind to (對人) vs. be kind of (個性): Our new teacher is very kind to everyone, but she is kind of angry when we forget our homework.
我們的新老師對每個人都很好，但當我們忘記作業時，她有點生氣。
too (也／太) vs. to (到): It was too cold to go to the park, so we stayed home and my sister wanted to stay home too.
天氣太冷，沒辦法去公園，所以我們留在家裡，而且我姊姊也想待在家。
two / too / to: The two boys were too tired to walk to the station, so their mother drove them there in the car.
這兩個男孩太累了，走不到車站，所以他們的媽媽開車送他們到那裡。
be good to (對人好) vs. be good for (有益) vs: Jenny is good at math, she is good to her little brother, and she knows that milk is good for her bones.
珍妮擅長數學，她對她的小弟弟很好，而且她知道牛奶對她的骨頭有益。
be late for (遲到) vs. be late to: I was late for school again this morning because I was also late to the bus stop by five minutes.
我今天早上又上學遲到了，因為我到公車站也晚了五分鐘。
up to you (由你決定): We can have pizza or noodles for dinner tonight; it is up to you, so just tell me what you want.
今晚我們可以吃披薩或麵當晚餐；由你決定，所以只要告訴我你想吃什麼。
You can join the basketball team or the music club, and it's up to you, so think about it carefully this week.
你可以加入籃球隊或音樂社，由你決定，所以這週請仔細想一想。
walk toward the door: When the bell rang, the students put their books in their bags and walked toward the door quickly.
鈴聲響起時，學生們把書放進書包，然後快速朝門走去。
run toward me: I was waiting at the park, and my dog saw me and started to run toward me with a ball in its mouth.
我在公園等著，我的狗看到我，就嘴裡含著球開始朝我跑來。
turn toward the window: When she heard the loud thunder, Amy turned toward the window and saw the rain falling hard outside.
當艾咪聽到巨大的雷聲時，她轉向窗戶，看到外面雨下得很大。
look toward the sea: We sat on the beach, looked toward the sea, and watched the sun go down slowly behind the boats.
我們坐在沙灘上，望向海面，看著太陽慢慢地在船隻後方落下。
point toward the hill: The old farmer pointed toward the hill and told us that his house was just behind the tall trees.
老農夫指向山丘，告訴我們他的房子就在那些高大的樹後面。
a step toward peace: When the two angry boys finally shook hands after the fight, it was the first step toward peace in our class.
當那兩個生氣的男孩打架後終於握手時，那是我們班邁向和平的第一步。
move toward the exit: After the movie ended, hundreds of people stood up and moved toward the exit at the same time.
電影結束後，數百人同時站起來朝出口移動。
head toward home: The sky was getting dark, so we picked up our bags and started to head toward home before the rain came.
天色漸漸變暗，所以我們拿起包包，在下雨前開始朝家前進。
toward the end of the year: Toward the end of the year, the stores in the city are full of people buying gifts for their families.
接近年底時，城裡的商店擠滿了為家人買禮物的人。
toward evening: Toward evening, the wind became cooler, and the children stopped playing in the park and went home for dinner.
傍晚時分，風變涼了，孩子們不再在公園玩，回家吃晚餐。
toward midnight: Toward midnight, the streets were quiet, and only one small store near the station was still open.
接近午夜時，街道很安靜，只有車站附近的一家小店還開著。
be kind toward animals: My grandmother is always kind toward animals, and she feeds the hungry cats near her house every morning.
我奶奶總是對動物很友善，她每天早上都餵她家附近的飢餓貓咪。
feelings toward him: Her feelings toward him changed after he helped her carry the heavy boxes up the stairs in the rain.
在他幫她在雨中把沉重的箱子搬上樓梯之後，她對他的感覺改變了。
save money toward a car: My older brother works at a restaurant on weekends because he is saving money toward a car for next year.
我哥哥週末在餐廳工作，因為他正在為明年買車存錢。
work toward a goal: Our team practices every day after school because we are working toward the goal of winning the city game.
我們的球隊每天放學後都練習，因為我們正朝著贏得市賽的目標努力。
a change toward the better: After the new teacher came, there was a change toward the better in our class, and everyone studied harder.
新老師來了之後，我們班往好的方向改變，每個人都更用功讀書。
toward (朝向, 不一定到) vs. to (到達): The boy walked toward the park for ten minutes, but he never got to the park because it started to rain.
那個男孩朝公園走了十分鐘，但他從沒到達公園，因為開始下雨了。
walk toward the station (朝車站走): Tom walked toward the station to meet his friend, but he stopped at a store to buy some drinks first.
湯姆朝車站走去見朋友，但他先在一家店停下來買些飲料。
walk to the station (走到車站): Every morning my mother walks to the station, not just toward it, and then she takes the train to her office.
每天早上我媽媽走到車站，不只是朝它走去，然後她搭火車到她的辦公室。
toward: The little girl ran toward her father with a big smile, and he picked her up and gave her a big hug.
小女孩帶著大大的笑容朝她爸爸跑去，他抱起她並給她一個大大的擁抱。
toward (態度對象) vs. to (對象): His feelings toward the new student are warm, so he gave his lunch to the boy when he had no food.
他對這位新同學的態度很溫暖，所以當那個男孩沒有食物時，他把自己的午餐給了他。
Our teacher is always kind toward us, and she is also kind to the new student who speaks little Chinese.
我們的老師總是對我們很好，她對那位不太會說中文的新生也很好。
under the table: The cat likes to sleep under the table during dinner because it hopes we will drop some food for it.
這隻貓喜歡在晚餐時睡在桌子下，因為它希望我們會掉一些食物給它。
under the bed: I could not find my shoes this morning, and at last I found them under the bed with my socks.
今天早上我找不到鞋子，最後我在床下找到它們和我的襪子。
under the tree: It was very hot at noon, so the children sat under the tree and ate their ice cream in the cool air.
中午很熱，所以孩子們坐在樹下，在涼爽的空氣中吃冰淇淋。
under the bridge: When the rain started, we ran under the bridge and waited there until the sky became clear again.
下雨時，我們跑到橋下，在那裡等到天空再次放晴。
under the water: My brother can hold his breath under the water for one minute, but I can only do it for twenty seconds.
我弟弟可以在水下閉氣一分鐘，但我只能閉二十秒。
under the sea: Many strange and beautiful fish live under the sea, and some of them can even make their own light.
許多奇怪又美麗的魚生活在海底，有些甚至可以自己發光。
under the sun: We stood under the sun for an hour at the sports meet, so everyone was thirsty and wanted cold water.
運動會時我們在太陽下站了一小時，所以每個人都很渴，想喝冰水。
under one's arm: The boy ran out of the house with a basketball under his arm and went to meet his friends at the park.
男孩腋下夾著一顆籃球跑出房子，去公園和朋友見面。
under the ground: The train goes under the ground for most of the trip, so you cannot see anything outside the window.
這班火車大部分路程都在地底下行駛，所以你從窗外什麼也看不到。
under the sky: On the first night of our camping trip, we slept under the sky and counted the stars until we fell asleep.
露營旅行的第一晚，我們睡在天空下，數著星星直到睡著。
under a blanket: It was so cold last night that my little sister hid under a blanket and would not come out to brush her teeth.
昨晚非常冷，我的小妹妹躲在毯子下，不肯出來刷牙。
under the door: When nobody answered the door, the mailman pushed the letter under the door and walked away.
沒人來應門時，郵差把信從門縫下推進去，然後走開了。
under 18: You cannot buy beer in this store if you are under 18, so the clerk asked the young man to show his ID.
如果你未滿十八歲，就不能在這家店買啤酒，所以店員請那個年輕人出示證件。
under 100 dollars: I want to buy a birthday gift for my mom under 100 dollars because I only have a little money this month.
我想買一個一百元以下的生日禮物給媽媽，因為我這個月只有一點錢。
children under five: Children under five can enter the zoo for free, so my parents did not have to pay for my little brother.
五歲以下的孩子可以免費進動物園，所以我爸媽不用為我的小弟弟付錢。
under an hour: If there is no traffic, we can get to the beach in under an hour, so let's leave early in the morning.
如果不塞車，我們可以在不到一小時內到海邊，所以我們早上早點出發吧。
under the weather: Jack felt a little under the weather this morning, so his mother told him to stay home and rest in bed.
傑克今天早上覺得身體有點不舒服，所以他媽媽叫他待在家裡躺在床上休息。

under way: The new school building is already under way, and the workers say it will be finished before next summer.
新的學校大樓已經在進行中，工人們說明年夏天之前就會完工。
under repair: The bridge near our school is under repair this week, so we have to take a longer road to get there.
我們學校附近的橋這週在維修中，所以我們必須走比較遠的路才能到那裡。
under discussion: The plan for a new school garden is still under discussion, and the teachers will decide on it next Monday.
新校園花園的計畫仍在討論中，老師們下星期一會做決定。
under attack: In the movie, the small town was under attack from a giant monster, and everyone ran to the hills.
電影裡，小鎮受到一隻巨大怪獸的攻擊，大家都往山上跑。
under fire: The restaurant came under fire after many people got sick, and the owner said sorry on TV last night.
許多人生病後，這家餐廳受到批評，老闆昨晚在電視上道歉。
under one's breath: Jack was angry about the homework, so he said something under his breath that the teacher could not hear.
傑克對作業很生氣，所以他低聲說了一些老師聽不到的話。

這位名作家用男人的名字賣出她的第一本書，因為當時很少人讀女性寫的書。
under the law: Under the law, every child in Taiwan must go to school, and parents cannot keep their children at home to work.
依法，台灣的每個孩子都必須上學，家長不能讓孩子留在家裡工作。
under the rules: Under the rules of the game, each team has five players, and nobody can touch the ball with their feet.
根據這個比賽的規定，每隊有五名球員，而且沒有人可以用腳碰球。
under the influence of: Under the influence of his older brother, Tom started playing the guitar and now practices every evening.
在哥哥的影響下，湯姆開始彈吉他，現在每天晚上都練習。
under the care of: The sick puppy is under the care of a kind doctor, and he says it will be able to run again soon.
這隻生病的小狗由一位好心的醫生照顧，他說它很快就能再跑了。
under the leadership of: Under the leadership of our new captain, the basketball team won five games in a row this season.

我姊姊師從一位名師學鋼琴三年，現在她彈得很美。
under one's nose: I looked everywhere for my glasses, and they were right under my nose on the kitchen table the whole time.
我到處找眼鏡，結果它們一直就在我眼前，放在廚房的桌子上。
under lock and key: My grandfather keeps his old letters and photos under lock and key in a brown box in his bedroom.
我爺爺把他的舊信和照片鎖得好好的，放在他房間的一個棕色盒子裡。
under cover of darkness: In the story, the prince left the castle under cover of darkness so that the guards would not see him.
故事裡，王子在夜色掩護下離開城堡，這樣守衛就不會看到他。
under orders: The soldiers were under orders to stay at the bridge all night, so they could not go home for dinner.
士兵們奉命整夜守在橋邊，所以他們不能回家吃晚餐。

她以「我最好的朋友」為標題寫了一篇關於她的狗的短篇故事，全班都很喜歡。
under the same roof: My grandmother, my parents and I all live under the same roof, so dinner at our house is always loud and fun.

under water: After the heavy rain last night, the whole street was under water, and cars could not drive through it.
昨晚下大雨後，整條街都被水淹了，汽車無法開過去。

under one's thumb: In the movie, the king is under his wife's thumb, and he does everything she tells him to do.

go under: The small bookstore near our school went under last year because most students began buying books on the Internet.
我們學校附近的小書店去年倒閉了，因為大部分學生開始在網路上買書。
under study: The new medicine for the flu is still under study, so doctors cannot give it to patients yet.

門口的男人不讓那些男孩進入俱樂部，因為他們還未成年。
under the age of 12: Children under the age of 12 must sit in the back seat of the car, because the front seat is not safe for them.
未滿十二歲的孩子必須坐在汽車後座，因為前座對他們來說不安全。
under (正下方／覆蓋) vs. below (較低處): The ball is under the sofa, and the picture on the wall hangs below the clock, a little lower than it.
球在沙發正下方，而牆上的那幅畫掛在時鐘下方，比它低一點。

狗在桌子下睡覺，一株小植物放在窗戶下方的地板上。
under (少於) vs. less than: The movie tickets were under 200 dollars each, which means they cost less than I expected, so I bought two.
電影票每張不到兩百元，也就是說比我預期的便宜，所以我買了兩張。

我哥哥喜歡在沙灘上曬太陽，他說那是天底下最棒的感覺。
under way (進行中) vs. on the way (路上): The class meeting is already under way, but Tom is still on the way to school because his bus was late.
班會已經在進行中，但湯姆還在上學的路上，因為他的公車晚了。

老師讓吵鬧的班級保持在控制中，但當她離開教室時，學生們就失控了。
get up: On school days I get up at six thirty, but on Sundays I stay in bed until almost ten o'clock.

學游泳對麗莎來說很難，但她沒有放棄，現在她游得比她哥哥還快。

pick up the kids: My mother leaves work early every day so that she can pick up the kids from school at four o'clock.
我媽媽每天提早下班，這樣她才能在四點去學校接小孩。
pick up a language: Children can pick up a language quickly, so my little sister learned a lot of Japanese from watching cartoons.

look up a word: When I read an English story and see a new word, I look up the word in my dictionary right away.
當我讀英文故事看到新單字時，我會馬上在字典裡查那個單字。

許多學生尊敬王老師，因為她是一位總是傾聽他們問題的好老師。
turn up: We waited for Kevin at the restaurant for an hour, but he did not turn up until everyone had finished dinner.
我們在餐廳等凱文等了一小時，但他直到大家吃完晚餐才出現。
show up: Only ten people showed up at the school party last night because it was raining hard all evening.
昨晚只有十個人出現在學校派對上，因為整個晚上都在下大雨。
make up a story: My little brother likes to make up a story about a brave cat every night before he goes to sleep.
我的小弟弟每晚睡前都喜歡編一個關於勇敢貓咪的故事。
make up one's mind: After thinking about it for a week, Mary finally made up her mind to join the school swimming team.
想了一個星期後，瑪麗終於下定決心加入學校游泳隊。

湯姆和傑克星期一大吵了一架，但他們在週末前就和好了。

珍妮錯過了好朋友的生日派對，所以她隔天烤了餅乾來彌補。
put up a tent: It took my father and me almost an hour to put up a tent on the beach because the wind was so strong.
我爸爸和我在海邊花了快一小時搭帳篷，因為風太強了。
put up with: I cannot put up with the loud music from the apartment next door anymore, so I will talk to the neighbor tonight.

put up one's hand: If you know the answer to the question, please put up your hand instead of shouting it out in class.
如果你知道這個問題的答案，請舉手，而不要在課堂上大聲喊出來。
set up a company: My uncle set up a company that sells tea on the Internet, and now he has five people working for him.

hurry up: Hurry up and put on your shoes, or we will miss the school bus and have to walk in the rain.

司機在高速公路上必須加速，因為我們要趕不上姊姊在台北的鋼琴表演了。
dress up: For the school party, all the students dressed up as their favorite movie characters and took funny pictures.

eat up: Mom told my little brother to eat up his vegetables before he could have any chocolate cake for dessert.
媽媽叫我的小弟弟先把蔬菜吃完，才可以吃巧克力蛋糕當點心。
drink up: The coach told us to drink up our water before the game because it was very hot outside today.
教練叫我們比賽前把水喝完，因為今天外面非常熱。
use up: We used up all the eggs making the cake this morning, so I have to go to the store before dinner.

開長途車去山上之前，我爸爸在加油站停下來把油加滿。
fill up the form: To join the swimming club, you need to fill up the form and give it to the teacher by Friday.

bring up a child: It is not easy to bring up a child alone, but my aunt did it well, and her son is a doctor now.

bring up a topic: At dinner, my brother brought up the topic of getting a dog, but my parents quickly changed the subject.
晚餐時，我哥哥提起養狗的話題，但我爸媽很快就換了話題。
break up: The famous band decided to break up after ten years together, and many fans cried when they heard the news.
這個著名的樂團在一起十年後決定解散，許多粉絲聽到這個消息都哭了。
catch up with: Peter was sick for two weeks, so now he has to study hard every night to catch up with the other students.
彼得生病了兩個星期，所以現在他每晚都得用功讀書才能趕上其他學生。
keep up with: The teacher speaks very fast in English class, and sometimes it is hard for me to keep up with her.

come up with an idea: We needed a name for our team, and Lisa came up with an idea that everyone in the group liked at once.

end up doing: We planned to study at the library, but we ended up playing basketball in the park all afternoon.

stay up late: Jack stayed up late last night to finish his science report, so he fell asleep in math class this morning.
傑克昨晚熬夜完成他的科學報告，所以今天早上他在數學課上睡著了。
sit up: The teacher told us to sit up straight in our chairs because sitting badly is not good for our backs.
老師叫我們在椅子上坐直，因為坐姿不良對我們的背不好。
take up a hobby: After he moved to a small town, my grandfather took up a hobby and now paints pictures of birds every day.
搬到一個小鎮後，我爺爺開始了一項嗜好，現在每天畫鳥的圖畫。
take up space: The old piano takes up too much space in our small living room, so my parents want to sell it.

take up time: Playing games on my phone takes up too much time, so I decided to use it for only one hour a day.
用手機玩遊戲占了太多時間，所以我決定一天只用一小時。
call up: If you forget what time the game starts, just call up Mike, because he always remembers these things.

hang up the phone: My mother was angry because I hung up the phone before she finished telling me what to buy at the store.

hang up the coat: When you come into the house, please hang up your coat by the door and put your shoes on the shelf.
進屋時，請把外套掛在門邊，並把鞋子放在架子上。
hold up: The heavy rain held up the trains for two hours, so many people were late for work in the city.
大雨使火車延誤了兩小時，所以很多人在市區上班遲到了。
back up: You should back up the photos on your phone every month, or you might lose them all if the phone breaks.

blow up: We spent an hour blowing up balloons for the birthday party, and then two of them blew up with a loud noise.

burn up: The old house on the hill burned up in the fire last night, but luckily nobody was living in it.
山上的老房子昨晚在火災中燒毀了，但幸運的是沒有人住在裡面。
check up on: My mother often calls my grandmother in the evening to check up on her and make sure she is eating well.
我媽媽常在晚上打電話給奶奶查看她的狀況，確認她吃得好。
cut up: Before you make the soup, cut up the carrots and onions into small pieces and put them in the pot.

do up one's buttons: It was cold outside, so my mother told my little brother to do up his buttons before he left for school.

draw up a plan: Before the class trip, the teacher asked us to draw up a plan for what we would do each day in Tainan.
班級旅行之前，老師請我們擬定一份在台南每天要做什麼的計畫。
dry up: It did not rain for three months last summer, so the small river near our village dried up completely.

face up to: Tom did not want to face up to the fact that he failed the test, but his mother made him talk about it.
湯姆不想面對他考試不及格的事實，但他媽媽要他談談這件事。
fix up: My father spent the whole weekend fixing up my old bike, and now it looks almost like a new one.

grow up to be: Mary loves animals so much that everyone thinks she will grow up to be an animal doctor one day.

heat up: Dinner is already in the kitchen, so just heat up the soup for two minutes before you eat it.

lock up: Please lock up the music room when you leave, and give the key to the teacher in the office.

當老師叫他的名字時，傑克從書本中抬頭看，發現大家都在笑他。

own up to: Nobody wanted to own up to breaking the window, so the teacher kept the whole class in the room after school.

當你的小妹妹想告訴你事情時，叫她閉嘴是不禮貌的。
sign up for: Many students signed up for the school basketball club because the new coach is young and very friendly.
很多學生報名參加學校籃球社，因為新教練年輕又很友善。
speak up: The people at the back of the room could not hear Tom, so the teacher asked him to speak up.
教室後面的人聽不到湯姆的聲音，所以老師請他大聲說。
stand up for: My best friend always stands up for me when other kids laugh at my old shoes or my glasses.
當別的小孩笑我的舊鞋子或眼鏡時，我最好的朋友總是站出來捍衛我。
stand up to: Mary was afraid at first, but she finally stood up to the big boy who took her lunch money.
瑪麗一開始很害怕，但她終於勇敢面對那個拿走她午餐錢的大男孩。
start up: My father started up the car early in the morning so that it would be warm when we left.
爸爸一大早就啟動車子，好讓我們出門時車裡是暖的。
take up: After he watched the games on TV, my cousin decided to take up swimming at the city pool this summer.
看了電視上的比賽之後，我表哥決定今年夏天開始在市立游泳池學游泳。
tidy up: Before Grandma and Grandpa arrive for dinner, Mom asked us to tidy up the living room and wash the dishes.
在爺爺奶奶來吃晚餐之前，媽媽要我們整理客廳並洗碗。
tie up: Please tie up the dog outside the store, because animals are not allowed inside the supermarket.
請把狗綁好在商店外面，因為超市裡面不准動物進入。
warm up: The players always warm up for ten minutes before the game so that they do not hurt their legs.
球員們總是在比賽前熱身十分鐘，這樣才不會傷到腿。
wash up: After the big family dinner, my sister and I washed up in the kitchen while Dad made some tea.
大家庭的晚餐之後，我和姊姊在廚房洗碗，爸爸則泡了茶。
write up: Our science teacher asked us to write up the results of our science project and hand them in on Friday.
我們的自然老師要我們把科學專題的結果寫成報告，星期五交。
add up: The waiter added up the bill, but the numbers did not add up, so my father asked him to check again.
服務生把帳單加總，但數字不合理，所以爸爸請他再檢查一次。
He says he was at home all night, but his friend saw him at the park, so it doesn't add up.
他說他整晚都在家，但他的朋友在公園看到他，所以這說不通。
be up: My grandmother is always up before six because she likes to walk in the park when the air is cool.
我奶奶總是六點前就起床了，因為她喜歡在空氣涼爽時到公園散步。
Time is up, so please put down your pencils and pass your test papers to the front of the room.
時間到了，請放下鉛筆，把考卷傳到教室前面。
What's up?: Lisa saw her brother crying on the sofa and asked him what's up, but he did not want to talk.
麗莎看到弟弟在沙發上哭，就問他怎麼了，但他不想說。
The two boys were talking quietly behind the tree, and the teacher knew they were up to something again.
那兩個男孩在樹後小聲說話，老師知道他們又在忙著做壞事了。
It is up to you whether we go to the movies or stay home and play cards tonight.
今晚我們要去看電影還是留在家裡玩牌，由你決定。
be up for: Are you up for a game of basketball after school, or are you too tired from the long test?
放學後你願意來打一場籃球嗎，還是長長的考試讓你太累了？
be up against: Our small school team is up against the best players in the city, so we must practice harder this week.
我們小小的校隊面臨全市最強的球員，所以這週必須更努力練習。
be fed up with: I am fed up with my noisy neighbors, because they play loud music every night until twelve o'clock.
我受夠了吵鬧的鄰居，因為他們每晚都放大聲的音樂直到十二點。
be up and about: Grandpa was very sick last week, but he is up and about now and even walks to the market.
爺爺上週病得很重，但他現在已經病後起床活動了，甚至還走路去市場。
be well up on: My uncle is well up on computers, so we always ask him for help when ours stops working.
我叔叔很了解電腦，所以我們的電腦壞掉時總是請他幫忙。
up to now: Up to now, I have read five books this summer, and I want to finish two more before school starts.
到目前為止，今年夏天我已經讀了五本書，我想在開學前再讀完兩本。
up to date: Our school library keeps its computers up to date, so students can find new information for their reports quickly.
我們學校圖書館的電腦保持最新的狀態，所以學生可以很快找到寫報告的新資訊。
up to 50 people: The new meeting room is quite big, and it can hold up to fifty people for a meeting or a party.
新的會議室相當大，開會或辦派對最多可以容納五十人。
up and down: The little boy was so excited about the trip that he jumped up and down on the bed all morning.
小男孩對這次旅行好興奮，整個早上都在床上上上下下地跳。
up in the air: Our plans for the weekend trip are still up in the air because we do not know if it will rain.
我們週末旅行的計畫仍然懸而未決，因為我們不知道會不會下雨。
up the stairs: The lift was broken, so we had to carry the heavy boxes up the stairs to the top floor.
電梯壞了，所以我們得把沉重的箱子搬上樓梯到頂樓。
up the hill: Every Sunday morning, my father and I ride our bikes up the hill to watch the sun come up.
每個星期天早上，爸爸和我騎腳踏車上山丘看日出。
up the street: Walk up the street for about five minutes, and you will see the post office on your left.
沿街往上走大約五分鐘，你就會看到郵局在你的左邊。
up north: My grandfather and grandmother live up north in Taipei, so we take the train to visit them during the winter holiday.
我的爺爺奶奶住在北方的臺北，所以寒假時我們搭火車去看他們。
up the river: The boat moved slowly up the river, and we saw many birds and tall green trees along the way.
船慢慢地往上游行駛，沿途我們看到許多鳥和高大的綠樹。
look up at the sky: We lay on the grass after the picnic and looked up at the sky to count the white clouds.
野餐後我們躺在草地上仰望天空，數著白雲。
up close: I had only seen elephants on TV before, so it was exciting to see one up close at the zoo.
我以前只在電視上看過大象，所以在動物園近看一頭大象好刺激。
up front: The hotel asked my parents to pay up front for the room, so Dad paid the man before we went upstairs.
飯店要求我爸媽預先付房費，所以爸爸在我們上樓前就把錢給了那位先生。
up to one's ears in work: My mother is up to her ears in work this month, so she often comes home after nine at night.
我媽媽這個月工作忙得不可開交，所以她常常晚上九點後才回家。
up in arms: The parents were up in arms when the school said it would close the swimming pool to save money.
當學校說為了省錢要關閉游泳池時，家長們憤怒抗議。
up to no good: The two boys were hiding behind the school wall after class, and I was sure they were up to no good.
下課後那兩個男孩躲在學校牆後面，我確定他們沒幹好事。
not up to much: The movie we watched last night was not up to much, so we left before it ended and got ice cream.
我們昨晚看的電影不怎麼樣，所以還沒結束就離開去買冰淇淋了。
up for sale: The old house at the end of our street is up for sale, and my aunt wants to buy it.
我們街尾的那間老房子待售中，我阿姨想買下來。
up and running: The new school computer system is up and running now, so students can check their homework on the computer every evening.
學校的新電腦系統現在運作中，所以學生每天晚上都可以用電腦查作業。
on the up: My grades were poor last year, but they are on the up now because I study with a friend every night.
我去年的成績很差，但現在正在好轉，因為我每晚都和朋友一起讀書。
up the wall: The loud noise from the new building next door is driving my father up the wall this week.
隔壁新大樓傳來的巨大噪音，這週快把我爸爸弄得發瘋了。
one up on: Jack is always trying to be one up on his older brother, so he studied all night for the English test.
傑克總是想勝過他哥哥一籌，所以他為了英文考試熬夜讀書。
up to the mark: The coach said my running was not up to the mark, so I have to practice every morning before school.
教練說我的跑步還沒達標，所以我每天早上上學前都要練習。
dressed up: Everyone was dressed up for my cousin's wedding, and my little brother looked funny in his new black suit.
大家都為了我表姊的婚禮穿著正式，我弟弟穿新的黑西裝看起來很滑稽。
up to scratch: My English report was not up to scratch, so the teacher asked me to write it again over the weekend.
我的英文報告沒有達到標準，所以老師要我週末重寫一次。
up to here: Please read the story up to here tonight, and tomorrow we will talk about what happens to the brave girl.
今晚請把故事讀到這裡，明天我們再討論那個勇敢的女孩發生了什麼事。
up to standard: The food in the new restaurant was not up to standard, so my parents decided not to go there again.
新餐廳的食物沒有達標，所以我爸媽決定不再去那裡了。
time's up: When the teacher said time's up, half of the students were still writing the last question on the test.
當老師說時間到時，有一半的學生還在寫考卷最後一題。
the game is up: When his mother found the broken plate under the bed, Tim knew the game was up and said sorry.
當媽媽在床底下發現打破的盤子時，提姆知道計謀被揭穿了，就道歉了。
up (向上) vs. down (向下): The price of vegetables went up after the heavy rain, but the price of rice went down a little this month.
大雨之後蔬菜價格往上漲，但這個月米價往下跌了一點。
turn up (調大) vs. turn down (調小／拒絕): Please turn up the TV because I cannot hear the news, but turn down the music in your room.
請把電視音量調大，因為我聽不到新聞，但把你房間的音樂調小。
get up (起床) vs. wake up (醒來): I usually wake up at six when the birds start to sing, but I do not get up until seven.
我通常六點在鳥開始唱歌時醒來，但七點才起床。
grow up (長大) vs. grow (生長): When I grow up, I want to be a farmer and grow sweet corn and tomatoes on my own land.
我長大後想當農夫，在自己的土地上種甜玉米和番茄。
look up (查) vs. look up to (尊敬) vs. look: I look up to my English teacher because she never looks down on students who have to look up every word.
我很尊敬我的英文老師，因為她從不看不起那些必須每個字都查的學生。
pick up (接／撿) vs. pick out (挑選): Mom will pick me up after school, and then we will pick out a birthday present for Dad together.
媽媽放學後會來接我，然後我們會一起挑選爸爸的生日禮物。
put up with (忍受) vs. put up (搭建): We put up our tent by the lake, but we could not put up with the hungry mosquitoes all night.
我們在湖邊搭起帳篷，但整晚都無法忍受飢餓的蚊子。
make up (編／和好／彌補): My sister made up a funny story about a talking cat to make up with me after our fight.
我姊姊編了一個會說話的貓的有趣故事，想在我們吵架後和我和好。
bring up (養育／提起) vs. grow up (長大): My grandmother brought up six children in a small village, and all of them grew up to be teachers.
我奶奶在小村子裡養育了六個孩子，他們全都長大成為老師。
catch up with (趕上) vs. keep up with (跟上): I was sick for a week, so now I must catch up with the class and keep up with the new lessons.
我病了一個星期，所以現在必須趕上班上的進度，然後跟上新的課程。
stay up (熬夜) vs. sit up: My parents do not let me stay up late on school nights, so I never sit up watching TV after ten.
我爸媽不讓我在上學日的晚上熬夜，所以我從不在十點後熬夜看電視。
up to date (最新) vs. out of date (過時): This map is out of date because the new road is not on it, so let's buy an up to date one.
這張地圖過時了，因為新路不在上面，所以我們買一張最新的吧。
be up to sb. (由某人決定) vs. be up to sth. (: It is up to Dad whether we can keep the puppy, but the puppy is up to something in the kitchen now.
我們能不能養這隻小狗由爸爸決定，但小狗現在正在廚房搞鬼。
up (副詞) vs. up (介係詞 + 名詞): The old man stood up slowly, picked up his bag, and then walked up the hill to his little house.
老先生慢慢站起來，拿起袋子，然後走上山丘到他的小房子。
use up (用完) vs. run out of: We used up all the eggs for breakfast, so we ran out of eggs and Mom had to go shopping.
我們早餐把蛋全用完了，所以蛋用光了，媽媽只好去買東西。
fill up (加滿) vs. fill in / fill out (填表): Dad filled up the car with gas, and then he filled out a form to join the gas station club.
爸爸把車加滿油，然後填了一張表格加入加油站的會員。
end up (最後成為) vs. in the end: We planned to eat pizza, but in the end the shop was closed, so we ended up eating noodles at home.
我們原本打算吃披薩，但最後店關了，所以我們最後在家吃麵。
hang up (掛電話) vs. hold on (稍等): Please hold on for a minute and do not hang up, because my mother is coming to the phone now.
請稍等一下，不要掛電話，因為我媽媽現在正要過來接電話。
once upon a time: Once upon a time, a poor young farmer lived with his old mother in a small house near the forest.
從前從前，有一個貧窮的年輕農夫和他年老的母親住在森林附近的小房子裡。
upon arriving: Upon arriving at the hotel, we put down our bags and ran to the beach to swim in the warm sea.
一到飯店，我們就放下行李，跑到海邊在溫暖的海水裡游泳。
upon hearing the news: Upon hearing the news that she won first prize, Amy jumped up from her seat and hugged her mother.
一聽到她得了第一名的消息，艾美就從座位上跳起來抱住媽媽。
depend upon: Whether we have the picnic on Saturday will depend upon the weather, so please watch the news tonight.
我們星期六會不會去野餐要依賴天氣而定，所以今晚請看新聞。
look upon A as B: My grandfather and grandmother look upon our old dog as a member of the family, so he eats dinner with us.
我的爺爺奶奶把我們的老狗視為家中的一員，所以牠和我們一起吃晚餐。
upon my word: Upon my word, I did not touch your cake, because I was playing basketball outside the whole afternoon.
我保證，我沒有碰你的蛋糕，因為我整個下午都在外面打籃球。
come upon: While we were walking in the mountains, we came upon a small old temple hidden behind some tall trees.
我們在山裡走路時，偶然發現一座藏在高樹後面的小古廟。
fall upon: A heavy storm fell upon the small fishing town at night, and many boats were broken by the big waves.
一場大風暴在夜裡襲擊了那個小漁鎮，許多船被大浪打壞了。
Christmas is upon us again, so my sister and I are making cards for our teachers and friends.
聖誕節又快到了，所以我和姊姊正在做卡片給老師和朋友。
year upon year: Year upon year, the old farmer plants rice in the same field and sells it at the market in town.
年復一年，老農夫在同一塊田裡種稻，然後在鎮上的市場賣。
put the blame upon: It was not fair to put the blame upon the youngest player when the whole team played badly.
全隊都打得不好時，把責任推給最年輕的球員是不公平的。
upon: In the old story, the king placed his hand upon the shoulder of the brave young soldier and thanked him.
在那個古老的故事裡，國王把手放在勇敢的年輕士兵肩上，向他道謝。
on arriving: On arriving home, Dad turned on the TV, and upon hearing the news about the storm, he called Grandma.
一到家，爸爸就打開電視，而一聽到風暴的消息，他就打電話給奶奶。
once upon a time (固定說法, 不用 on): Every story my grandmother tells at night starts with once upon a time, and we always ask for one more.
奶奶每晚講的每個故事都以從前從前開頭，而我們總是要求再講一個。
upon (書面) vs. on (口語): My English teacher told us that upon is often used in writing, but we usually say on when we talk with friends.
英文老師告訴我們 upon 常用於書面語，但和朋友聊天時我們通常說 on。
write with a pen: You should write with a pen on the test, because the teacher cannot read the words you wrote with a pencil.
考試時你應該用筆寫，因為老師看不清你用鉛筆寫的字。
eat with chopsticks: My American friend learned to eat with chopsticks when he visited Taiwan, and now he uses them every day.
我的美國朋友來臺灣時學會用筷子吃飯，現在他每天都用筷子。
see with one's own eyes: I did not believe the river was so dirty until I saw it with my own eyes last weekend.
直到上週末親眼看見，我才相信那條河那麼髒。
with a smile: The shop owner greeted every customer with a smile, so people liked to buy bread from her small store.
店老闆帶著微笑迎接每位顧客，所以人們喜歡到她的小店買麵包。
with care: Please carry the glass plates with care, because they were a gift from my grandmother many years ago.
請小心地拿這些玻璃盤，因為那是我奶奶多年前送的禮物。
with pleasure: I will help you clean the room after class with pleasure, because you helped me with my math homework last week.
我很樂意地在下課後幫你打掃教室，因為你上週幫我做了數學作業。
with ease: Lily passed the English test with ease because she reads English stories for thirty minutes every night.
莉莉輕鬆地通過英文考試，因為她每晚讀三十分鐘的英文故事。
with luck: With luck, the rain will stop before noon, and we can still have our picnic in the park this afternoon.
幸運的話，雨會在中午前停，我們今天下午還是可以在公園野餐。
with all my heart: I love my grandmother with all my heart, so I visit her every weekend and cook dinner for her.
我全心全意地愛我的奶奶，所以我每個週末都去看她，為她做晚餐。
with difficulty: The old man climbed the stairs with difficulty, so a kind young student helped him carry his heavy bag.
老先生費力地爬樓梯，所以一位好心的年輕學生幫他拿沉重的袋子。
with joy: The children shouted with joy when their teacher said there would be no homework during the long holiday.
當老師說長假期間沒有作業時，孩子們高興地大叫。
with one's help: With my father's help, I finished the model plane in two hours and flew it in the park.
在爸爸的幫助下，我兩小時就做完模型飛機，並在公園放飛它。
with one voice: When the teacher asked if we wanted a class trip to the beach, all the students answered yes with one voice.
當老師問我們想不想去海邊班遊時，所有學生異口同聲地回答想。
with open arms: My grandfather and grandmother welcomed us with open arms when we arrived at their farm for the summer holidays.
我們暑假抵達爺爺奶奶的農場時，他們熱情地歡迎我們。
with the lights on: My little sister is afraid of the dark, so she always sleeps with the lights on in her room.
我妹妹怕黑，所以她總是在房間裡開著燈睡覺。
with your mouth full: Mom told my brother not to talk with his mouth full, because it is not polite at the dinner table.
媽媽叫弟弟不要嘴裡塞滿食物還講話，因為在餐桌上這樣不禮貌。
with time: With time, the pain in my leg became less, and after two months I could play basketball again.
隨著時間過去，我腿上的疼痛減輕了，兩個月後我又能打籃球了。
with age: My grandfather's hair turned white with age, but he still rides his bike to the market every morning.
爺爺的頭髮隨著年齡變白了，但他每天早上仍騎腳踏車去市場。
with the wind: The boat sailed with the wind across the lake, so we reached the other side in only ten minutes.
船順風駛過湖面，所以我們只花十分鐘就到了對岸。
with a view to: My brother is learning Japanese with a view to studying in Japan after he finishes high school next year.
我哥哥正在學日文，為了明年高中畢業後去日本讀書。
with respect to: With respect to the school trip, the teacher said we must bring a hat, water, and our lunch on Friday.
關於校外教學，老師說我們星期五必須帶帽子、水和午餐。
with the help of: With the help of a kind police officer, the lost little girl found her mother at the night market.
在一位好心警察的幫助下，走失的小女孩在夜市找到了媽媽。
with no doubt: With no doubt, Mary is the best singer in our class, so she will sing at the school party.
毫無疑問，瑪麗是我們班最會唱歌的人，所以她會在學校派對上唱歌。
without doubt (非 with): Without doubt, summer is the best season for swimming, because the water in the sea is warm and clear.
無疑地，夏天是最適合游泳的季節，因為海水溫暖又清澈。
with a heavy heart: With a heavy heart, Tom said goodbye to his best friend, who was moving to Japan with his family.
湯姆心情沉重地向最好的朋友道別，他的朋友要和家人搬去日本。
with one's eyes closed: My brother can play that song on the piano with his eyes closed because he has practiced it a hundred times.
我哥哥可以閉著眼睛彈那首鋼琴曲，因為他已經練了一百次。
with the door open: Please do not leave the room with the door open, because the cold air from outside will come in.
請不要讓房間門開著就離開，因為外面的冷空氣會進來。
with a book in hand: Every afternoon, my grandfather sits under the big tree with a book in hand and reads until dinner time.
每天下午，爺爺手拿著書坐在大樹下，一直讀到晚餐時間。
with my family: I usually go to the mountains with my family on the weekend, and we have a picnic by the river.
週末我通常和我家人一起去山上，我們會在河邊野餐。
go with you: I will go with you to the new bookstore after school if you help me finish my math homework first.
如果你先幫我做完數學作業，放學後我會和你一起去新書店。
come with me: Come with me to the kitchen, and I will show you how to make the noodles my grandmother taught me.
跟我來廚房，我會教你怎麼做我奶奶教我的麵。
At the school party, Jack was too shy to dance with Mary, so he just stood by the window.
在學校派對上，傑克太害羞而不敢和瑪麗跳舞，所以他只是站在窗邊。
play with friends: After I finish my homework, Mom lets me play with friends in the park until it gets dark.
我做完作業後，媽媽讓我和朋友在公園玩到天黑。
When I have a problem at school, I like to talk with my mother because she always listens carefully.
當我在學校遇到問題時，我喜歡和媽媽談話，因為她總是仔細聽。
stay with us: My cousin from Tainan will stay with us for a week, so we are getting the small room ready for her.
我臺南的表妹會和我們住一個星期，所以我們正在為她準備小房間。
live with one's parents: My older brother still lives with our parents because houses in the city cost too much money these days.
我哥哥還和父母同住，因為現在城裡的房子太貴了。
I argued with my sister about who should wash the dishes, so Mom made us do them together.
我和姊姊爭論誰該洗碗，所以媽媽叫我們一起洗。
Peter fought with a boy in his class over a ball, and both of them had to see the teacher.
彼得為了一顆球和班上一個男孩打架，兩個人都得去見老師。
I agree with my mother that too much TV is bad, but I still want to watch one show a day.
我同意媽媽說看太多電視不好，但我還是想一天看一個節目。
Lisa always shares her lunch with her friends, so everyone in the class likes to sit next to her.
麗莎總是和朋友分享她的午餐，所以班上每個人都喜歡坐在她旁邊。
a girl with long hair: The girl with long hair sitting in the front row is my cousin, and she sings very well.
坐在前排那個長頭髮的女孩是我表妹，她唱歌唱得很好。
a man with a dog: A man with a big brown dog walks past our school every morning, and the children always wave to him.
每天早上都有一個帶著大棕狗的男人走過我們學校，孩子們總是向他揮手。
a house with a garden: My grandfather and grandmother live in a house with a garden, where they grow tomatoes and beautiful red roses.
我爺爺奶奶住在一間有花園的房子，他們在那裡種番茄和美麗的紅玫瑰。
coffee with milk: My father drinks coffee with milk every morning, but my mother likes hers black with no sugar.
我爸爸每天早上喝加牛奶的咖啡，但我媽媽喜歡不加糖的黑咖啡。
a room with a view: We paid a little more for a room with a view, and we could see the whole blue sea from our window.
我們多付了一點錢訂一間有景觀的房間，從窗戶可以看到整片藍色大海。
a boy with glasses: The boy with glasses in the corner is the best student in our class, and he helps everyone with math.
角落那個戴眼鏡的男孩是我們班最好的學生，他幫大家學數學。
a shirt with a hole: I cannot wear this shirt with a hole in it to school, so I need to buy a new one this weekend.
我不能穿這件有破洞的襯衫去上學，所以這週末我需要買一件新的。
with 100 dollars: With one hundred dollars, you can buy a bowl of noodles and a drink at the night market near our school.
帶著一百元，你可以在我們學校附近的夜市買一碗麵和一杯飲料。
Mom was angry with me because I came home late and forgot to call her from my friend's house.
媽媽生我的氣，因為我晚回家，又忘了從朋友家打電話給她。
be pleased with: My teacher was pleased with my English report, so she read part of it to the whole class.
老師對我的英文報告很滿意，所以她把其中一部分讀給全班聽。
be happy with: I am happy with my new bike, because it is light and fast and was not very expensive.
我對我的新腳踏車很滿意，因為它又輕又快，而且不太貴。
be satisfied with: The customers were satisfied with the food and the friendly service, so they came back to the restaurant again.
顧客對食物和友善的服務很滿意，所以他們又回到那家餐廳。
be bored with: My brother is bored with his old video games, so he wants to spend his money on a new one.
我弟弟對他的舊電動遊戲感到無聊，所以他想把錢花在買新的上。
be busy with homework: I was busy with homework all weekend, so I could not go to the movies with my friends.
我整個週末都忙於作業，所以不能和朋友去看電影。
be careful with money: My grandmother taught me to be careful with money, so I always write down what I buy each day.
奶奶教我要小心用錢，所以我總是記下每天買了什麼。
be filled with: The whole room was filled with happy voices when the teacher told us a funny story about her cat.
當老師講她的貓的有趣故事時，整個教室裡充滿了快樂的聲音。
be crowded with people: The night market was crowded with people on Saturday, so we waited twenty minutes for a bowl of noodles.
星期六夜市擠滿了人，所以我們等了二十分鐘才買到一碗麵。
be popular with students: The new PE teacher is very popular with students because he plays basketball with us after class.
新的體育老師很受學生歡迎，因為他下課後會和我們打籃球。
be patient with: My mother is always patient with my little brother, even when he asks the same question ten times.
媽媽對我弟弟總是很有耐心，即使他同一個問題問了十次。
be in love with: My older sister is in love with a boy from her music class, and she talks about him every day.
我姊姊愛上了她音樂課上的一個男孩，每天都談到他。
be wrong with: Something is wrong with my phone, because it turns off by itself every time I try to take a picture.
我的手機有問題，因為每次我想拍照它就自己關機。
What's wrong with you?: You have not said a word all morning, so what's wrong with you, and did something happen at home?
你整個早上一句話都沒說，你怎麼了，家裡發生什麼事了嗎？
What's the matter with you?: You look so tired and you did not eat your lunch at all, so tell me, what's the matter with you?
你看起來好累，午餐也完全沒吃，告訴我，你怎麼了？
be done with: When you are done with the computer, please turn it off, because your sister needs to use it later.
當你用完電腦時，請把它關掉，因為你妹妹晚一點要用。
be good with children: My aunt is very good with children, so all the kids on our street love to visit her house.
我阿姨很會帶小孩，所以我們街上所有的小孩都愛去她家。
be good with one's hands: My grandfather is good with his hands, and he made this wood table and the chairs by himself.
我爺爺手很巧，這張木桌和椅子都是他自己做的。
be friends with: I have been friends with Amy since first grade, and we still walk to school together every morning.
我從一年級起就和艾美是朋友，我們現在每天早上仍一起走路上學。
be fine with me: If you want to meet at the library instead of the park, that is fine with me, so just send a message.
如果你想在圖書館而不是公園見面，我沒意見，傳個訊息就好。
be OK with it: Dad wants to have dinner at seven instead of six, and everyone in the family is OK with it.
爸爸想七點而不是六點吃晚餐，家裡每個人都可以接受。
be honest with: You should be honest with your parents about the broken window, because they will find out anyway.
你應該對父母坦誠窗戶打破的事，因為他們反正會發現。
be gentle with: Please be gentle with the baby rabbit, because it is very small and gets scared easily.
請溫柔對待這隻小兔子，因為它很小，很容易受到驚嚇。
be sick with a cold: Jenny was sick with a cold last week, so she stayed in bed and missed the school sports day.
珍妮上週感冒生病，所以她躺在床上休息，錯過了學校運動會。
be down with the flu: Half of my class was down with the flu in January, so the teacher moved the big test to February.
一月時我們班有一半的人因流感病倒，所以老師把大考移到二月。
be ill with: My grandfather has been ill with a bad cough for two weeks, so we are taking him to the doctor tomorrow.
我爺爺患嚴重的咳嗽病已經兩個星期，所以我們明天要帶他去看醫生。
shake with fear: The little boy was shaking with fear when he saw the big black dog running toward him in the park.
小男孩看到大黑狗在公園朝他跑來時，怕得發抖。
jump with joy: My sister jumped with joy when she opened the box and found the new phone she had wanted for months.
我姊姊打開盒子發現她想了好幾個月的新手機時，高興得跳起來。
cry with pain: Tom fell off his bike and cried with pain, so his father carried him home and put ice on his knee.
湯姆從腳踏車上摔下來痛得哭了，所以爸爸把他抱回家，在他膝蓋上敷冰。
die with hunger (錯) → die of hunger: During the long war with no food in the shops, many poor people in the town died of hunger.
在商店裡沒有食物的漫長戰爭期間，鎮上許多窮人死於飢餓。
be red with anger: Dad's face was red with anger when he saw that someone had broken the window of his new car.
爸爸看到有人打破他新車的車窗時，氣得臉紅。
be white with fear: Her face was white with fear when the lights went out and she heard a strange noise in the kitchen.
燈熄了，她聽到廚房傳來奇怪的聲音時，嚇得臉色發白。
be green with envy: When Jack showed us his new game, his little brother was green with envy and asked Mom for one too.
傑克給我們看他的新遊戲時，他弟弟羨慕得眼紅，也向媽媽要一個。
burst with pride: My parents were bursting with pride when I walked up to the stage to get the first prize for English.
當我走上舞台領英文第一名的獎時，我爸媽充滿驕傲。
help sb. with homework: My older sister often helps me with my homework, especially when I do not understand the math problems.
我姊姊常常幫我做作業，尤其是我看不懂數學題目的時候。
The school provides every student with a hot lunch, so we do not have to bring food from home.
學校提供每位學生熱的午餐，所以我們不必從家裡帶食物。
fill the glass with water: Please fill the glass with water for Grandma, because she needs to take her medicine after dinner.
請把杯子裝滿水給奶奶，因為她晚餐後需要吃藥。
compare A with B: When you compare this phone with the old one, you can see that the new camera takes much better pictures.
當你比較這支手機和舊的那支，你會發現新相機拍的照片好得多。
deal with the problem: Our teacher taught us how to deal with the problem in a kind way when we have a fight with a friend.
老師教我們和朋友吵架時要如何用友善的方式處理問題。
do with: I do not know what to do with these old books, so maybe I will give them to the school library.
我不知道要怎麼處理這些舊書，所以也許我會把它們送給學校圖書館。
have to do with: The story we read in class today has to do with a boy who moves to a new city and feels lonely.
我們今天在課堂上讀的故事與一個搬到新城市、感到孤單的男孩有關。
have nothing to do with: I had nothing to do with the broken window, because I was in the library all afternoon with my friends.
我和打破的窗戶無關，因為我整個下午都和朋友在圖書館。
get along with: My brother and I get along with each other very well, and we almost never fight about anything.
我和哥哥彼此相處得很好，我們幾乎從不吵架。
get away with: You cannot get away with cheating on the test, because the teacher watches every student very carefully.
你不可能考試作弊還逃過懲罰，因為老師非常仔細地看著每一位學生。
come up with: After thinking for an hour, Lisa finally came up with a great idea for our class science project.
想了一小時後，麗莎終於為我們班的科學專題想出一個很棒的點子。
fall in love with: My parents fell in love with each other in college, and they got married five years later.
我爸媽在大學時彼此愛上了對方，五年後結婚。
keep in touch with: Although my best friend moved to America last year, we still keep in touch with each other by email every week.
雖然我最好的朋友去年搬去美國，我們每週仍用電子郵件保持聯絡。
make friends with: On the first day of school, I made friends with a girl who sits next to me and loves comic books.
開學第一天，我和坐在我旁邊、喜歡漫畫書的女孩交了朋友。
go out with: My cousin has been going out with a boy from her school for a year, and we all like him.
我表姊和她學校的一個男孩約會一年了，我們都喜歡他。
break up with: Amy broke up with the boy she loved last month, so she spent the whole weekend crying in her room.
艾美上個月和她愛的男孩分手了，所以她整個週末都在房間裡哭。
When my brother and I argue, Mom never sides with either of us, so we have to talk and find an answer.
我和哥哥爭吵時，媽媽從不支持我們任何一方，所以我們得談一談找出答案。
stick with: Learning the guitar is hard at first, but if you stick with it, you will play well in a year.
剛開始學吉他很難，但如果你堅持下去，一年後你就會彈得很好。
start with: Let's start with the easy questions on the test paper, and then we can go back to the hard ones.
我們從考卷上簡單的題目開始，然後再回頭做難的。
begin with: The teacher asked us to write a story that begins with a rainy morning and has a surprise at the end.
老師要我們寫一個以下雨的早晨開始、結尾有驚喜的故事。
end with: Our school day always ends with a short clean-up time, and then we can go home or play sports.
我們學校的一天總是以短短的打掃時間結束，然後我們可以回家或運動。
with that: Jack said he had to catch the last bus, and with that, he picked up his bag and ran out the door.
傑克說他得趕最後一班公車，說完那句話，他就拿起包包跑出門。
with this: The bell rang for the last time this year, and with this, our summer holiday finally began for everyone.
今年最後一次鈴聲響起，隨著這個，大家的暑假終於開始了。
along with: My mother packed some fruit along with the sandwiches, so we had a healthy lunch on the mountain.
媽媽把一些水果和三明治一起打包，所以我們在山上吃了健康的午餐。
together with: Please send the report together with the photos you took on the school trip before Friday afternoon.
請在星期五下午之前，把報告連同你在學校旅行拍的照片一起寄來。
What with…and…: What with the heavy rain and the long traffic jam, we got to the train station almost an hour late.
由於下大雨，又遇到長長的塞車，我們到火車站時幾乎晚了一小時。
Don't worry about the big game tomorrow, because all your friends and teachers will be with you.
不用擔心明天的大比賽，因為你所有的朋友和老師都會支持你。
I'm with you on this one; we should wait for the rain to stop before we ride our bikes home.
這件事我同意你；我們應該等雨停了再騎腳踏車回家。
Are you with me?: If we leave at seven, we can catch the early bus and get there before the shop opens, are you with me?
如果我們七點出發，就能趕上早班公車，在店開門前到那裡，你懂我意思嗎？
with it: My grandmother is really with it; she uses her phone to watch videos and talk with her old friends.
我奶奶真的很跟得上潮流；她用手機看影片，還和老朋友聊天。
with child: My aunt is with child, so she cannot carry the heavy boxes up the stairs by herself this time.
我阿姨懷孕了，所以這次她不能自己搬重箱子上樓。
with the times: Our old teacher tries hard to move with the times, and now she teaches English with games on the computer.
我們的老師努力跟上時代，現在她用電腦遊戲教英文。
with reason: Mom got angry with reason, because I came home late again and did not call her first.
媽媽生氣是有道理的，因為我又晚回家，而且沒有先打電話給她。
with interest: The children listened with interest when the old man told them stories about the sea and his ships.
當老人講述關於大海和他的船的故事時，孩子們有興趣地聽著。
handle with care: The box says handle with care, so please carry it slowly and do not drop it on the floor.
箱子上寫著小心搬運，所以請慢慢搬，不要把它掉到地上。
with the best will in the world: With the best will in the world, I cannot finish all this homework in one night before the test.
即使有最大的善意，我也無法在考試前一晚寫完這麼多作業。
leave it with me: Leave it with me, and I will call the restaurant and book a table for your birthday dinner tonight.
交給我吧，我會打電話給餐廳，為你今晚的生日晚餐訂位。
part with: My little brother will not part with his old toy bear, even though it is dirty and has one eye.
我弟弟不肯捨棄他的舊玩具熊，即使它很髒而且只剩一隻眼睛。
My parents trust me with the house key now, so I can come home alone after school every day.
我爸媽現在放心把家裡的鑰匙交給我，所以我每天放學後可以自己回家。
charge sb. with: The police charged the man with stealing a car, and he had to go to court the next week.
警察控告那名男子偷車，他下週必須上法庭。
be faced with: When we were faced with a very difficult math problem, our teacher told us to work in groups.
當我們面對一個非常困難的數學題時，老師叫我們分組討論。
be armed with: My uncle and his friends were armed with warm coats, maps, and lots of water before they climbed the high mountain.
我叔叔和他的朋友在爬高山之前配備了保暖外套、地圖和大量的水。
be blessed with: Our class is blessed with a kind teacher who always stays after school to help us with our homework.
我們班有幸擁有一位親切的老師，她總是放學後留下來幫我們寫作業。
be gifted with: My cousin is gifted with a beautiful voice, so she sings for the whole school at every big event.
我表姊天生有美妙的歌喉，所以每次大型活動她都為全校唱歌。
be born with: Some people are born with a good sense of direction, but I always get lost in a new city.
有些人生來就有很好的方向感，但我在新城市總是迷路。
be left with: After we paid for the train tickets and lunch, we were left with only fifty dollars for the whole afternoon.
付了火車票和午餐的錢之後，我們整個下午只剩下五十元。
be stuck with: Everyone else went to the movies, and I was stuck with the dishes and a kitchen full of dirty plates.
其他人都去看電影了，而我被一堆碗盤和滿是髒盤子的廚房困住。
be met with: Her idea for a class picnic was met with loud cheers, and everyone started planning the food right away.
她提出班級野餐的點子，受到熱烈歡呼，大家馬上開始計畫食物。
be comfortable with: My sister is comfortable with speaking English in front of people, but I still get nervous and quiet.
我姊姊在人前講英文覺得很自在，但我還是會緊張又安靜。
be in line with: The new school rules are in line with what most parents asked for at the meeting last month.
新的校規與大多數家長上個月在會議上要求的內容一致。
be level with: Please hang the picture so that the top is level with the window, or the wall will look strange.
請把畫掛得讓頂端與窗戶平齊，否則牆面看起來會很奇怪。
be even with: I paid you back the money for lunch yesterday, so now we are even with each other again.
我昨天把午餐的錢還你了，所以現在我們又扯平了。
get even with: Tom hid his brother's shoes to get even with him for eating the last piece of cake.
湯姆把哥哥的鞋子藏起來，為了報復他吃掉最後一塊蛋糕。
be quits with: You bought the movie tickets and I paid for dinner, so I think we are quits with each other now.
你買了電影票，我付了晚餐，所以我想我們現在兩不相欠了。
be at war with: In the story, the two small countries were at war with each other for more than ten years.
故事裡，這兩個小國彼此交戰超過十年。
be at peace with: After a long talk, the two brothers are finally at peace with each other and share a room again.
經過長談之後，兩兄弟終於和平相處，又一起住一間房了。
with (工具) vs. by (方式): I wrote the card with a red pen, and then I sent it to my grandmother by mail last week.
我用紅筆寫了這張卡片，然後上星期用郵寄的方式寄給奶奶。
cut with a knife vs. go by bus: Dad cut the big cake with a sharp knife, and then we all went to the park by bus to eat it.
爸爸用一把鋒利的刀切了大蛋糕，然後我們全都搭公車去公園吃。
with (和) vs. and (以及): Mary went to the night market with her brother, and they bought hot dogs and ice cream for everyone.
瑪麗和她弟弟一起去夜市，他們買了熱狗以及冰淇淋給大家。
be angry with sb. (人) vs. be angry at st: Dad was angry with my brother for breaking the window, but he was not angry at the broken glass itself.
爸爸因為弟弟打破窗戶而生他的氣，但他並不是對破掉的玻璃本身生氣。
agree with sb. (人) vs. agree on sth. (事): I agree with my mother about most things, but we still cannot agree on where to go this summer.
大部分的事情我都同意我媽，但我們還是無法就今年夏天去哪裡達成一致。
be covered with (被覆蓋) vs. be covered by: In the morning the whole park was covered with white snow, and the small lake was covered by thin ice.
早上整個公園被白雪覆蓋，小湖則由薄冰覆蓋著。
be filled with (裝滿) vs. be full of: Grandma's basket was filled with red apples from the farm, and the kitchen was full of their sweet smell.
奶奶的籃子裝滿了農場的紅蘋果，廚房裡充滿了蘋果的香甜味道。
be pleased with (對…滿意) vs. be pleased to: My teacher was pleased with my English report, and she was pleased to show it to the whole class.
老師對我的英文報告很滿意，她很高興把它拿給全班看。
be bored with (對…無聊) vs. be bored of (口語: After three rainy days inside, the kids were bored with their video games and wanted to go to the park.
在屋裡待了三個下雨天之後，孩子們對電玩感到無聊，想去公園。
be popular with (受…歡迎) vs. be popular am: The new ice cream shop near the school is popular with students, and it is always busy after four o'clock.
學校附近新開的冰淇淋店很受學生歡迎，四點以後總是很忙。
be busy with (忙於某事) vs. be busy doing: Dad is busy with the car in the garage, and Mom is busy cooking dinner for our ten guests.
爸爸在車庫忙著修車，媽媽忙著為我們的十位客人煮晚餐。
compare with (比較) vs. compare to (比作): If you compare this phone with mine, you will see that mine takes much better pictures at night.
如果你把這支手機和我的比較，你會發現我的手機夜間拍照好很多。
with (附帶) vs. without (沒有): I like my tea with a little milk, but my sister always drinks hers without anything in it.
我喜歡茶裡加一點牛奶，但我姊姊總是什麼都不加地喝她的茶。
